from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
W = 8
N = 50
N_new = 50
r_I = 10
r_II = 6
h_normal = 40
h_ot = 60
w_skilled = 360
w_trainee = 120
w_new = 240
w_ot = 540
c_I = 0.5
c_II = 0.6
train_cap = 3
d1 = [10000, 10000, 12000, 12000, 16000, 16000, 20000, 20000]
d2 = [6000, 7200, 8400, 10800, 10800, 12000, 12000, 12000]

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables (t indexed 0..7 for weeks 1..8)
# Skilled workers: x (food I normal), y (food II normal), a (food I OT), b (food II OT)
x = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"x_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
y = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"y_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
a = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"a_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
b = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"b_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]

# Newly trained workers: X (food I normal), Y (food II normal), A (food I OT), B (food II OT)
X = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"X_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
Y = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"Y_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
A = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"A_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
B = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"B_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]

# Training: p_t = new workers starting training in week t (t=1..7), q_t = skilled workers starting training in week t (t=1..7)
p = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"p_{t+1}") for t in range(W - 1)]
q = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"q_{t+1}") for t in range(W - 1)]

# Inventory (can be negative = backlog)
I = [m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=-100000, ub=100000, name=f"I_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
II = [m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=-100000, ub=100000, name=f"II_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]

# Penalty variables
P1 = [m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=0, ub=100000, name=f"P1_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
P2 = [m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=0, ub=100000, name=f"P2_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]

# Objective: minimize total cost
obj_terms = []
for t in range(W):
    # Skilled worker wages
    obj_terms.append(w_skilled * (x[t] + y[t]))
    obj_terms.append(w_ot * (a[t] + b[t]))
    # Newly trained worker wages
    obj_terms.append(w_new * (X[t] + Y[t]))
    obj_terms.append(w_ot * (A[t] + B[t]))
    # Trainee wages: p_t started this week, p_{t-1} started last week (still in training)
    trainees_this_week = p[t] if t < W - 1 else 0
    trainees_prev_week = p[t - 1] if t >= 1 else 0
    obj_terms.append(w_trainee * (trainees_this_week + trainees_prev_week))
    # Penalty costs
    obj_terms.append(c_I * P1[t])
    obj_terms.append(c_II * P2[t])

m.setObjective(quicksum(obj_terms), "minimize")

# Constraint: total_training - sum of p_t = 50
m.addCons(quicksum(p[t] for t in range(W - 1)) == N_new, name="total_training")

# Constraint: training_capacity - 3*q_t >= p_t for t=1..7
for t in range(W - 1):
    m.addCons(train_cap * q[t] >= p[t], name=f"training_capacity_{t+1}")

# Constraint: skilled_availability
# x_t + y_t + a_t + b_t <= 50 - q_{t-1} - q_t
# q_0 = 0, q_8 = 0 (q only defined for t=1..7, i.e., index 0..6)
for t in range(W):
    q_prev = q[t - 1] if t >= 1 else 0
    q_curr = q[t] if t < W - 1 else 0
    m.addCons(x[t] + y[t] + a[t] + b[t] <= N - q_prev - q_curr, name=f"skilled_avail_{t+1}")

# Constraint: newly_trained_availability
# X_t + Y_t + A_t + B_t <= sum_{j=1}^{t-2} p_j  (empty sum = 0)
for t in range(W):
    # Workers who started in weeks 1..(t-2) are available in week t
    # p index: week j -> p[j-1], so weeks 1..(t-2) -> p[0]..p[t-3]
    if t - 2 >= 1:
        trained_available = quicksum(p[j] for j in range(0, t - 1))
    else:
        trained_available = 0
    m.addCons(X[t] + Y[t] + A[t] + B[t] <= trained_available, name=f"new_avail_{t+1}")

# Constraint: inventory_I
# I_t = I_{t-1} + 400*(x_t + X_t) + 600*(a_t + A_t) - d1_t
for t in range(W):
    I_prev = I[t - 1] if t >= 1 else 0
    prod_I = r_I * h_normal * (x[t] + X[t]) + r_I * h_ot * (a[t] + A[t])
    m.addCons(I[t] == I_prev + prod_I - d1[t], name=f"inv_I_{t+1}")

# Constraint: inventory_II
# II_t = II_{t-1} + 240*(y_t + Y_t) + 360*(b_t + B_t) - d2_t
for t in range(W):
    II_prev = II[t - 1] if t >= 1 else 0
    prod_II = r_II * h_normal * (y[t] + Y[t]) + r_II * h_ot * (b[t] + B[t])
    m.addCons(II[t] == II_prev + prod_II - d2[t], name=f"inv_II_{t+1}")

# Constraint: penalty_I - P1_t >= -I_t
for t in range(W):
    m.addCons(P1[t] >= -I[t], name=f"pen_I_{t+1}")

# Constraint: penalty_II - P2_t >= -II_t
for t in range(W):
    m.addCons(P2[t] >= -II[t], name=f"pen_II_{t+1}")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

weak_points: Objective is missing the weekly wage cost for skilled workers who are actively training (360*(q_t + q_{t-1})); the problem explicitly pays trainees 120/week during training, implying skilled trainers are also compensated at their base rate of 360/week while unavailable for production.

The skilled_availability constraint uses an inequality (<=) rather than an equality, allowing skilled workers to be unaccounted for (neither producing, training, nor explicitly idle). A proper formulation should enforce x_t + y_t + a_t + b_t + q_t + q_{t-1} = 50 so all 50 employed skilled workers are fully allocated each week.

Variable 'source' fields are semantically incorrect or misleading (e.g., x_t is sourced to 'the weekly wage of a skilled worker is 360 yuan' rather than a description of what x_t represents), making the formulation difficult to audit and verify.

There is no explicit constraint bounding q_t by the number of skilled workers actually available to start a new training cycle in week t (i.e., 50 - q_{t-1} - (workers already committed to prior training)); the current skilled_availability inequality only limits production workers, not the trainers directly.

The penalty mechanism (P1_t >= -I_t) charges the full cumulative backlog each week, which is a reasonable interpretation of 'per week of delay per kg,' but the formulation does not explicitly state whether the penalty applies to the running backlog or only the current week's unmet demand, leaving ambiguity for a solver or reviewer.

No constraint or variable explicitly models the possibility that newly trained workers (who become available from week j+2 onward) could also be assigned to train future cohorts, which the problem does not forbid but the formulation implicitly excludes by restricting trainers to the original 50 skilled workers only.

weak_points: The 2-week training lag is not correctly modeled: the constraint p_t <= 3*s_t should be p_t <= 3*s_{t-2} to reflect that workers completing in week t started training two weeks earlier.

The trainee wage term 120*(p_t + p_{t-1}) does not correctly count the number of trainees present in week t; it should be 120*3*(s_t + s_{t-1}) or equivalently 120*(p_t + p_{t+1}) depending on the chosen indexing convention.

The new_worker_availability constraint X_t+Y_t+A_t+B_t <= sum_{j=1}^{t-2} p_j has an incorrect upper index; workers completing in week j should be available from week j+1 onward, so the cumulative sum should extend to at least t-1 or t.

The total_training_completed constraint sum_{t=1}^{7} p_t = 50 uses the wrong index range; since training takes 2 weeks, completions cannot occur before week 3, so the sum should be over t=3 to 8 (or starts over t=1 to 6).

There is no explicit equality or linking constraint that enforces the exact 2-week relationship between skilled workers who start training (s_t) and new workers who finish (p_{t+2} = 3*s_t), leaving the model under-constrained and allowing infeasible training schedules.

The variable definitions for s_t and p_t are ambiguous (it is unclear whether s_t denotes workers who start training in week t or workers in training during week t), which propagates inconsistencies into the allocation, wage, and availability constraints.

weak_points: New workers (n1_t, n2_t) are restricted to 40 h/week with no overtime option; the problem's phrasing 'arrange some workers to work 60 h' could arguably include newly trained workers, so the formulation may be overly restrictive.

The backlog penalty is applied to the end-of-week backlog (P1_t, P2_t) each week, which correctly accumulates multi-week delays, but the formulation does not explicitly state that I_t and II_t are permitted to be negative (only the loose bounds [-200000, 200000] allow it); a clearer non-negativity-free declaration or a split into positive/negative parts would improve readability and solver compatibility.

There is no explicit constraint linking the number of trainees who START in week t to f_{t+1}; the model relies on f_{t+1} being a free decision variable bounded only by 3*s_t. While mathematically consistent, an auxiliary variable for 'trainees starting in week t' with an equality to f_{t+1} would make the two-week training pipeline more transparent and less error-prone in implementation.

The skilled_allocation constraint uses s_{t-1}+s_t to account for two weeks of training occupancy, but it does not prevent a skilled worker from being counted in s_t in one week and simultaneously in a production variable in the same week through a different index; while the equality constraint prevents this in aggregate, a per-worker tracking or a note clarifying that s_t and s_{t-1} are disjoint cohorts would strengthen the formulation.

No terminal condition is imposed on I_8 or II_8 (e.g., no requirement to clear backlog by week 8 or a salvage/penalty for remaining inventory); if the contract requires all booked food to be delivered by the end of the horizon, a constraint I_8 >= 0 and II_8 >= 0 (or P1_8 = 0, P2_8 = 0) would be needed.

# Penalty variables
P1 = [m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=0, ub=100000, name=f"P1_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
P2 = [m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=0, ub=100000, name=f"P2_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]

# Objective: minimize total cost
obj_terms = []
for t in range(W):
    # Skilled worker wages
    obj_terms.append(w_skilled * (x[t] + y[t]))
    obj_terms.append(w_ot * (a[t] + b[t]))
    # Newly trained worker wages
    obj_terms.append(w_new * (X[t] + Y[t]))
    obj_terms.append(w_ot * (A[t] + B[t]))
    # Trainee wages: p_t started this week, p_{t-1} started last week (still in training)
    trainees_this_week = p[t] if t < W - 1 else 0
    trainees_prev_week = p[t - 1] if t >= 1 else 0
    obj_terms.append(w_trainee * (trainees_this_week + trainees_prev_week))
    # Penalty costs
    obj_terms.append(c_I * P1[t])
    obj_terms.append(c_II * P2[t])

m.setObjective(quicksum(obj_terms), "minimize")

# Constraint: total_training - sum of p_t = 50
m.addCons(quicksum(p[t] for t in range(W - 1)) == N_new, name="total_training")

# Constraint: training_capacity - 3*q_t >= p_t for t=1..7
for t in range(W - 1):
    m.addCons(train_cap * q[t] >= p[t], name=f"training_capacity_{t+1}")

# Constraint: skilled_availability
# x_t + y_t + a_t + b_t <= 50 - q_{t-1} - q_t
# q_0 = 0, q_8 = 0 (q only defined for t=1..7, i.e., index 0..6)
for t in range(W):
    q_prev = q[t - 1] if t >= 1 else 0
    q_curr = q[t] if t < W - 1 else 0
    m.addCons(x[t] + y[t] + a[t] + b[t] <= N - q_prev - q_curr, name=f"skilled_avail_{t+1}")

# Constraint: newly_trained_availability
# X_t + Y_t + A_t + B_t <= sum_{j=1}^{t-2} p_j  (empty sum = 0)
for t in range(W):
    # Workers who started in weeks 1..(t-2) are available in week t
    # p index: week j -> p[j-1], so weeks 1..(t-2) -> p[0]..p[t-3]
    if t - 2 >= 1:
        trained_available = quicksum(p[j] for j in range(0, t - 1))
    else:
        trained_available = 0
    m.addCons(X[t] + Y[t] + A[t] + B[t] <= trained_available, name=f"new_avail_{t+1}")

# Constraint: inventory_I

    m.addCons(I[t] == I_prev + prod_I - d1[t], name=f"inv_I_{t+1}")

# Constraint: inventory_II

    II_prev = II[t - 1] if t >= 1 else 0
    prod_II = r_II * h_normal * (y[t] + Y[t]) + r_II * h_ot * (b[t] + B[t])
    m.addCons(II[t] == II_prev + prod_II - d2[t], name=f"inv_II_{t+1}")

# Constraint: penalty_I - P1_t >= -I_t
for t in range(W):
    m.addCons(P1[t] >= -I[t], name=f"pen_I_{t+1}")

# Constraint: penalty_II - P2_t >= -II_t
for t in range(W):
    m.addCons(P2[t] >= -II[t], name=f"pen_II_{t+1}")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

weak_points: Objective is missing the weekly wage cost for skilled workers who are actively training (360*(q_t + q_{t-1})); the problem explicitly pays trainees 120/week during training, implying skilled trainers are also compensated at their base rate of 360/week while unavailable for production.

The skilled_availability constraint uses an inequality (<=) rather than an equality, allowing skilled workers to be unaccounted for (neither producing, training, nor explicitly idle). A proper formulation should enforce x_t + y_t + a_t + b_t + q_t + q_{t-1} = 50 so all 50 employed skilled workers are fully allocated each week.

Variable 'source' fields are semantically incorrect or misleading (e.g., x_t is sourced to 'the weekly wage of a skilled worker is 360 yuan' rather than a description of what x_t represents), making the formulation difficult to audit and verify.

There is no explicit constraint bounding q_t by the number of skilled workers actually available to start a new training cycle in week t (i.e., 50 - q_{t-1} - (workers already committed to prior training)); the current skilled_availability inequality only limits production workers, not the trainers directly.

The penalty mechanism (P1_t >= -I_t) charges the full cumulative backlog each week, which is a reasonable interpretation of 'per week of delay per kg,' but the formulation does not explicitly state whether the penalty applies to the running backlog or only the current week's unmet demand, leaving ambiguity for a solver or reviewer.

No constraint or variable explicitly models the possibility that newly trained workers (who become available from week j+2 onward) could also be assigned to train future cohorts, which the problem does not forbid but the formulation implicitly excludes by restricting trainers to the original 50 skilled workers only.

weak_points: New workers (n1_t, n2_t) are restricted to 40 h/week with no overtime option; the problem's phrasing 'arrange some workers to work 60 h' could arguably include newly trained workers, so the formulation may be overly restrictive.

The backlog penalty is applied to the end-of-week backlog (P1_t, P2_t) each week, which correctly accumulates multi-week delays, but the formulation does not explicitly state that I_t and II_t are permitted to be negative (only the loose bounds [-200000, 200000] allow it); a clearer non-negativity-free declaration or a split into positive/negative parts would improve readability and solver compatibility.

There is no explicit constraint linking the number of trainees who START in week t to f_{t+1}; the model relies on f_{t+1} being a free decision variable bounded only by 3*s_t. While mathematically consistent, an auxiliary variable for 'trainees starting in week t' with an equality to f_{t+1} would make the two-week training pipeline more transparent and less error-prone in implementation.

The skilled_allocation constraint uses s_{t-1}+s_t to account for two weeks of training occupancy, but it does not prevent a skilled worker from being counted in s_t in one week and simultaneously in a production variable in the same week through a different index; while the equality constraint prevents this in aggregate, a per-worker tracking or a note clarifying that s_t and s_{t-1} are disjoint cohorts would strengthen the formulation.

No terminal condition is imposed on I_8 or II_8 (e.g., no requirement to clear backlog by week 8 or a salvage/penalty for remaining inventory); if the contract requires all booked food to be delivered by the end of the horizon, a constraint I_8 >= 0 and II_8 >= 0 (or P1_8 = 0, P2_8 = 0) would be needed.

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
W = 8
N = 50
N_new = 50
r_I = 10
r_II = 6
h_normal = 40
h_ot = 60
w_skilled = 360
w_trainee = 120
w_new = 240
w_ot = 540
c_I = 0.5
c_II = 0.6
train_cap = 3
d1 = [10000, 10000, 12000, 12000, 16000, 16000, 20000, 20000]
d2 = [6000, 7200, 8400, 10800, 10800, 12000, 12000, 12000]

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables (t indexed 0..7 for weeks 1..8)
# Skilled workers: x (food I normal), y (food II normal), a (food I OT), b (food II OT)
x = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"x_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
y = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"y_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
a = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"a_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
b = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"b_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]

# Newly trained workers: X (food I normal), Y (food II normal), A (food I OT), B (food II OT)
X = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"X_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
Y = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"Y_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
A = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"A_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
B = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"B_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]

# Training: p_t = new workers starting training in week t (t=1..7), q_t = skilled workers starting training in week t (t=1..7)
p = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"p_{t+1}") for t in range(W - 1)]
q = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"q_{t+1}") for t in range(W - 1)]

# Inventory (can be negative = backlog)
I = [m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=-100000, ub=100000, name=f"I_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
II = [m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=-100000, ub=100000, name=f"II_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]

# Penalty variables
P1 = [m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=0, ub=100000, name=f"P1_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
P2 = [m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=0, ub=100000, name=f"P2_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]

# Objective: minimize total cost
obj_terms = []
for t in range(W):
    # Skilled worker wages
    obj_terms.append(w_skilled * (x[t] + y[t]))
    obj_terms.append(w_ot * (a[t] + b[t]))
    # Newly trained worker wages
    obj_terms.append(w_new * (X[t] + Y[t]))
    obj_terms.append(w_ot * (A[t] + B[t]))
    # Trainee wages: p_t started this week, p_{t-1} started last week (still in training)
    trainees_this_week = p[t] if t < W - 1 else 0
    trainees_prev_week = p[t - 1] if t >= 1 else 0
    obj_terms.append(w_trainee * (trainees_this_week + trainees_prev_week))
    # Penalty costs
    obj_terms.append(c_I * P1[t])
    obj_terms.append(c_II * P2[t])

m.setObjective(quicksum(obj_terms), "minimize")

# Constraint: total_training - sum of p_t = 50
m.addCons(quicksum(p[t] for t in range(W - 1)) == N_new, name="total_training")

# Constraint: training_capacity - 3*q_t >= p_t for t=1..7
for t in range(W - 1):
    m.addCons(train_cap * q[t] >= p[t], name=f"training_capacity_{t+1}")

# Constraint: skilled_availability
# x_t + y_t + a_t + b_t <= 50 - q_{t-1} - q_t
# q_0 = 0, q_8 = 0 (q only defined for t=1..7, i.e., index 0..6)
for t in range(W):
    q_prev = q[t - 1] if t >= 1 else 0
    q_curr = q[t] if t < W - 1 else 0
    m.addCons(x[t] + y[t] + a[t] + b[t] <= N - q_prev - q_curr, name=f"skilled_avail_{t+1}")

# Constraint: newly_trained_availability
# X_t + Y_t + A_t + B_t <= sum_{j=1}^{t-2} p_j  (empty sum = 0)
for t in range(W):
    # Workers who started in weeks 1..(t-2) are available in week t
    # p index: week j -> p[j-1], so weeks 1..(t-2) -> p[0]..p[t-3]
    if t - 2 >= 1:
        trained_available = quicksum(p[j] for j in range(0, t - 1))
    else:
        trained_available = 0
    m.addCons(X[t] + Y[t] + A[t] + B[t] <= trained_available, name=f"new_avail_{t+1}")

# Constraint: inventory_I
# I_t = I_{t-1} + 400*(x_t + X_t) + 600*(a_t + A_t) - d1_t
for t in range(W):
    I_prev = I[t - 1] if t >= 1 else 0
    prod_I = r_I * h_normal * (x[t] + X[t]) + r_I * h_ot * (a[t] + A[t])
    m.addCons(I[t] == I_prev + prod_I - d1[t], name=f"inv_I_{t+1}")

# Constraint: inventory_II
# II_t = II_{t-1} + 240*(y_t + Y_t) + 360*(b_t + B_t) - d2_t
for t in range(W):
    II_prev = II[t - 1] if t >= 1 else 0
    prod_II = r_II * h_normal * (y[t] + Y[t]) + r_II * h_ot * (b[t] + B[t])
    m.addCons(II[t] == II_prev + prod_II - d2[t], name=f"inv_II_{t+1}")

# Constraint: penalty_I - P1_t >= -I_t
for t in range(W):
    m.addCons(P1[t] >= -I[t], name=f"pen_I_{t+1}")

# Constraint: penalty_II - P2_t >= -II_t
for t in range(W):
    m.addCons(P2[t] >= -II[t], name=f"pen_II_{t+1}")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

No terminal condition is imposed on I_8 or II_8 (e.g., no requirement to clear backlog by week 8 or a salvage/penalty for remaining inventory); if the contract requires all booked food to be delivered by the end of the horizon, a constraint I_8 >= 0 and II_8 >= 0 (or P1_8 = 0, P2_8 = 0) would be needed.

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
W = 8
N = 50
N_new = 50
r_I = 10
r_II = 6
h_normal = 40
h_ot = 60
w_skilled = 360
w_trainee = 120
w_new = 240
w_ot = 540
c_I = 0.5
c_II = 0.6
train_cap = 3
d1 = [10000, 10000, 12000, 12000, 16000, 16000, 20000, 20000]
d2 = [6000, 7200, 8400, 10800, 10800, 12000, 12000, 12000]

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables (t indexed 0..7 for weeks 1..8)
# Skilled workers: x (food I normal), y (food II normal), a (food I OT), b (food II OT)
x = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"x_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
y = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"y_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
a = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"a_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
b = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"b_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]

# Newly trained workers: X (food I normal), Y (food II normal), A (food I OT), B (food II OT)
X = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"X_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
Y = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"Y_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
A = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"A_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
B = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"B_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]

# Training: p_t = new workers starting training in week t (t=1..7), q_t = skilled workers starting training in week t (t=1..7)
p = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"p_{t+1}") for t in range(W - 1)]
q = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"q_{t+1}") for t in range(W - 1)]

# Inventory (can be negative = backlog)
I = [m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=-100000, ub=100000, name=f"I_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
II = [m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=-100000, ub=100000, name=f"II_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]

# Penalty variables
P1 = [m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=0, ub=100000, name=f"P1_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
P2 = [m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=0, ub=100000, name=f"P2_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]

# Objective: minimize total cost
obj_terms = []
for t in range(W):
    # Skilled worker wages
    obj_terms.append(w_skilled * (x[t] + y[t]))
    obj_terms.append(w_ot * (a[t] + b[t]))
    # Newly trained worker wages
    obj_terms.append(w_new * (X[t] + Y[t]))
    obj_terms.append(w_ot * (A[t] + B[t]))
    # Trainee wages: p_t started this week, p_{t-1} started last week (still in training)
    trainees_this_week = p[t] if t < W - 1 else 0
    trainees_prev_week = p[t - 1] if t >= 1 else 0
    obj_terms.append(w_trainee * (trainees_this_week + trainees_prev_week))
    # Penalty costs
    obj_terms.append(c_I * P1[t])
    obj_terms.append(c_II * P2[t])

m.setObjective(quicksum(obj_terms), "minimize")

# Constraint: total_training - sum of p_t = 50
m.addCons(quicksum(p[t] for t in range(W - 1)) == N_new, name="total_training")

# Constraint: training_capacity - 3*q_t >= p_t for t=1..7
for t in range(W - 1):
    m.addCons(train_cap * q[t] >= p[t], name=f"training_capacity_{t+1}")

# Constraint: skilled_availability
# x_t + y_t + a_t + b_t <= 50 - q_{t-1} - q_t
# q_0 = 0, q_8 = 0 (q only defined for t=1..7, i.e., index 0..6)
for t in range(W):
    q_prev = q[t - 1] if t >= 1 else 0
    q_curr = q[t] if t < W - 1 else 0
    m.addCons(x[t] + y[t] + a[t] + b[t] <= N - q_prev - q_curr, name=f"skilled_avail_{t+1}")

# Constraint: newly_trained_availability
# X_t + Y_t + A_t + B_t <= sum_{j=1}^{t-2} p_j  (empty sum = 0)
for t in range(W):
    # Workers who started in weeks 1..(t-2) are available in week t
    # p index: week j -> p[j-1], so weeks 1..(t-2) -> p[0]..p[t-3]
    if t - 2 >= 1:
        trained_available = quicksum(p[j] for j in range(0, t - 1))
    else:
        trained_available = 0
    m.addCons(X[t] + Y[t] + A[t] + B[t] <= trained_available, name=f"new_avail_{t+1}")

# Constraint: inventory_I
# I_t = I_{t-1} + 400*(x_t + X_t) + 600*(a_t + A_t) - d1_t
for t in range(W):
    I_prev = I[t - 1] if t >= 1 else 0
    prod_I = r_I * h_normal * (x[t] + X[t]) + r_I * h_ot * (a[t] + A[t])
    m.addCons(I[t] == I_prev + prod_I - d1[t], name=f"inv_I_{t+1}")

# Constraint: inventory_II
# II_t = II_{t-1} + 240*(y_t + Y_t) + 360*(b_t + B_t) - d2_t
for t in range(W):
    II_prev = II[t - 1] if t >= 1 else 0
    prod_II = r_II * h_normal * (y[t] + Y[t]) + r_II * h_ot * (b[t] + B[t])
    m.addCons(II[t] == II_prev + prod_II - d2[t], name=f"inv_II_{t+1}")

# Constraint: penalty_I - P1_t >= -I_t
for t in range(W):
    m.addCons(P1[t] >= -I[t], name=f"pen_I_{t+1}")

# Constraint: penalty_II - P2_t >= -II_t
for t in range(W):
    m.addCons(P2[t] >= -II[t], name=f"pen_II_{t+1}")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
W = 8
N = 50
N_new = 50
r_I = 10
r_II = 6
h_normal = 40
h_ot = 60
w_skilled = 360
w_trainee = 120
w_new = 240
w_ot = 540
c_I = 0.5
c_II = 0.6
train_cap = 3
d1 = [10000, 10000, 12000, 12000, 16000, 16000, 20000, 20000]
d2 = [6000, 7200, 8400, 10800, 10800, 12000, 12000, 12000]

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables (t indexed 0..7 for weeks 1..8)
# Skilled workers: x (food I normal), y (food II normal), a (food I OT), b (food II OT)
x = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"x_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
y = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"y_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
a = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"a_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
b = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"b_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]

# Newly trained workers: X (food I normal), Y (food II normal), A (food I OT), B (food II OT)
X = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"X_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
Y = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"Y_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
A = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"A_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
B = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"B_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]

# Training: p_t = new workers starting training in week t (t=1..7), q_t = skilled workers starting training in week t (t=1..7)
p = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"p_{t+1}") for t in range(W - 1)]
q = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50, name=f"q_{t+1}") for t in range(W - 1)]

# Inventory (can be negative = backlog)
I = [m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=-100000, ub=100000, name=f"I_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
II = [m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=-100000, ub=100000, name=f"II_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]

# Penalty variables
P1 = [m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=0, ub=100000, name=f"P1_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]
P2 = [m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=0, ub=100000, name=f"P2_{t+1}") for t in range(W)]

# Objective: minimize total cost
obj_terms = []
for t in range(W):
    # Skilled worker wages
    obj_terms.append(w_skilled * (x[t] + y[t]))
    obj_terms.append(w_ot * (a[t] + b[t]))
    # Newly trained worker wages
    obj_terms.append(w_new * (X[t] + Y[t]))
    obj_terms.append(w_ot * (A[t] + B[t]))
    # Trainee wages: p_t started this week, p_{t-1} started last week (still in training)
    trainees_this_week = p[t] if t < W - 1 else 0
    trainees_prev_week = p[t - 1] if t >= 1 else 0
    obj_terms.append(w_trainee * (trainees_this_week + trainees_prev_week))
    # Penalty costs
    obj_terms.append(c_I * P1[t])
    obj_terms.append(c_II * P2[t])

m.setObjective(quicksum(obj_terms), "minimize")

# Constraint: total_training - sum of p_t = 50
m.addCons(quicksum(p[t] for t in range(W - 1)) == N_new, name="total_training")

# Constraint: training_capacity - 3*q_t >= p_t for t=1..7
for t in range(W - 1):
    m.addCons(train_cap * q[t] >= p[t], name=f"training_capacity_{t+1}")

# Constraint: skilled_availability
# x_t + y_t + a_t + b_t <= 50 - q_{t-1} - q_t
# q_0 = 0, q_8 = 0 (q only defined for t=1..7, i.e., index 0..6)
for t in range(W):
    q_prev = q[t - 1] if t >= 1 else 0
    q_curr = q[t] if t < W - 1 else 0
    m.addCons(x[t] + y[t] + a[t] + b[t] <= N - q_prev - q_curr, name=f"skilled_avail_{t+1}")

# Constraint: newly_trained_availability
# X_t + Y_t + A_t + B_t <= sum_{j=1}^{t-2} p_j  (empty sum = 0)
for t in range(W):
    # Workers who started in weeks 1..(t-2) are available in week t
    # p index: week j -> p[j-1], so weeks 1..(t-2) -> p[0]..p[t-3]
    if t - 2 >= 1:
        trained_available = quicksum(p[j] for j in range(0, t - 1))
    else:
        trained_available = 0
    m.addCons(X[t] + Y[t] + A[t] + B[t] <= trained_available, name=f"new_avail_{t+1}")

# Constraint: inventory_I
# I_t = I_{t-1} + 400*(x_t + X_t) + 600*(a_t + A_t) - d1_t
for t in range(W):
    I_prev = I[t - 1] if t >= 1 else 0
    prod_I = r_I * h_normal * (x[t] + X[t]) + r_I * h_ot * (a[t] + A[t])
    m.addCons(I[t] == I_prev + prod_I - d1[t], name=f"inv_I_{t+1}")

# Constraint: inventory_II
# II_t = II_{t-1} + 240*(y_t + Y_t) + 360*(b_t + B_t) - d2_t
for t in range(W):
    II_prev = II[t - 1] if t >= 1 else 0
    prod_II = r_II * h_normal * (y[t] + Y[t]) + r_II * h_ot * (b[t] + B[t])
    m.addCons(II[t] == II_prev + prod_II - d2[t], name=f"inv_II_{t+1}")

# Constraint: penalty_I - P1_t >= -I_t
for t in range(W):
    m.addCons(P1[t] >= -I[t], name=f"pen_I_{t+1}")

# Constraint: penalty_II - P2_t >= -II_t
for t in range(W):
    m.addCons(P2[t] >= -II[t], name=f"pen_II_{t+1}")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

weak_points: Objective is missing the weekly wage cost for skilled workers who are actively training (360*(q_t + q_{t-1})); the problem explicitly pays trainees 120/week during training, implying skilled trainers are also compensated at their base rate of 360/week while unavailable for production.

The skilled_availability constraint uses an inequality (<=) rather than an equality, allowing skilled workers to be unaccounted for (neither producing, training, nor explicitly idle). A proper formulation should enforce x_t + y_t + a_t + b_t + q_t + q_{t-1} = 50 so all 50 employed skilled workers are fully allocated each week.

Variable 'source' fields are semantically incorrect or misleading (e.g., x_t is sourced to 'the weekly wage of a skilled worker is 360 yuan' rather than a description of what x_t represents), making the formulation difficult to audit and verify.

There is no explicit constraint bounding q_t by the number of skilled workers actually available to start a new training cycle in week t (i.e., 50 - q_{t-1} - (workers already committed to prior training)); the current skilled_availability inequality only limits production workers, not the trainers directly.

The penalty mechanism (P1_t >= -I_t) charges the full cumulative backlog each week, which is a reasonable interpretation of 'per week of delay per kg,' but the formulation does not explicitly state whether the penalty applies to the running backlog or only the current week's unmet demand, leaving ambiguity for a solver or reviewer.

No constraint or variable explicitly models the possibility that newly trained workers (who become available from week j+2 onward) could also be assigned to train future cohorts, which the problem does not forbid but the formulation implicitly excludes by restricting trainers to the original 50 skilled workers only.

The variable definitions for s_t and p_t are ambiguous (it is unclear whether s_t denotes workers who start training in week t or workers in training during week t), which propagates inconsistencies into the allocation, wage, and availability constraints.

a_2 = 15

m.addCons(x_2 <= a_2, name="training_jets_year2")

# Solve
m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")
    print(f"x_1: {m.getVal(x_1)}")
    print(f"x_2: {m.getVal(x_2)}")

No constraint or note clarifies whether jets produced in year 1 remain available and operational for training in year 2 (i.e., no attrition, maintenance, or reassignment is considered), which is a critical assumption embedded in the objective but not stated as a constraint or parameter.

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data literals
T = 6
W0 = 1000
I0 = 15000
B0 = 0
price = 300
rm_cost = 90
out_cost = 200
hold_cost = 15
back_cost = 35
labor_req = 5
reg_hours = 160
reg_wage = 30
ot_limit_per_worker = 20
ot_wage = 40
hire_cost = 5000
fire_cost = 8000
min_end_inv = 10000
D = [20000, 40000, 42000, 35000, 19000, 18500]

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
P = [m.addVar(v=f"P_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=100000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
O = [m.addVar(v=f"O_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=100000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
I = [m.addVar(v=f"I_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=200000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
B = [m.addVar(v=f"B_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=200000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
W = [m.addVar(v=f"W_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=5000, vtype="I") for t in range(T)]
H = [m.addVar(v=f"H_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=5000, vtype="I") for t in range(T)]
F = [m.addVar(v=f"F_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=5000, vtype="I") for t in range(T)]
OT = [m.addVar(v=f"OT_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=100000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]

# Inventory balance constraints
prev_I = I0
prev_B = B0
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(I[t] - B[t] == prev_I - prev_B + P[t] + O[t] - D[t], name=f"inv_balance_{t+1}")
    prev_I = I[t]
    prev_B = B[t]

# Workforce balance constraints
prev_W = W0
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(W[t] == prev_W + H[t] - F[t], name=f"workforce_balance_{t+1}")
    prev_W = W[t]

# Production capacity constraints
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(labor_req * P[t] <= reg_hours * W[t] + OT[t], name=f"prod_capacity_{t+1}")

# Overtime limit constraints
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(OT[t] <= ot_limit_per_worker * W[t], name=f"ot_limit_{t+1}")

# Terminal conditions
m.addCons(I[T-1] >= min_end_inv, name="terminal_inventory")
m.addCons(B[T-1] == 0, name="terminal_backorder")

# Objective: maximize net profit
total_revenue = price * quicksum(D)
total_cost = (rm_cost * quicksum(P)
              + out_cost * quicksum(O)
              + hold_cost * quicksum(I)
              + back_cost * quicksum(B)
              + reg_wage * reg_hours * quicksum(W)
              + ot_wage * quicksum(OT)
              + hire_cost * quicksum(H)
              + fire_cost * quicksum(F))

m.setObjective(total_revenue - total_cost, "maximize")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

weak_points: Variable upper bounds (P_t≤54000, O_t≤50000, I_t≤120000, B_t≤50000, W_t≤1500, H_t≤1500, F_t≤1500, OT_t≤30000) are arbitrary and not derived from the problem statement; while they do not cut off the optimal solution, they lack a stated justification and could be tightened or made explicit as modeling assumptions.

No complementarity constraint (I_t · B_t = 0) is included to prevent simultaneous positive inventory and backorders in the same month. Although the positive holding and backorder costs make this non-binding at the optimum, its absence is a theoretical gap that a rigorous formulation should address.

No constraint prevents simultaneous hiring and firing in the same month (H_t > 0 and F_t > 0). While suboptimal and thus non-binding at the solution, a complete formulation would include H_t · F_t = 0 or an equivalent logical restriction.

The revenue term 300·(174500 − B_6) reduces to the constant 300·174500 because the terminal constraint forces B_6 = 0, making the 'maximize profit' objective equivalent to a pure cost-minimization problem. The formulation is correct but does not make this structural insight explicit, which could confuse a reader about the role of the revenue term.

Production and outsourcing variables are declared continuous rather than integer. While acceptable for a linear-programming relaxation, the problem context (discrete tables) suggests integer production quantities would be more faithful; at minimum this modeling choice should be noted.

The overtime variable OT_t represents total workforce overtime hours, and the constraint OT_t ≤ 20·W_t correctly enforces the per-worker cap. However, the formulation does not explicitly track the split between regular hours actually consumed and overtime hours consumed, relying implicitly on the fact that regular wages are paid regardless of utilization. This is correct but could be made more transparent by introducing a regular-hours-used variable for clarity.

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data literals
T = 6
W0 = 1000
I0 = 15000
B0 = 0
price = 300
rm_cost = 90
out_cost = 200
hold_cost = 15
back_cost = 35
labor_req = 5
reg_hours = 160
reg_wage = 30
ot_limit_per_worker = 20
ot_wage = 40
hire_cost = 5000
fire_cost = 8000
min_end_inv = 10000
D = [20000, 40000, 42000, 35000, 19000, 18500]

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
P = [m.addVar(v=f"P_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=100000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
O = [m.addVar(v=f"O_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=100000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
I = [m.addVar(v=f"I_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=200000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
B = [m.addVar(v=f"B_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=200000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
W = [m.addVar(v=f"W_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=5000, vtype="I") for t in range(T)]
H = [m.addVar(v=f"H_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=5000, vtype="I") for t in range(T)]
F = [m.addVar(v=f"F_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=5000, vtype="I") for t in range(T)]
OT = [m.addVar(v=f"OT_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=100000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]

# Inventory balance constraints
prev_I = I0
prev_B = B0
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(I[t] - B[t] == prev_I - prev_B + P[t] + O[t] - D[t], name=f"inv_balance_{t+1}")
    prev_I = I[t]
    prev_B = B[t]

# Workforce balance constraints
prev_W = W0
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(W[t] == prev_W + H[t] - F[t], name=f"workforce_balance_{t+1}")
    prev_W = W[t]

# Production capacity constraints
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(labor_req * P[t] <= reg_hours * W[t] + OT[t], name=f"prod_capacity_{t+1}")

# Overtime limit constraints
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(OT[t] <= ot_limit_per_worker * W[t], name=f"ot_limit_{t+1}")

# Terminal conditions
m.addCons(I[T-1] >= min_end_inv, name="terminal_inventory")
m.addCons(B[T-1] == 0, name="terminal_backorder")

# Objective: maximize net profit
total_revenue = price * quicksum(D)
total_cost = (rm_cost * quicksum(P)
              + out_cost * quicksum(O)
              + hold_cost * quicksum(I)
              + back_cost * quicksum(B)
              + reg_wage * reg_hours * quicksum(W)
              + ot_wage * quicksum(OT)
              + hire_cost * quicksum(H)
              + fire_cost * quicksum(F))

m.setObjective(total_revenue - total_cost, "maximize")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data literals
T = 6
W0 = 1000
I0 = 15000
B0 = 0
price = 300
rm_cost = 90
out_cost = 200
hold_cost = 15
back_cost = 35
labor_req = 5
reg_hours = 160
reg_wage = 30
ot_limit_per_worker = 20
ot_wage = 40
hire_cost = 5000
fire_cost = 8000
min_end_inv = 10000
D = [20000, 40000, 42000, 35000, 19000, 18500]

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
P = [m.addVar(v=f"P_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=100000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
O = [m.addVar(v=f"O_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=100000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
I = [m.addVar(v=f"I_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=200000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
B = [m.addVar(v=f"B_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=200000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
W = [m.addVar(v=f"W_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=5000, vtype="I") for t in range(T)]
H = [m.addVar(v=f"H_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=5000, vtype="I") for t in range(T)]
F = [m.addVar(v=f"F_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=5000, vtype="I") for t in range(T)]
OT = [m.addVar(v=f"OT_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=100000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]

# Inventory balance constraints
prev_I = I0
prev_B = B0
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(I[t] - B[t] == prev_I - prev_B + P[t] + O[t] - D[t], name=f"inv_balance_{t+1}")
    prev_I = I[t]
    prev_B = B[t]

# Workforce balance constraints
prev_W = W0
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(W[t] == prev_W + H[t] - F[t], name=f"workforce_balance_{t+1}")
    prev_W = W[t]

# Production capacity constraints
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(labor_req * P[t] <= reg_hours * W[t] + OT[t], name=f"prod_capacity_{t+1}")

# Overtime limit constraints
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(OT[t] <= ot_limit_per_worker * W[t], name=f"ot_limit_{t+1}")

# Terminal conditions
m.addCons(I[T-1] >= min_end_inv, name="terminal_inventory")
m.addCons(B[T-1] == 0, name="terminal_backorder")

# Objective: maximize net profit
total_revenue = price * quicksum(D)
total_cost = (rm_cost * quicksum(P)
              + out_cost * quicksum(O)
              + hold_cost * quicksum(I)
              + back_cost * quicksum(B)
              + reg_wage * reg_hours * quicksum(W)
              + ot_wage * quicksum(OT)
              + hire_cost * quicksum(H)
              + fire_cost * quicksum(F))

m.setObjective(total_revenue - total_cost, "maximize")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data literals
T = 6
W0 = 1000
I0 = 15000
B0 = 0
price = 300
rm_cost = 90
out_cost = 200
hold_cost = 15
back_cost = 35
labor_req = 5
reg_hours = 160
reg_wage = 30
ot_limit_per_worker = 20
ot_wage = 40
hire_cost = 5000
fire_cost = 8000
min_end_inv = 10000
D = [20000, 40000, 42000, 35000, 19000, 18500]

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
P = [m.addVar(v=f"P_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=100000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
O = [m.addVar(v=f"O_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=100000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
I = [m.addVar(v=f"I_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=200000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
B = [m.addVar(v=f"B_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=200000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
W = [m.addVar(v=f"W_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=5000, vtype="I") for t in range(T)]
H = [m.addVar(v=f"H_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=5000, vtype="I") for t in range(T)]
F = [m.addVar(v=f"F_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=5000, vtype="I") for t in range(T)]
OT = [m.addVar(v=f"OT_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=100000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]

# Inventory balance constraints
prev_I = I0
prev_B = B0
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(I[t] - B[t] == prev_I - prev_B + P[t] + O[t] - D[t], name=f"inv_balance_{t+1}")
    prev_I = I[t]
    prev_B = B[t]

# Workforce balance constraints
prev_W = W0
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(W[t] == prev_W + H[t] - F[t], name=f"workforce_balance_{t+1}")
    prev_W = W[t]

# Production capacity constraints
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(labor_req * P[t] <= reg_hours * W[t] + OT[t], name=f"prod_capacity_{t+1}")

# Overtime limit constraints
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(OT[t] <= ot_limit_per_worker * W[t], name=f"ot_limit_{t+1}")

# Terminal conditions
m.addCons(I[T-1] >= min_end_inv, name="terminal_inventory")
m.addCons(B[T-1] == 0, name="terminal_backorder")

# Objective: maximize net profit
total_revenue = price * quicksum(D)
total_cost = (rm_cost * quicksum(P)
              + out_cost * quicksum(O)
              + hold_cost * quicksum(I)
              + back_cost * quicksum(B)
              + reg_wage * reg_hours * quicksum(W)
              + ot_wage * quicksum(OT)
              + hire_cost * quicksum(H)
              + fire_cost * quicksum(F))

m.setObjective(total_revenue - total_cost, "maximize")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

Parameter B_0 has an incorrect source attribution (cites 'Initial Workforce: 1,000 employees' instead of referencing the absence of initial backorders), which could cause confusion in model documentation or auditing.

Variable upper bounds (e.g., 100,000 for production, 200,000 for inventory, 5,000 for workforce) are arbitrary and not derived from problem data; tighter data-driven bounds would improve solver performance and model clarity.

No constraint explicitly prevents simultaneous hiring and firing in the same month (H_t and F_t both positive); although this is dominated in the optimal solution given the cost structure, an explicit H_t * F_t = 0 or a logical constraint would make the model more robust.

The objective includes total revenue as a fixed constant (300 × 174,500), which is valid only because the terminal backorder constraint forces all demand to be fulfilled; if the terminal condition were relaxed, this formulation would incorrectly assume all demand generates revenue.

Variable upper bounds (P_t ≤ 100000, W_t ≤ 3000, OT_t ≤ 60000, I_t ≤ 200000) are arbitrary and not derived from any problem data or capacity calculation; while non-binding, they reduce the formulation's self-documenting quality and could mask infeasibility if tightened incorrectly.

The objective does not explicitly separate the constant revenue term from the variable cost terms, making it harder to verify that the optimization is effectively minimizing total cost; a clearer structure (constant + variable costs) would improve auditability.

There is no constraint or note addressing the implicit fulfillment priority (use prior inventory before producing or outsourcing); although the cost structure makes the priority emerge naturally, an explicit note or alternative formulation (e.g., using a single net-inventory variable) would reduce ambiguity for implementers.

Production and outsourcing variables are declared continuous rather than integer. While acceptable for a linear-programming relaxation, the problem context (discrete tables) suggests integer production quantities would be more faithful; at minimum this modeling choice should be noted.

The overtime variable OT_t represents total workforce overtime hours, and the constraint OT_t ≤ 20·W_t correctly enforces the per-worker cap. However, the formulation does not explicitly track the split between regular hours actually consumed and overtime hours consumed, relying implicitly on the fact that regular wages are paid regardless of utilization. This is correct but could be made more transparent by introducing a regular-hours-used variable for clarity.

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data literals
T = 6
W0 = 1000
I0 = 15000
B0 = 0
price = 300
rm_cost = 90
out_cost = 200
hold_cost = 15
back_cost = 35
labor_req = 5
reg_hours = 160
reg_wage = 30
ot_limit_per_worker = 20
ot_wage = 40
hire_cost = 5000
fire_cost = 8000
min_end_inv = 10000
D = [20000, 40000, 42000, 35000, 19000, 18500]

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
P = [m.addVar(v=f"P_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=100000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
O = [m.addVar(v=f"O_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=100000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
I = [m.addVar(v=f"I_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=200000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
B = [m.addVar(v=f"B_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=200000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
W = [m.addVar(v=f"W_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=5000, vtype="I") for t in range(T)]
H = [m.addVar(v=f"H_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=5000, vtype="I") for t in range(T)]
F = [m.addVar(v=f"F_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=5000, vtype="I") for t in range(T)]
OT = [m.addVar(v=f"OT_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=100000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]

# Inventory balance constraints
prev_I = I0
prev_B = B0
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(I[t] - B[t] == prev_I - prev_B + P[t] + O[t] - D[t], name=f"inv_balance_{t+1}")
    prev_I = I[t]
    prev_B = B[t]

# Workforce balance constraints
prev_W = W0
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(W[t] == prev_W + H[t] - F[t], name=f"workforce_balance_{t+1}")
    prev_W = W[t]

# Production capacity constraints
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(labor_req * P[t] <= reg_hours * W[t] + OT[t], name=f"prod_capacity_{t+1}")

# Overtime limit constraints
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(OT[t] <= ot_limit_per_worker * W[t], name=f"ot_limit_{t+1}")

# Terminal conditions
m.addCons(I[T-1] >= min_end_inv, name="terminal_inventory")
m.addCons(B[T-1] == 0, name="terminal_backorder")

# Objective: maximize net profit
total_revenue = price * quicksum(D)
total_cost = (rm_cost * quicksum(P)
              + out_cost * quicksum(O)
              + hold_cost * quicksum(I)
              + back_cost * quicksum(B)
              + reg_wage * reg_hours * quicksum(W)
              + ot_wage * quicksum(OT)
              + hire_cost * quicksum(H)
              + fire_cost * quicksum(F))

m.setObjective(total_revenue - total_cost, "maximize")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

Variable upper bounds (P_t ≤ 100000, W_t ≤ 3000, OT_t ≤ 60000, I_t ≤ 200000) are arbitrary and not derived from any problem data or capacity calculation; while non-binding, they reduce the formulation's self-documenting quality and could mask infeasibility if tightened incorrectly.

The objective does not explicitly separate the constant revenue term from the variable cost terms, making it harder to verify that the optimization is effectively minimizing total cost; a clearer structure (constant + variable costs) would improve auditability.

There is no constraint or note addressing the implicit fulfillment priority (use prior inventory before producing or outsourcing); although the cost structure makes the priority emerge naturally, an explicit note or alternative formulation (e.g., using a single net-inventory variable) would reduce ambiguity for implementers.

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data literals
T = 6
W0 = 1000
I0 = 15000
B0 = 0
price = 300
rm_cost = 90
out_cost = 200
hold_cost = 15
back_cost = 35
labor_req = 5
reg_hours = 160
reg_wage = 30
ot_limit_per_worker = 20
ot_wage = 40
hire_cost = 5000
fire_cost = 8000
min_end_inv = 10000
D = [20000, 40000, 42000, 35000, 19000, 18500]

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
P = [m.addVar(v=f"P_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=100000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
O = [m.addVar(v=f"O_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=100000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
I = [m.addVar(v=f"I_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=200000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
B = [m.addVar(v=f"B_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=200000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
W = [m.addVar(v=f"W_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=5000, vtype="I") for t in range(T)]
H = [m.addVar(v=f"H_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=5000, vtype="I") for t in range(T)]
F = [m.addVar(v=f"F_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=5000, vtype="I") for t in range(T)]
OT = [m.addVar(v=f"OT_{t+1}", lb=0, ub=100000, vtype="C") for t in range(T)]

# Inventory balance constraints
prev_I = I0
prev_B = B0
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(I[t] - B[t] == prev_I - prev_B + P[t] + O[t] - D[t], name=f"inv_balance_{t+1}")
    prev_I = I[t]
    prev_B = B[t]

# Workforce balance constraints
prev_W = W0
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(W[t] == prev_W + H[t] - F[t], name=f"workforce_balance_{t+1}")
    prev_W = W[t]

# Production capacity constraints
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(labor_req * P[t] <= reg_hours * W[t] + OT[t], name=f"prod_capacity_{t+1}")

# Overtime limit constraints
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(OT[t] <= ot_limit_per_worker * W[t], name=f"ot_limit_{t+1}")

# Terminal conditions
m.addCons(I[T-1] >= min_end_inv, name="terminal_inventory")
m.addCons(B[T-1] == 0, name="terminal_backorder")

# Objective: maximize net profit
total_revenue = price * quicksum(D)
total_cost = (rm_cost * quicksum(P)
              + out_cost * quicksum(O)
              + hold_cost * quicksum(I)
              + back_cost * quicksum(B)
              + reg_wage * reg_hours * quicksum(W)
              + ot_wage * quicksum(OT)
              + hire_cost * quicksum(H)
              + fire_cost * quicksum(F))

m.setObjective(total_revenue - total_cost, "maximize")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
sell_price_cow = 500
sell_price_sheep = 200
sell_price_chicken = 8
feed_cost_cow = 100
feed_cost_sheep = 80
feed_cost_chicken = 5
manure_per_cow = 10
manure_per_sheep = 5
manure_per_chicken = 3
max_manure = 800
max_chickens = 50
min_cows = 10
min_sheep = 20
max_total_animals = 100

# Model
m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Variables
c = m.addVar("cows", vtype="I", lb=min_cows, ub=max_total_animals)
s = m.addVar("sheep", vtype="I", lb=min_sheep, ub=max_total_animals)
k = m.addVar("chickens", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=max_chickens)

# Objective: maximize profit
profit_cow = sell_price_cow - feed_cost_cow
profit_sheep = sell_price_sheep - feed_cost_sheep
profit_chicken = sell_price_chicken - feed_cost_chicken
m.setObjective(profit_cow * c + profit_sheep * s + profit_chicken * k, "maximize")

# Constraints
m.addCons(manure_per_cow * c + manure_per_sheep * s + manure_per_chicken * k <= max_manure, "manure_limit")
m.addCons(k <= max_chickens, "max_chickens")
m.addCons(c >= min_cows, "min_cows")
m.addCons(s >= min_sheep, "min_sheep")
m.addCons(c + s + k <= max_total_animals, "total_animals")

# Solve
m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
sell_price_cow = 500
sell_price_sheep = 200
sell_price_chicken = 8
feed_cost_cow = 100
feed_cost_sheep = 80
feed_cost_chicken = 5
manure_per_cow = 10
manure_per_sheep = 5
manure_per_chicken = 3
max_manure = 800
max_chickens = 50
min_cows = 10
min_sheep = 20
max_total_animals = 100

# Model
m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Variables
c = m.addVar("c", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=100)
s = m.addVar("s", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=100)
k = m.addVar("k", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50)

# Objective: maximize profit
obj = (sell_price_cow - feed_cost_cow) * c + (sell_price_sheep - feed_cost_sheep) * s + (sell_price_chicken - feed_cost_chicken) * k
m.setObjective(obj, "maximize")

# Constraints
m.addCons(manure_per_cow * c + manure_per_sheep * s + manure_per_chicken * k <= max_manure, "manure_limit")
m.addCons(k <= max_chickens, "max_chickens")
m.addCons(c >= min_cows, "min_cows")
m.addCons(s >= min_sheep, "min_sheep")
m.addCons(c + s + k <= max_total_animals, "total_animals")

# Solve
m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
sell_price_cow = 500
sell_price_sheep = 200
sell_price_chicken = 8
feed_cost_cow = 100
feed_cost_sheep = 80
feed_cost_chicken = 5
manure_per_cow = 10
manure_per_sheep = 5
manure_per_chicken = 3
max_manure = 800
max_chickens = 50
min_cows = 10
min_sheep = 20
max_total_animals = 100

# Model
m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Variables
c = m.addVar("c", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=100)
s = m.addVar("s", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=100)
k = m.addVar("k", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=50)

# Objective: maximize profit
obj = (sell_price_cow - feed_cost_cow) * c + (sell_price_sheep - feed_cost_sheep) * s + (sell_price_chicken - feed_cost_chicken) * k
m.setObjective(obj, "maximize")

# Constraints
m.addCons(manure_per_cow * c + manure_per_sheep * s + manure_per_chicken * k <= max_manure, "manure_limit")
m.addCons(k <= max_chickens, "max_chickens")
m.addCons(c >= min_cows, "min_cows")
m.addCons(s >= min_sheep, "min_sheep")
m.addCons(c + s + k <= max_total_animals, "total_animals")

# Solve
m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

[export_rebinding_v1]
When business variables exist under different solver names, bind names instead of rewriting the model. Preserve the objective and constraints. Positive evidence: IDs 4, 8 and 25 passed independent audit after rebinding with unchanged objectives. Counterexample: ID 48 lacks total production roles, so name-only rebinding is insufficient; add missing roles instead.
Source: work/industryor_semantic_dag_dev_v0.2

[indicator_bidirectional_v1]
A binary indicator must be consistent with positive quantity in both directions: indicator <= quantity and quantity <= independent_upper_bound * indicator. Do not invent the upper bound. Positive evidence: IDs 9, 19, 20 and 21 recovered after scoped repair. Counterexample: indicator repair alone cannot fix a wrong business objective.
Source: work/industryor_semantic_dag_dev_v0.2

[objective_consistency_v1]
Recompute the business objective from semantic variables and check its direction. Goal-programming deviations are not business profit. ID 48 had feasible variables and an independent business optimum but a mismatched reported objective, and must remain rejected. Never inject a target value.
Source: work/industryor_semantic_dag_dev_v0.2/prob_048/branch_dag/regenerate/score.json

[regenerate_rebind_v1]
After regeneration, stale aliases can erase the export. Remove aliases whose solver names no longer exist, prefer verified canonical names, and rebind if needed. Rebinding completes evidence but does not prove business correctness. ID 48 demonstrates that objective semantics still need independent verification.
Source: work/industryor_semantic_dag_dev_v0.2/prob_048/branch_dag/regenerate/score.json

[dynamic_collection_binding_v1]
Dictionary comprehensions and simple loops may bind semantic names to expressions such as x['A']. Use only constant, code-verified index sets when repairing them. Do not guess nested or dynamic bindings. ID 19 supports this scoped mechanism; unsupported structures remain UNKNOWN.

# Data (transcribed from problem text)
fiber_okra_per_100g = 3.2
fiber_carrots_per_100g = 2.7
fiber_celery_per_100g = 1.6
fiber_cabbage_per_100g = 2.0

price_salmon_per_100g = 4.0
price_beef_per_100g = 3.6
price_pork_per_100g = 1.8
price_okra_per_100g = 2.6
price_carrots_per_100g = 1.2
price_celery_per_100g = 1.6
price_cabbage_per_100g = 2.3

budget = 15.0
total_intake_grams = 600

# Per-gram coefficients
fiber_okra = fiber_okra_per_100g / 100.0
fiber_carrots = fiber_carrots_per_100g / 100.0
fiber_celery = fiber_celery_per_100g / 100.0
fiber_cabbage = fiber_cabbage_per_100g / 100.0

price_salmon = price_salmon_per_100g / 100.0
price_beef = price_beef_per_100g / 100.0
price_pork = price_pork_per_100g / 100.0
price_okra = price_okra_per_100g / 100.0
price_carrots = price_carrots_per_100g / 100.0
price_celery = price_celery_per_100g / 100.0
price_cabbage = price_cabbage_per_100g / 100.0

M = 600.0

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Continuous variables (grams)
s = m.addVar("s", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=600)
b = m.addVar("b", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=600)
p = m.addVar("p", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=600)
o = m.addVar("o", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=600)
c = m.addVar("c", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=600)
ce = m.addVar("ce", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=600)
ca = m.addVar("ca", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=600)

# Binary variables
y_s = m.addVar("y_s", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y_b = m.addVar("y_b", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y_p = m.addVar("y_p", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y_o = m.addVar("y_o", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y_c = m.addVar("y_c", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y_ce = m.addVar("y_ce", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y_ca = m.addVar("y_ca", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)

# Objective: maximize fiber
obj = fiber_okra * o + fiber_carrots * c + fiber_celery * ce + fiber_cabbage * ca
m.setObjective(obj, "maximize")

# Exactly one protein
m.addCons(y_s + y_b + y_p == 1, "exactly_one_protein")

# At least two vegetables
m.addCons(y_o + y_c + y_ce + y_ca >= 2, "at_least_two_vegetables")

# Budget
m.addCons(price_salmon * s + price_beef * b + price_pork * p + price_okra * o + price_carrots * c + price_celery * ce + price_cabbage * ca <= budget, "budget")

# Total intake
m.addCons(s + b + p + o + c + ce + ca == total_intake_grams, "total_intake")

# Linking constraints (big-M)
m.addCons(s <= M * y_s, "link_salmon")
m.addCons(b <= M * y_b, "link_beef")
m.addCons(p <= M * y_p, "link_pork")
m.addCons(o <= M * y_o, "link_okra")
m.addCons(c <= M * y_c, "link_carrots")
m.addCons(ce <= M * y_ce, "link_celery")
m.addCons(ca <= M * y_ca, "link_cabbage")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

[export_rebinding_v1]
When business variables exist under different solver names, bind names instead of rewriting the model. Preserve the objective and constraints. Positive evidence: IDs 4, 8 and 25 passed independent audit after rebinding with unchanged objectives. Counterexample: ID 48 lacks total production roles, so name-only rebinding is insufficient; add missing roles instead.
Source: work/industryor_semantic_dag_dev_v0.2

[indicator_bidirectional_v1]
A binary indicator must be consistent with positive quantity in both directions: indicator <= quantity and quantity <= independent_upper_bound * indicator. Do not invent the upper bound. Positive evidence: IDs 9, 19, 20 and 21 recovered after scoped repair. Counterexample: indicator repair alone cannot fix a wrong business objective.
Source: work/industryor_semantic_dag_dev_v0.2

[objective_consistency_v1]
Recompute the business objective from semantic variables and check its direction. Goal-programming deviations are not business profit. ID 48 had feasible variables and an independent business optimum but a mismatched reported objective, and must remain rejected. Never inject a target value.
Source: work/industryor_semantic_dag_dev_v0.2/prob_048/branch_dag/regenerate/score.json

[regenerate_rebind_v1]
After regeneration, stale aliases can erase the export. Remove aliases whose solver names no longer exist, prefer verified canonical names, and rebind if needed. Rebinding completes evidence but does not prove business correctness. ID 48 demonstrates that objective semantics still need independent verification.
Source: work/industryor_semantic_dag_dev_v0.2/prob_048/branch_dag/regenerate/score.json

[dynamic_collection_binding_v1]
Dictionary comprehensions and simple loops may bind semantic names to expressions such as x['A']. Use only constant, code-verified index sets when repairing them. Do not guess nested or dynamic bindings. ID 19 supports this scoped mechanism; unsupported structures remain UNKNOWN.

weak_points: The parameter min_qty_per_selected_food = 1 is an unstated assumption; the original problem never specifies a minimum quantity for a selected food, yet the lower-bound linking constraints (e.g., s >= 1*y_s) depend on it. A later formulation should either justify this choice or use a tighter/looser bound with explicit reasoning.

Protein items (salmon, beef, pork) are implicitly assigned zero fiber because they are absent from the objective, but no parameter or note documents this assumption. A later formulation should explicitly state that proteins contribute 0 g fiber per 100 g to avoid ambiguity.

The individual variable upper bounds of 600 g are redundant given the total-intake equality (s+b+p+ok+cr+ce+cb = 600) and could be tightened to the actual maximum feasible amount per item under the budget, improving solver performance.

The formulation does not include a non-negativity note separate from the bounds; while bounds [0,600] imply it, an explicit non-negativity declaration would make the model more self-documenting for a reader unfamiliar with the convention.

price_celery_per_100g = 1.6

budget = 15.0
total_intake_grams = 600

# Per-gram coefficients
fiber_okra = fiber_okra_per_100g / 100.0
fiber_carrots = fiber_carrots_per_100g / 100.0
fiber_celery = fiber_celery_per_100g / 100.0
fiber_cabbage = fiber_cabbage_per_100g / 100.0

price_salmon = price_salmon_per_100g / 100.0
price_beef = price_beef_per_100g / 100.0
price_pork = price_pork_per_100g / 100.0
price_okra = price_okra_per_100g / 100.0
price_carrots = price_carrots_per_100g / 100.0
price_celery = price_celery_per_100g / 100.0
price_cabbage = price_cabbage_per_100g / 100.0

M = 600.0

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Continuous variables (grams)
s = m.addVar("s", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=600)
b = m.addVar("b", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=600)
p = m.addVar("p", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=600)
o = m.addVar("o", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=600)
c = m.addVar("c", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=600)
ce = m.addVar("ce", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=600)
ca = m.addVar("ca", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=600)

# Binary variables
y_s = m.addVar("y_s", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y_b = m.addVar("y_b", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y_p = m.addVar("y_p", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y_o = m.addVar("y_o", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y_c = m.addVar("y_c", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y_ce = m.addVar("y_ce", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y_ca = m.addVar("y_ca", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)

# Objective: maximize fiber
obj = fiber_okra * o + fiber_carrots * c + fiber_celery * ce + fiber_cabbage * ca
m.setObjective(obj, "maximize")

# Exactly one protein
m.addCons(y_s + y_b + y_p == 1, "exactly_one_protein")

# At least two vegetables
m.addCons(y_o + y_c + y_ce + y_ca >= 2, "at_least_two_vegetables")

# Budget
m.addCons(price_salmon * s + price_beef * b + price_pork * p + price_okra * o + price_carrots * c + price_celery * ce + price_cabbage * ca <= budget, "budget")

# Total intake
m.addCons(s + b + p + o + c + ce + ca == total_intake_grams, "total_intake")

# Linking constraints (big-M)
m.addCons(s <= M * y_s, "link_salmon")
m.addCons(b <= M * y_b, "link_beef")
m.addCons(p <= M * y_p, "link_pork")
m.addCons(o <= M * y_o, "link_okra")
m.addCons(c <= M * y_c, "link_carrots")
m.addCons(ce <= M * y_ce, "link_celery")
m.addCons(ca <= M * y_ca, "link_cabbage")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

price_celery_per_100g = 1.6
price_cabbage_per_100g = 2.3

budget = 15.0
total_intake_grams = 600.0
min_selected_qty_grams = 1.0

# Per-gram coefficients
fiber_okra = fiber_okra_per_100g / 100.0
fiber_carrots = fiber_carrots_per_100g / 100.0
fiber_celery = fiber_celery_per_100g / 100.0

price_salmon = price_salmon_per_100g / 100.0

price_pork = price_pork_per_100g / 100.0
price_okra = price_okra_per_100g / 100.0
price_carrots = price_carrots_per_100g / 100.0
price_celery = price_celery_per_100g / 100.0
price_cabbage = price_cabbage_per_100g / 100.0

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Continuous variables: grams of each food
x_salmon = m.addVar("x_salmon", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=total_intake_grams)
x_beef = m.addVar("x_beef", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=total_intake_grams)
x_pork = m.addVar("x_pork", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=total_intake_grams)
x_okra = m.addVar("x_okra", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=total_intake_grams)
x_carrots = m.addVar("x_carrots", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=total_intake_grams)
x_celery = m.addVar("x_celery", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=total_intake_grams)
x_cabbage = m.addVar("x_cabbage", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=total_intake_grams)

# Binary variables: selection indicators
y_salmon = m.addVar("y_salmon", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y_beef = m.addVar("y_beef", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y_pork = m.addVar("y_pork", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y_okra = m.addVar("y_okra", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y_carrots = m.addVar("y_carrots", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y_celery = m.addVar("y_celery", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y_cabbage = m.addVar("y_cabbage", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)

# Objective: maximize fiber intake
obj = fiber_okra * x_okra + fiber_carrots * x_carrots + fiber_celery * x_celery + fiber_cabbage * x_cabbage
m.setObjective(obj, "maximize")

# Exactly one protein
m.addCons(y_salmon + y_beef + y_pork == 1, "exactly_one_protein")

# At least two vegetables
m.addCons(y_okra + y_carrots + y_celery + y_cabbage >= 2, "at_least_two_vegetables")

# Budget
m.addCons(
    price_salmon * x_salmon + price_beef * x_beef + price_pork * x_pork
    + price_okra * x_okra + price_carrots * x_carrots + price_celery * x_celery
    + price_cabbage * x_cabbage <= budget, "budget"
)

# Total intake
m.addCons(
    x_salmon + x_beef + x_pork + x_okra + x_carrots + x_celery + x_cabbage == total_intake_grams,
    "total_intake"
)

# Linking constraints: upper
m.addCons(x_salmon <= total_intake_grams * y_salmon, "salmon_upper_link")
m.addCons(x_beef <= total_intake_grams * y_beef, "beef_upper_link")
m.addCons(x_pork <= total_intake_grams * y_pork, "pork_upper_link")
m.addCons(x_okra <= total_intake_grams * y_okra, "okra_upper_link")
m.addCons(x_carrots <= total_intake_grams * y_carrots, "carrots_upper_link")
m.addCons(x_celery <= total_intake_grams * y_celery, "celery_upper_link")
m.addCons(x_cabbage <= total_intake_grams * y_cabbage, "cabbage_upper_link")

# Linking constraints: lower
m.addCons(x_salmon >= min_selected_qty_grams * y_salmon, "salmon_lower_link")
m.addCons(x_beef >= min_selected_qty_grams * y_beef, "beef_lower_link")
m.addCons(x_pork >= min_selected_qty_grams * y_pork, "pork_lower_link")
m.addCons(x_okra >= min_selected_qty_grams * y_okra, "okra_lower_link")
m.addCons(x_carrots >= min_selected_qty_grams * y_carrots, "carrots_lower_link")
m.addCons(x_celery >= min_selected_qty_grams * y_celery, "celery_lower_link")
m.addCons(x_cabbage >= min_selected_qty_grams * y_cabbage, "cabbage_lower_link")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")
    print(f"x_salmon: {m.getVal(x_salmon)}")
    print(f"x_beef: {m.getVal(x_beef)}")
    print(f"x_pork: {m.getVal(x_pork)}")
    print(f"x_okra: {m.getVal(x_okra)}")
    print(f"x_carrots: {m.getVal(x_carrots)}")
    print(f"x_celery: {m.getVal(x_celery)}")

Because the backlog is not carried forward, the penalty term in the objective (20·ΣL for I/II, 10·ΣL for III) underestimates the true cost: a unit delayed by two quarters is charged only one quarter's penalty instead of two.

A later formulation should either (a) add the −L_{i,t−1} term to every balance equation for t≥2, or (b) introduce an explicit cumulative-backlog variable B_{i,t} with its own recurrence B_{i,t} = max(0, B_{i,t−1} + D_{i,t} − I_{i,t−1} − x_{i,t}) and charge the penalty on B_{i,t}.

The end-of-horizon inventory constraint I_{i,4} ≥ 150 is stated as a lower bound; while the optimizer will typically set it to exactly 150, the formulation should clarify whether the requirement is 'at least' or 'exactly' 150 units to avoid ambiguity in edge cases where excess inventory is free.

weak_points: All decision variables are declared as continuous; production units are physically discrete, so integer (or at least non-negative integer) types would be more appropriate for x_{i,t}, I_{i,t}, and L_{i,t}.

No explicit mutual-exclusion constraint prevents I_{i,t} and L_{i,t} from being simultaneously positive in the same period; although the objective naturally discourages this, a constraint such as I_{i,t} * L_{i,t} = 0 (or a big-M linearization) would make the model logically tighter.

The end-of-horizon inventory requirement is modeled as I_{i,4} >= 150 (at least 150). The problem states 'required to have 150 units in stock,' which could be read as an exact target; if the intent is exactly 150, an equality constraint would be needed.

No explicit upper bounds are placed on individual production variables x_{i,t}; while the quarterly capacity constraints implicitly bound them, adding per-product upper bounds (e.g., derived from capacity / hours-per-unit) would improve numerical conditioning and solver performance.

The balance equations use the net-position form (I_{i,t} - L_{i,t} = I_{i,t-1} - L_{i,t-1} + x_{i,t} - D_{i,t}), which is valid but couples inventory and backorder into a single scalar; a formulation with separate inventory and backorder balance equations (I_{i,t} = I_{i,t-1} + x_{i,t} - D_{i,t} + L_{i,t-1} - L_{i,t}) would make the physical interpretation more transparent and avoid potential solver confusion with the sign of the net position.

weak_points: Complementarity constraints (I_{i,t} * L_{i,t} = 0) are bilinear and make the problem a MINLP, yet they are fully redundant: the balance equation I_{i,t} - L_{i,t} = (net position) combined with I_{i,t} >= 0 and L_{i,t} >= 0 already forces at most one of I or L to be positive in any feasible solution. Removing them yields an equivalent MILP that is far easier to solve.

The separate inventory (I) and backorder (L) variable design is the root cause of the non-linearity. A cleaner formulation would use a single signed net-position variable (e.g., S_{i,t} = I_{i,t} - L_{i,t}) that can be negative, then define the cost terms as 5*max(0,S) + penalty*max(0,-S) via auxiliary linear constraints, keeping the model fully linear.

The upper bound on x_1_2 is listed as 7500 even though the no-production constraint x_1_2 = 0 is imposed separately; while not incorrect, setting the bound to [0,0] directly would tighten the formulation and avoid a redundant constraint.

The end-of-horizon requirement is modeled as I_{i,4} >= 150 (inequality). The problem states 'required to have 150 units in stock,' which is naturally a minimum, so this is acceptable, but the formulation does not explicitly state that all outstanding backorders must be cleared by Q4 (L_{i,4} = 0). This is implicitly enforced by the balance equation when I_{i,4} >= 150 > 0, but making it explicit would improve clarity and robustness if the complementarity constraints are removed.

weak_points: Balance equations for quarters 2–4 are missing the '−L_{i,t−1}' term: the correct form should be I_{i,t} − L_{i,t} = I_{i,t−1} − L_{i,t−1} + x_{i,t} − D_{i,t}. As written, the prior-period backlog is dropped, so L_{i,t} captures only the current-period shortfall rather than the cumulative unmet demand.

Because the backlog is not carried forward, the penalty term in the objective (20·ΣL for I/II, 10·ΣL for III) underestimates the true cost: a unit delayed by two quarters is charged only one quarter's penalty instead of two.

A later formulation should either (a) add the −L_{i,t−1} term to every balance equation for t≥2, or (b) introduce an explicit cumulative-backlog variable B_{i,t} with its own recurrence B_{i,t} = max(0, B_{i,t−1} + D_{i,t} − I_{i,t−1} − x_{i,t}) and charge the penalty on B_{i,t}.

The end-of-horizon inventory constraint I_{i,4} ≥ 150 is stated as a lower bound; while the optimizer will typically set it to exactly 150, the formulation should clarify whether the requirement is 'at least' or 'exactly' 150 units to avoid ambiguity in edge cases where excess inventory is free.

weak_points: All decision variables are declared as continuous; production units are physically discrete, so integer (or at least non-negative integer) types would be more appropriate for x_{i,t}, I_{i,t}, and L_{i,t}.

No explicit mutual-exclusion constraint prevents I_{i,t} and L_{i,t} from being simultaneously positive in the same period; although the objective naturally discourages this, a constraint such as I_{i,t} * L_{i,t} = 0 (or a big-M linearization) would make the model logically tighter.

The end-of-horizon inventory requirement is modeled as I_{i,4} >= 150 (at least 150). The problem states 'required to have 150 units in stock,' which could be read as an exact target; if the intent is exactly 150, an equality constraint would be needed.

No explicit upper bounds are placed on individual production variables x_{i,t}; while the quarterly capacity constraints implicitly bound them, adding per-product upper bounds (e.g., derived from capacity / hours-per-unit) would improve numerical conditioning and solver performance.

The balance equations use the net-position form (I_{i,t} - L_{i,t} = I_{i,t-1} - L_{i,t-1} + x_{i,t} - D_{i,t}), which is valid but couples inventory and backorder into a single scalar; a formulation with separate inventory and backorder balance equations (I_{i,t} = I_{i,t-1} + x_{i,t} - D_{i,t} + L_{i,t-1} - L_{i,t}) would make the physical interpretation more transparent and avoid potential solver confusion with the sign of the net position.

weak_points: Complementarity constraints (I_{i,t} * L_{i,t} = 0) are bilinear and make the problem a MINLP, yet they are fully redundant: the balance equation I_{i,t} - L_{i,t} = (net position) combined with I_{i,t} >= 0 and L_{i,t} >= 0 already forces at most one of I or L to be positive in any feasible solution. Removing them yields an equivalent MILP that is far easier to solve.

The separate inventory (I) and backorder (L) variable design is the root cause of the non-linearity. A cleaner formulation would use a single signed net-position variable (e.g., S_{i,t} = I_{i,t} - L_{i,t}) that can be negative, then define the cost terms as 5*max(0,S) + penalty*max(0,-S) via auxiliary linear constraints, keeping the model fully linear.

The upper bound on x_1_2 is listed as 7500 even though the no-production constraint x_1_2 = 0 is imposed separately; while not incorrect, setting the bound to [0,0] directly would tighten the formulation and avoid a redundant constraint.

The end-of-horizon requirement is modeled as I_{i,4} >= 150 (inequality). The problem states 'required to have 150 units in stock,' which is naturally a minimum, so this is acceptable, but the formulation does not explicitly state that all outstanding backorders must be cleared by Q4 (L_{i,4} = 0). This is implicitly enforced by the balance equation when I_{i,4} >= 150 > 0, but making it explicit would improve clarity and robustness if the complementarity constraints are removed.

weak_points: Balance equations for quarters 2–4 are missing the '−L_{i,t−1}' term: the correct form should be I_{i,t} − L_{i,t} = I_{i,t−1} − L_{i,t−1} + x_{i,t} − D_{i,t}. As written, the prior-period backlog is dropped, so L_{i,t} captures only the current-period shortfall rather than the cumulative unmet demand.

Because the backlog is not carried forward, the penalty term in the objective (20·ΣL for I/II, 10·ΣL for III) underestimates the true cost: a unit delayed by two quarters is charged only one quarter's penalty instead of two.

A later formulation should either (a) add the −L_{i,t−1} term to every balance equation for t≥2, or (b) introduce an explicit cumulative-backlog variable B_{i,t} with its own recurrence B_{i,t} = max(0, B_{i,t−1} + D_{i,t} − I_{i,t−1} − x_{i,t}) and charge the penalty on B_{i,t}.

The end-of-horizon inventory constraint I_{i,4} ≥ 150 is stated as a lower bound; while the optimizer will typically set it to exactly 150, the formulation should clarify whether the requirement is 'at least' or 'exactly' 150 units to avoid ambiguity in edge cases where excess inventory is free.
