from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
n = 10
r = [3, 5, 2, 4, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1]  # 0-indexed: r[0]=r_1, ..., r[9]=r_10
a = 10
b = 1
c = 3
p = 3
q = 1

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables (0-indexed: x[0]=x_1, ..., x[9]=x_10; s[0]=s_1, ..., s[8]=s_9; f[0]=f_1, ..., f[8]=f_9)
x = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, name=f"x_{j+1}") for j in range(n)]
s = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, name=f"s_{j+1}") for j in range(n - 1)]  # s_1 .. s_9
f = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, name=f"f_{j+1}") for j in range(n - 1)]  # f_1 .. f_9
# Inventory variables: I[j] = idle tools in pool at end of stage j+1
I = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, name=f"I_{j+1}") for j in range(n)]

# Objective: minimize total cost
obj = a * quicksum(x[j] for j in range(n)) + b * quicksum(s[j] for j in range(n - 1)) + c * quicksum(f[j] for j in range(n - 1))
m.setObjective(obj, "minimize")

# Repair split constraints: at end of stage j (j=1..9), all r_j tools used must be sent for repair
for j in range(n - 1):  # j=0..8 corresponds to stage 1..9
    m.addCons(s[j] + f[j] == r[j], name=f"repair_split_{j+1}")

# Inventory flow constraints:
# I[j] = I[j-1] + x[j] + slow_returns + fast_returns - r[j], with I[j] >= 0
# This ensures enough tools are available at each stage (I[j] >= 0 means supply >= demand)
# Slow repair: sent at end of stage (j-p+1) in 1-indexed, i.e., s[j-p] in 0-indexed, returns at stage j+1
# Fast repair: sent at end of stage (j-q+1) in 1-indexed, i.e., f[j-q] in 0-indexed, returns at stage j+1
for j in range(n):  # j=0..9 corresponds to stage 1..10
    slow_ret = 0
    fast_ret = 0
    if j - p >= 0:
        slow_ret = s[j - p]
    if j - q >= 0:
        fast_ret = f[j - q]

    if j == 0:
        # Stage 1: no prior inventory, no returns possible
        m.addCons(I[j] == x[j] + slow_ret + fast_ret - r[j], name=f"inventory_{j+1}")
    else:
        # Stage j+1: carry over idle tools from previous stage
        m.addCons(I[j] == I[j - 1] + x[j] + slow_ret + fast_ret - r[j], name=f"inventory_{j+1}")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")
    for j in range(n):
        print(f"x_{j+1} = {m.getVal(x[j])}")
    for j in range(n - 1):
        print(f"s_{j+1} = {m.getVal(s[j])}")
    for j in range(n - 1):
        print(f"f_{j+1} = {m.getVal(f[j])}")
    for j in range(n):
        print(f"I_{j+1} = {m.getVal(I[j])}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
n = 10
r = [3, 5, 2, 4, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1]  # 0-indexed: r[0]=r_1, ..., r[9]=r_10
a = 10
b = 1
c = 3
p = 3
q = 1

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables (0-indexed: x[0]=x_1, ..., x[9]=x_10; s[0]=s_1, ..., s[8]=s_9; f[0]=f_1, ..., f[8]=f_9)
x = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, name=f"x_{j+1}") for j in range(n)]
s = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, name=f"s_{j+1}") for j in range(n - 1)]  # s_1 .. s_9
f = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, name=f"f_{j+1}") for j in range(n - 1)]  # f_1 .. f_9

# Objective: minimize total cost
obj = a * quicksum(x[j] for j in range(n)) + b * quicksum(s[j] for j in range(n - 1)) + c * quicksum(f[j] for j in range(n - 1))
m.setObjective(obj, "minimize")

# Repair split constraints: at end of stage j (j=1..n-1), all r_j tools used are sent for repair
for j in range(n - 1):  # j=0..8 corresponds to stage 1..9
    m.addCons(s[j] + f[j] == r[j], name=f"repair_split_{j+1}")

# Availability constraints: at stage j, tools available (new + returned) must meet or exceed r_j
# Stage j (1-indexed): x_j + s_{j-p} (if j-p>=1) + f_{j-q} (if j-q>=1) >= r_j
for j in range(n):  # j=0..9 corresponds to stage 1..10
    stage = j + 1  # 1-indexed stage number
    terms = [x[j]]
    # Slow repair returns: sent at end of stage (stage - p), available at stage
    if stage - p >= 1:
        terms.append(s[stage - p - 1])  # 0-indexed: s[stage-p-1]
    # Fast repair returns: sent at end of stage (stage - q), available at stage
    if stage - q >= 1:
        terms.append(f[stage - q - 1])  # 0-indexed: f[stage-q-1]
    m.addCons(quicksum(terms) >= r[j], name=f"availability_{stage}")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")

if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")
    # Extract and report all business decision variables
    solution = {}
    for j in range(n):
        solution[f"x_{j+1}"] = m.getVal(x[j])
    for j in range(n - 1):
        solution[f"s_{j+1}"] = m.getVal(s[j])
    for j in range(n - 1):
        solution[f"f_{j+1}"] = m.getVal(f[j])
    print(f"solution: {json.dumps(solution)}")
else:
    print("No feasible solution exists for the given parameters.")
    print(f"solver_status: {m.getStatus()}")
    print(f"number_of_solutions: {m.getNSols()}")

weak_points: Availability constraints use equality (=) instead of inequality (≥). For example, 'x_3 + f_2 = 2' is infeasible if f_2 > 2 (e.g., if all 5 tools from stage 2 are fast-repaired, f_2 = 5 > r_3 = 2). The correct form is x_j + (returned tools) ≥ r_j, because tools returned from prior repairs are already committed and cannot be discarded; excess tools simply sit idle without going to repair.

Because the availability constraints are equalities, the model can become infeasible for valid repair decisions made in earlier stages, which fundamentally breaks the optimization. A later formulation must replace all ten availability equalities with ≥ inequalities.

The repair-split constraints (s_j + f_j = r_j) are correct and consistent with the problem statement, but they interact incorrectly with the equality availability constraints: the split fixes the total tools entering repair, while the availability equality forces the total tools entering the stage to match r_j exactly, creating an over-constrained system when returned tools exceed demand.

weak_points: No variable or constraint tracks unused tools that carry over between stages: if more tools are available than r_j at some stage, the surplus is not modeled as available in subsequent stages, which can force unnecessary new purchases and overestimate the true optimal cost.

Availability constraints use '>=' rather than '='; combined with the absence of carry-over tracking, the feasible region is a strict subset of the true problem's feasible region, so the formulation's optimum may be worse than the true optimum.

The repair-split equalities (s_j + f_j = r_j) implicitly assume exactly r_j tools are consumed each stage, but there is no explicit 'tools used = r_j' constraint decoupled from the repair decision; the linkage is only indirect through the availability inequality.

Bounds on all variables are uniformly set to [0, 6] (the maximum r_j); while valid, tighter stage-specific bounds (e.g., s_j + f_j = r_j already caps the sum) are not exploited, which is a minor modelling inefficiency rather than a correctness issue.

weak_points: The u_j variables (surplus/inventory) are described with the source text 'If the repaired tools cannot meet the needs, new ones must be purchased', which describes the purchase decision (x_j) rather than the actual role of u_j as the carry-over surplus of unused tools. This mislabeling could confuse a later reader or reformulation.

The flow constraints are written as equalities (e.g., x_2 + f_1 + u_1 = 5 + u_2) rather than as the more transparent inequality form (available >= r_j) with a separate surplus definition. While mathematically equivalent, the equality form obscures the logical structure of 'satisfy demand, carry the remainder forward'.

The upper bounds on u_j are set to 6 (the maximum r_j) without explicit justification. While valid for optimal solutions (no reason to hold more than max demand in surplus), the reasoning is not stated, and a tighter or data-driven bound would strengthen the formulation.

The objective expression uses hardcoded numeric coefficients (10, 1, 3) rather than referencing the parameter names (a, b, c), reducing readability and making it harder to verify correctness against the parameter list.

There is no explicit terminal condition or note that tools sent for slow repair at stages 8 and 9 (s_8, s_9) return after the planning horizon (stages 11 and 12) and thus provide no benefit, only cost. While implicitly handled by their absence from later flow constraints, an explicit acknowledgment would prevent a later formulation from accidentally adding spurious return terms.

The repair-split constraints (s_j + f_j = r_j) correctly enforce that all used tools are repaired, but the formulation does not explicitly state that no repair is required after stage n (i.e., s_10 and f_10 are intentionally absent). A later reader might wonder whether this is an omission or a deliberate modeling choice.

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
n = 10
r = [3, 5, 2, 4, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1]  # 0-indexed: r[0]=r_1, ..., r[9]=r_10
a = 10
b = 1
c = 3
p = 3
q = 1

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables (0-indexed: x[0]=x_1, ..., x[9]=x_10; s[0]=s_1, ..., s[8]=s_9; f[0]=f_1, ..., f[8]=f_9)
x = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, name=f"x_{j+1}") for j in range(n)]
s = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, name=f"s_{j+1}") for j in range(n - 1)]  # s_1 .. s_9
f = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, name=f"f_{j+1}") for j in range(n - 1)]  # f_1 .. f_9

# Objective: minimize total cost
obj = a * quicksum(x[j] for j in range(n)) + b * quicksum(s[j] for j in range(n - 1)) + c * quicksum(f[j] for j in range(n - 1))
m.setObjective(obj, "minimize")

# Repair split constraints: at end of stage j (j=1..9), all r_j tools sent for repair
for j in range(n - 1):  # j=0..8 corresponds to stage 1..9
    m.addCons(s[j] + f[j] == r[j], name=f"repair_split_{j+1}")

# Availability constraints: at stage j, tools available = r_j
# Stage j (1-indexed): x_j + (s_{j-p} if j-p>=1) + (f_{j-q} if j-q>=1) = r_j
for j in range(n):  # j=0..9 corresponds to stage 1..10
    stage = j + 1  # 1-indexed stage number
    terms = [x[j]]
    # Slow repair returns: sent at end of stage (stage - p), available at stage
    if stage - p >= 1:
        terms.append(s[stage - p - 1])  # 0-indexed: s[stage-p-1]
    # Fast repair returns: sent at end of stage (stage - q), available at stage
    if stage - q >= 1:
        terms.append(f[stage - q - 1])  # 0-indexed: f[stage-q-1]
    m.addCons(quicksum(terms) == r[j], name=f"availability_{stage}")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
n = 10
r = [3, 5, 2, 4, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1]  # 0-indexed: r[0]=r_1, ..., r[9]=r_10
a = 10
b = 1
c = 3
p = 3
q = 1

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables (0-indexed: x[0]=x_1, ..., x[9]=x_10; s[0]=s_1, ..., s[8]=s_9; f[0]=f_1, ..., f[8]=f_9)
x = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, name=f"x_{j+1}") for j in range(n)]
s = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, name=f"s_{j+1}") for j in range(n - 1)]  # s_1 .. s_9
f = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, name=f"f_{j+1}") for j in range(n - 1)]  # f_1 .. f_9
# Inventory carried over from stage j to stage j+1 (tools available but not used)
y = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, name=f"y_{j+1}") for j in range(n - 1)]  # y_1 .. y_9

# Objective: minimize total cost
obj = a * quicksum(x[j] for j in range(n)) + b * quicksum(s[j] for j in range(n - 1)) + c * quicksum(f[j] for j in range(n - 1))
m.setObjective(obj, "minimize")

# Repair split constraints: at end of stage j (j=1..n-1), all r_j tools used are sent for repair
for j in range(n - 1):
    m.addCons(s[j] + f[j] == r[j], name=f"repair_split_{j+1}")

# Inventory balance and availability constraints
# At stage j+1 (0-indexed j): available = carryover + new purchases + slow returns + fast returns
# For stages 1..n-1: y[j] = available - r[j]  (excess tools carry over)
# For stage n: available >= r[n-1] (no carryover needed, tools discarded after)
for j in range(n):
    terms = [x[j]]
    if j >= 1:
        terms.append(y[j - 1])       # tools carried over from previous stage
    if j >= p:
        terms.append(s[j - p])       # slow repair: sent at end of stage (j-p+1), returns at stage (j+1)
    if j >= q:
        terms.append(f[j - q])       # fast repair: sent at end of stage (j-q+1), returns at stage (j+1)

    if j < n - 1:
        # Inventory balance: excess tools carry to next stage
        m.addCons(quicksum(terms) - r[j] == y[j], name=f"inventory_balance_{j+1}")
    else:
        # Final stage: need at least r_n tools, no further use
        m.addCons(quicksum(terms) >= r[j], name=f"availability_{j+1}")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")
    for j in range(n):
        print(f"x_{j+1} = {m.getVal(x[j])}")
    for j in range(n - 1):
        print(f"s_{j+1} = {m.getVal(s[j])}")
    for j in range(n - 1):
        print(f"f_{j+1} = {m.getVal(f[j])}")
    for j in range(n - 1):
        print(f"y_{j+1} = {m.getVal(y[j])}")

weak_points: Availability constraints use equality (=) instead of inequality (≥). For example, 'x_3 + f_2 = 2' is infeasible if f_2 > 2 (e.g., if all 5 tools from stage 2 are fast-repaired, f_2 = 5 > r_3 = 2). The correct form is x_j + (returned tools) ≥ r_j, because tools returned from prior repairs are already committed and cannot be discarded; excess tools simply sit idle without going to repair.

Because the availability constraints are equalities, the model can become infeasible for valid repair decisions made in earlier stages, which fundamentally breaks the optimization. A later formulation must replace all ten availability equalities with ≥ inequalities.

The repair-split constraints (s_j + f_j = r_j) are correct and consistent with the problem statement, but they interact incorrectly with the equality availability constraints: the split fixes the total tools entering repair, while the availability equality forces the total tools entering the stage to match r_j exactly, creating an over-constrained system when returned tools exceed demand.

weak_points: No variable or constraint tracks unused tools that carry over between stages: if more tools are available than r_j at some stage, the surplus is not modeled as available in subsequent stages, which can force unnecessary new purchases and overestimate the true optimal cost.

Availability constraints use '>=' rather than '='; combined with the absence of carry-over tracking, the feasible region is a strict subset of the true problem's feasible region, so the formulation's optimum may be worse than the true optimum.

The repair-split equalities (s_j + f_j = r_j) implicitly assume exactly r_j tools are consumed each stage, but there is no explicit 'tools used = r_j' constraint decoupled from the repair decision; the linkage is only indirect through the availability inequality.

Bounds on all variables are uniformly set to [0, 6] (the maximum r_j); while valid, tighter stage-specific bounds (e.g., s_j + f_j = r_j already caps the sum) are not exploited, which is a minor modelling inefficiency rather than a correctness issue.

This mislabeling could confuse a later reader or reformulation.

The flow constraints are written as equalities (e.g., x_2 + f_1 + u_1 = 5 + u_2) rather than as the more transparent inequality form (available >= r_j) with a separate surplus definition. While mathematically equivalent, the equality form obscures the logical structure of 'satisfy demand, carry the remainder forward'.

The upper bounds on u_j are set to 6 (the maximum r_j) without explicit justification. While valid for optimal solutions (no reason to hold more than max demand in surplus), the reasoning is not stated, and a tighter or data-driven bound would strengthen the formulation.

The objective expression uses hardcoded numeric coefficients (10, 1, 3) rather than referencing the parameter names (a, b, c), reducing readability and making it harder to verify correctness against the parameter list.

There is no explicit terminal condition or note that tools sent for slow repair at stages 8 and 9 (s_8, s_9) return after the planning horizon (stages 11 and 12) and thus provide no benefit, only cost. While implicitly handled by their absence from later flow constraints, an explicit acknowledgment would prevent a later formulation from accidentally adding spurious return terms.

The repair-split constraints (s_j + f_j = r_j) correctly enforce that all used tools are repaired, but the formulation does not explicitly state that no repair is required after stage n (i.e., s_10 and f_10 are intentionally absent). A later reader might wonder whether this is an omission or a deliberate modeling choice.

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
n = 10
r = [3, 5, 2, 4, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1]  # 0-indexed: r[0]=r_1, ..., r[9]=r_10
a = 10
b = 1
c = 3
p = 3
q = 1

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables (0-indexed: x[0]=x_1, ..., x[9]=x_10; s[0]=s_1, ..., s[8]=s_9; f[0]=f_1, ..., f[8]=f_9)
x = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, name=f"x_{j+1}") for j in range(n)]
s = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, name=f"s_{j+1}") for j in range(n - 1)]  # s_1 .. s_9
f = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, name=f"f_{j+1}") for j in range(n - 1)]  # f_1 .. f_9

# Objective: minimize total cost
obj = a * quicksum(x[j] for j in range(n)) + b * quicksum(s[j] for j in range(n - 1)) + c * quicksum(f[j] for j in range(n - 1))
m.setObjective(obj, "minimize")

# Repair split constraints: at end of stage j (j=1..9), all r_j tools sent for repair
for j in range(n - 1):  # j=0..8 corresponds to stage 1..9
    m.addCons(s[j] + f[j] == r[j], name=f"repair_split_{j+1}")

# Availability constraints: at stage j, tools available = r_j
# Stage j (1-indexed): x_j + (s_{j-p} if j-p>=1) + (f_{j-q} if j-q>=1) = r_j
for j in range(n):  # j=0..9 corresponds to stage 1..10
    stage = j + 1  # 1-indexed stage number
    terms = [x[j]]
    # Slow repair returns: sent at end of stage (stage - p), available at stage
    if stage - p >= 1:
        terms.append(s[stage - p - 1])  # 0-indexed: s[stage-p-1]
    # Fast repair returns: sent at end of stage (stage - q), available at stage
    if stage - q >= 1:
        terms.append(f[stage - q - 1])  # 0-indexed: f[stage-q-1]
    m.addCons(quicksum(terms) == r[j], name=f"availability_{stage}")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

obj = a * quicksum(x[j] for j in range(n)) + b * quicksum(s[j] for j in range(n - 1)) + c * quicksum(f[j] for j in range(n - 1))
m.setObjective(obj, "minimize")

# For stages 1..n-1: y[j] = available - r[j]  (excess tools carry over)
# For stage n: available >= r[n-1] (no carryover needed, tools discarded after)
for j in range(n):
    terms = [x[j]]
    if j >= 1:

    if j >= p:
        terms.append(s[j - p])       # slow repair: sent at end of stage (j-p+1), returns at stage (j+1)
    if j >= q:

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data transcribed from problem
max_heavy = 28
max_light = 12
fuel_limit = 10000
dist = [450, 480, 540, 600]
p_h = [0.03, 0.10, 0.05, 0.05]
p_l = [0.08, 0.11, 0.12, 0.09]
rate_heavy = 2
rate_light = 3
rate_empty = 4
fuel_tl = 100

# Fuel per bomb trip to each target
fuel_h = [dist[i] / rate_heavy + dist[i] / rate_empty + fuel_tl for i in range(4)]
fuel_l = [dist[i] / rate_light + dist[i] / rate_empty + fuel_tl for i in range(4)]

# Precompute survival probability tables: q[i][h][l] = (1-p_h[i])^h * (1-p_l[i])^l
q_tables = []
for i in range(4):
    a = 1 - p_h[i]
    b = 1 - p_l[i]
    table = [[a ** h * b ** l for l in range(max_light + 1)] for h in range(max_heavy + 1)]
    q_tables.append(table)

# Create SCIP model with linear constraints
m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

h_vars = [m.addVar(f"h_{i}", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=max_heavy) for i in range(4)]
l_vars = [m.addVar(f"l_{i}", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=max_light) for i in range(4)]

m.addCons(quicksum(h_vars) <= max_heavy, "heavy_stockpile")
m.addCons(quicksum(l_vars) <= max_light, "light_stockpile")
m.addCons(quicksum(fuel_h[i] * h_vars[i] + fuel_l[i] * l_vars[i] for i in range(4)) <= fuel_limit, "fuel")

# The objective is nonlinear (involves powers of integer variables), so enumerate
best_prob = -1.0
best_sol = None

for h1 in range(max_heavy + 1):
    fh1 = fuel_h[0] * h1
    if fh1 > fuel_limit:
        break
    for h2 in range(max_heavy + 1):
        fh12 = fh1 + fuel_h[1] * h2
        if fh12 > fuel_limit:
            break
        for h3 in range(max_heavy + 1):
            fh123 = fh12 + fuel_h[2] * h3
            if fh123 > fuel_limit:
                break
            for h4 in range(max_heavy + 1):
                fh = fh123 + fuel_h[3] * h4
                if fh > fuel_limit:
                    break
                hs = h1 + h2 + h3 + h4
                if hs > max_heavy:
                    break
                rem = fuel_limit - fh
                q1 = q_tables[0][h1]
                q2 = q_tables[1][h2]
                q3 = q_tables[2][h3]
                q4 = q_tables[3][h4]
                for l1 in range(max_light + 1):
                    fl1 = fuel_l[0] * l1
                    if fl1 > rem:
                        break
                    q1v = q1[l1]
                    for l2 in range(max_light + 1):
                        fl12 = fl1 + fuel_l[1] * l2
                        if fl12 > rem:
                            break
                        if l1 + l2 > max_light:
                            break
                        q2v = q2[l2]
                        for l3 in range(max_light + 1):
                            fl123 = fl12 + fuel_l[2] * l3
                            if fl123 > rem:
                                break
                            if l1 + l2 + l3 > max_light:
                                break
                            q3v = q3[l3]
                            for l4 in range(max_light + 1):
                                if l1 + l2 + l3 + l4 > max_light:
                                    break
                                if fl123 + fuel_l[3] * l4 > rem:
                                    break
                                q4v = q4[l4]
                                # P(0 destroyed)
                                p0 = q1v * q2v * q3v * q4v
                                # P(exactly 1 destroyed)
                                p1_ = ((1 - q1v) * q2v * q3v * q4v
                                       + q1v * (1 - q2v) * q3v * q4v
                                       + q1v * q2v * (1 - q3v) * q4v
                                       + q1v * q2v * q3v * (1 - q4v))
                                prob = 1.0 - p0 - p1_
                                if prob > best_prob:
                                    best_prob = prob
                                    best_sol = (h1, h2, h3, h4, l1, l2, l3, l4)

print(f"Optimal heavy bombs: h1={best_sol[0]}, h2={best_sol[1]}, h3={best_sol[2]}, h4={best_sol[3]}")
print(f"Optimal light bombs: l1={best_sol[4]}, l2={best_sol[5]}, l3={best_sol[6]}, l4={best_sol[7]}")
print(f"Max probability of success: {best_prob}")

# Set a linear objective for SCIP and solve (demonstrates the model)
m.setObjective(quicksum(h_vars) + quicksum(l_vars), "minimize")
m.optimize()

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data transcribed from problem
max_heavy = 28
max_light = 12
fuel_limit = 10000
dist = [450, 480, 540, 600]
p_h = [0.03, 0.10, 0.05, 0.05]
p_l = [0.08, 0.11, 0.12, 0.09]
rate_heavy = 2
rate_light = 3
rate_empty = 4
fuel_tl = 100

# Fuel per bomb trip to each target
fuel_h = [dist[i] / rate_heavy + dist[i] / rate_empty + fuel_tl for i in range(4)]
fuel_l = [dist[i] / rate_light + dist[i] / rate_empty + fuel_tl for i in range(4)]

# Precompute survival probability tables: q[i][h][l] = (1-p_h[i])^h * (1-p_l[i])^l
q_tables = []
for i in range(4):
    a = 1 - p_h[i]
    b = 1 - p_l[i]
    table = [[a ** h * b ** l for l in range(max_light + 1)] for h in range(max_heavy + 1)]
    q_tables.append(table)

# Create SCIP model with linear constraints
m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

h_vars = [m.addVar(f"h_{i}", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=max_heavy) for i in range(4)]
l_vars = [m.addVar(f"l_{i}", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=max_light) for i in range(4)]

m.addCons(quicksum(h_vars) <= max_heavy, "heavy_stockpile")
m.addCons(quicksum(l_vars) <= max_light, "light_stockpile")
m.addCons(quicksum(fuel_h[i] * h_vars[i] + fuel_l[i] * l_vars[i] for i in range(4)) <= fuel_limit, "fuel")

# The objective is nonlinear (involves powers of integer variables), so enumerate
best_prob = -1.0
best_sol = None

for h1 in range(max_heavy + 1):
    fh1 = fuel_h[0] * h1
    if fh1 > fuel_limit:
        break
    for h2 in range(max_heavy + 1):
        fh12 = fh1 + fuel_h[1] * h2
        if fh12 > fuel_limit:
            break
        for h3 in range(max_heavy + 1):
            fh123 = fh12 + fuel_h[2] * h3
            if fh123 > fuel_limit:
                break
            for h4 in range(max_heavy + 1):
                fh = fh123 + fuel_h[3] * h4
                if fh > fuel_limit:
                    break
                hs = h1 + h2 + h3 + h4
                if hs > max_heavy:
                    break
                rem = fuel_limit - fh
                q1 = q_tables[0][h1]
                q2 = q_tables[1][h2]
                q3 = q_tables[2][h3]
                q4 = q_tables[3][h4]
                for l1 in range(max_light + 1):
                    fl1 = fuel_l[0] * l1
                    if fl1 > rem:
                        break
                    q1v = q1[l1]
                    for l2 in range(max_light + 1):
                        fl12 = fl1 + fuel_l[1] * l2
                        if fl12 > rem:
                            break
                        if l1 + l2 > max_light:
                            break
                        q2v = q2[l2]
                        for l3 in range(max_light + 1):
                            fl123 = fl12 + fuel_l[2] * l3
                            if fl123 > rem:
                                break
                            if l1 + l2 + l3 > max_light:
                                break
                            q3v = q3[l3]
                            for l4 in range(max_light + 1):
                                if l1 + l2 + l3 + l4 > max_light:
                                    break
                                if fl123 + fuel_l[3] * l4 > rem:
                                    break
                                q4v = q4[l4]
                                # P(0 destroyed)
                                p0 = q1v * q2v * q3v * q4v
                                # P(exactly 1 destroyed)
                                p1_ = ((1 - q1v) * q2v * q3v * q4v
                                       + q1v * (1 - q2v) * q3v * q4v
                                       + q1v * q2v * (1 - q3v) * q4v
                                       + q1v * q2v * q3v * (1 - q4v))
                                prob = 1.0 - p0 - p1_
                                if prob > best_prob:
                                    best_prob = prob
                                    best_sol = (h1, h2, h3, h4, l1, l2, l3, l4)

print(f"Optimal heavy bombs: h1={best_sol[0]}, h2={best_sol[1]}, h3={best_sol[2]}, h4={best_sol[3]}")
print(f"Optimal light bombs: l1={best_sol[4]}, l2={best_sol[5]}, l3={best_sol[6]}, l4={best_sol[7]}")
print(f"Max probability of success: {best_prob}")

# Set a linear objective for SCIP and solve (demonstrates the model)
m.setObjective(quicksum(h_vars) + quicksum(l_vars), "minimize")
m.optimize()
st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data transcribed from problem
max_heavy = 28
max_light = 12
fuel_limit = 10000
dist = [450, 480, 540, 600]
p_h = [0.03, 0.10, 0.05, 0.05]
p_l = [0.08, 0.11, 0.12, 0.09]
rate_heavy = 2
rate_light = 3
rate_empty = 4
fuel_tl = 100

# Fuel per bomb trip to each target
fuel_h = [dist[i] / rate_heavy + dist[i] / rate_empty + fuel_tl for i in range(4)]
fuel_l = [dist[i] / rate_light + dist[i] / rate_empty + fuel_tl for i in range(4)]

# Precompute survival probability tables: q[i][h][l] = (1-p_h[i])^h * (1-p_l[i])^l
q_tables = []
for i in range(4):
    a = 1 - p_h[i]
    b = 1 - p_l[i]
    table = [[a ** h * b ** l for l in range(max_light + 1)] for h in range(max_heavy + 1)]
    q_tables.append(table)

# Create SCIP model with linear constraints
m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

h_vars = [m.addVar(f"h_{i}", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=max_heavy) for i in range(4)]
l_vars = [m.addVar(f"l_{i}", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=max_light) for i in range(4)]

m.addCons(quicksum(h_vars) <= max_heavy, "heavy_stockpile")
m.addCons(quicksum(l_vars) <= max_light, "light_stockpile")
m.addCons(quicksum(fuel_h[i] * h_vars[i] + fuel_l[i] * l_vars[i] for i in range(4)) <= fuel_limit, "fuel")

# The objective is nonlinear (involves powers of integer variables), so enumerate
best_prob = -1.0
best_sol = None

for h1 in range(max_heavy + 1):
    fh1 = fuel_h[0] * h1
    if fh1 > fuel_limit:
        break
    for h2 in range(max_heavy + 1):
        fh12 = fh1 + fuel_h[1] * h2
        if fh12 > fuel_limit:
            break
        for h3 in range(max_heavy + 1):
            fh123 = fh12 + fuel_h[2] * h3
            if fh123 > fuel_limit:
                break
            for h4 in range(max_heavy + 1):
                fh = fh123 + fuel_h[3] * h4
                if fh > fuel_limit:
                    break
                hs = h1 + h2 + h3 + h4
                if hs > max_heavy:
                    break
                rem = fuel_limit - fh
                q1 = q_tables[0][h1]
                q2 = q_tables[1][h2]
                q3 = q_tables[2][h3]
                q4 = q_tables[3][h4]
                for l1 in range(max_light + 1):
                    fl1 = fuel_l[0] * l1
                    if fl1 > rem:
                        break
                    q1v = q1[l1]
                    for l2 in range(max_light + 1):
                        fl12 = fl1 + fuel_l[1] * l2
                        if fl12 > rem:
                            break
                        if l1 + l2 > max_light:
                            break
                        q2v = q2[l2]
                        for l3 in range(max_light + 1):
                            fl123 = fl12 + fuel_l[2] * l3
                            if fl123 > rem:
                                break
                            if l1 + l2 + l3 > max_light:
                                break
                            q3v = q3[l3]
                            for l4 in range(max_light + 1):
                                if l1 + l2 + l3 + l4 > max_light:
                                    break
                                if fl123 + fuel_l[3] * l4 > rem:
                                    break
                                q4v = q4[l4]
                                # P(0 destroyed)
                                p0 = q1v * q2v * q3v * q4v
                                # P(exactly 1 destroyed)
                                p1_ = ((1 - q1v) * q2v * q3v * q4v
                                       + q1v * (1 - q2v) * q3v * q4v
                                       + q1v * q2v * (1 - q3v) * q4v
                                       + q1v * q2v * q3v * (1 - q4v))
                                prob = 1.0 - p0 - p1_
                                if prob > best_prob:
                                    best_prob = prob
                                    best_sol = (h1, h2, h3, h4, l1, l2, l3, l4)

print(f"Optimal heavy bombs: h1={best_sol[0]}, h2={best_sol[1]}, h3={best_sol[2]}, h4={best_sol[3]}")
print(f"Optimal light bombs: l1={best_sol[4]}, l2={best_sol[5]}, l3={best_sol[6]}, l4={best_sol[7]}")
print(f"Max probability of success: {best_prob}")

# Set a linear objective for SCIP and solve (demonstrates the model)
m.setObjective(quicksum(h_vars) + quicksum(l_vars), "minimize")
m.optimize()
st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data transcribed from problem
max_heavy = 28
max_light = 12
fuel_limit = 10000
dist = [450, 480, 540, 600]
p_h = [0.03, 0.10, 0.05, 0.05]
p_l = [0.08, 0.11, 0.12, 0.09]
rate_heavy = 2
rate_light = 3
rate_empty = 4
fuel_tl = 100

# Fuel per bomb trip to each target
fuel_h = [dist[i] / rate_heavy + dist[i] / rate_empty + fuel_tl for i in range(4)]
fuel_l = [dist[i] / rate_light + dist[i] / rate_empty + fuel_tl for i in range(4)]

# Precompute survival probability tables: q[i][h][l] = (1-p_h[i])^h * (1-p_l[i])^l
q_tables = []
for i in range(4):
    a = 1 - p_h[i]
    b = 1 - p_l[i]
    table = [[a ** h * b ** l for l in range(max_light + 1)] for h in range(max_heavy + 1)]
    q_tables.append(table)

# Create SCIP model with linear constraints
m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

h_vars = [m.addVar(f"h_{i}", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=max_heavy) for i in range(4)]
l_vars = [m.addVar(f"l_{i}", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=max_light) for i in range(4)]

m.addCons(quicksum(h_vars) <= max_heavy, "heavy_stockpile")
m.addCons(quicksum(l_vars) <= max_light, "light_stockpile")
m.addCons(quicksum(fuel_h[i] * h_vars[i] + fuel_l[i] * l_vars[i] for i in range(4)) <= fuel_limit, "fuel")

# The objective is nonlinear (involves powers of integer variables), so enumerate
best_prob = -1.0
best_sol = None

for h1 in range(max_heavy + 1):
    fh1 = fuel_h[0] * h1
    if fh1 > fuel_limit:
        break
    for h2 in range(max_heavy + 1):
        fh12 = fh1 + fuel_h[1] * h2
        if fh12 > fuel_limit:
            break
        for h3 in range(max_heavy + 1):
            fh123 = fh12 + fuel_h[2] * h3
            if fh123 > fuel_limit:
                break
            for h4 in range(max_heavy + 1):
                fh = fh123 + fuel_h[3] * h4
                if fh > fuel_limit:
                    break
                hs = h1 + h2 + h3 + h4
                if hs > max_heavy:
                    break
                rem = fuel_limit - fh
                q1 = q_tables[0][h1]
                q2 = q_tables[1][h2]
                q3 = q_tables[2][h3]
                q4 = q_tables[3][h4]
                for l1 in range(max_light + 1):
                    fl1 = fuel_l[0] * l1
                    if fl1 > rem:
                        break
                    q1v = q1[l1]
                    for l2 in range(max_light + 1):
                        fl12 = fl1 + fuel_l[1] * l2
                        if fl12 > rem:
                            break
                        if l1 + l2 > max_light:
                            break
                        q2v = q2[l2]
                        for l3 in range(max_light + 1):
                            fl123 = fl12 + fuel_l[2] * l3
                            if fl123 > rem:
                                break
                            if l1 + l2 + l3 > max_light:
                                break
                            q3v = q3[l3]
                            for l4 in range(max_light + 1):
                                if l1 + l2 + l3 + l4 > max_light:
                                    break
                                if fl123 + fuel_l[3] * l4 > rem:
                                    break
                                q4v = q4[l4]
                                # P(0 destroyed)
                                p0 = q1v * q2v * q3v * q4v
                                # P(exactly 1 destroyed)
                                p1_ = ((1 - q1v) * q2v * q3v * q4v
                                       + q1v * (1 - q2v) * q3v * q4v
                                       + q1v * q2v * (1 - q3v) * q4v
                                       + q1v * q2v * q3v * (1 - q4v))
                                prob = 1.0 - p0 - p1_
                                if prob > best_prob:
                                    best_prob = prob
                                    best_sol = (h1, h2, h3, h4, l1, l2, l3, l4)

print(f"Optimal heavy bombs: h1={best_sol[0]}, h2={best_sol[1]}, h3={best_sol[2]}, h4={best_sol[3]}")
print(f"Optimal light bombs: l1={best_sol[4]}, l2={best_sol[5]}, l3={best_sol[6]}, l4={best_sol[7]}")
print(f"Max probability of success: {best_prob}")

# Set a linear objective for SCIP and solve (demonstrates the model)
m.setObjective(quicksum(h_vars) + quicksum(l_vars), "minimize")
m.optimize()
st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
T = 110
r = 1000
M_curtain = 70000
M_clothing = 45000
OT_max = 10

# Preemptive priority weights (P1 >> P2 >> P3 >> P4)
P1 = 10**12
P2 = 10**8
P3 = 1000
P4 = 1

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables (continuous, >= 0)
x1 = m.addVar("x1", vtype="C", lb=0)
x2 = m.addVar("x2", vtype="C", lb=0)

# Deviation variables
d1_minus = m.addVar("d1_minus", vtype="C", lb=0)
d1_plus = m.addVar("d1_plus", vtype="C", lb=0)
d2_minus = m.addVar("d2_minus", vtype="C", lb=0)
d2_plus = m.addVar("d2_plus", vtype="C", lb=0)
d3_minus = m.addVar("d3_minus", vtype="C", lb=0)
d3_plus = m.addVar("d3_plus", vtype="C", lb=0)
d4_minus = m.addVar("d4_minus", vtype="C", lb=0)
d4_plus = m.addVar("d4_plus", vtype="C", lb=0)

# Goal 1: (x1 + x2)/1000 + d1_minus - d1_plus = 110
m.addCons(x1 / r + x2 / r + d1_minus - d1_plus == T, "goal_1_time_utilization")

# Goal 2: d1_plus + d2_minus - d2_plus = 10
m.addCons(d1_plus + d2_minus - d2_plus == OT_max, "goal_2_overtime_limit")

# Goal 3a: x1 + d3_minus - d3_plus = 70000
m.addCons(x1 + d3_minus - d3_plus == M_curtain, "goal_3a_curtain_minimum")

# Goal 3b: x2 + d4_minus - d4_plus = 45000
m.addCons(x2 + d4_minus - d4_plus == M_clothing, "goal_3b_clothing_minimum")

# Objective: minimize P1*d1_minus + P2*d2_plus + P3*(d3_minus + d4_minus) + P4*d1_plus
obj = P1 * d1_minus + P2 * d2_plus + P3 * (d3_minus + d4_minus) + P4 * d1_plus
m.setObjective(obj, "minimize")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")
    print(f"x1 (curtain): {m.getVal(x1)}")
    print(f"x2 (clothing): {m.getVal(x2)}")
    print(f"d1_minus: {m.getVal(d1_minus)}")
    print(f"d1_plus (overtime): {m.getVal(d1_plus)}")
    print(f"d2_plus: {m.getVal(d2_plus)}")
    print(f"d3_minus: {m.getVal(d3_minus)}")
    print(f"d4_minus: {m.getVal(d4_minus)}")

x2 = m.addVar("x2", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=M_car)
x3 = m.addVar("x3", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=M_blocks)
x4 = m.addVar("x4", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=M_doll)

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data literals
profit_robot = 15
profit_car = 8
profit_blocks = 12
profit_doll = 5

plastic_available = 1200
plastic_robot = 30
plastic_car = 10
plastic_blocks = 20
plastic_doll = 15

electronics_available = 800
electronics_robot = 8
electronics_car = 5
electronics_blocks = 3
electronics_doll = 2

M_robot = 40
M_car = 120
M_blocks = 60
M_doll = 80

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
x1 = m.addVar("x1", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=M_robot)
x2 = m.addVar("x2", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=M_car)
x3 = m.addVar("x3", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=M_blocks)
x4 = m.addVar("x4", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=M_doll)

y1 = m.addVar("y1", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y2 = m.addVar("y2", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y3 = m.addVar("y3", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y4 = m.addVar("y4", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)

# Objective: maximize profit
m.setObjective(profit_robot * x1 + profit_car * x2 + profit_blocks * x3 + profit_doll * x4, "maximize")

# Plastic constraint
m.addCons(plastic_robot * x1 + plastic_car * x2 + plastic_blocks * x3 + plastic_doll * x4 <= plastic_available, "plastic_limit")

# Electronics constraint
m.addCons(electronics_robot * x1 + electronics_car * x2 + electronics_blocks * x3 + electronics_doll * x4 <= electronics_available, "electronics_limit")

# Robots and dolls mutually exclusive
m.addCons(y1 + y4 <= 1, "robots_dolls_mutually_exclusive")

# Robot indicator link
m.addCons(x1 <= M_robot * y1, "robot_indicator_link")

# Doll indicator link
m.addCons(x4 <= M_doll * y4, "doll_indicator_link")

# Cars imply blocks
m.addCons(y2 <= y3, "cars_imply_blocks")

# Car indicator link
m.addCons(x2 <= M_car * y2, "car_indicator_link")

# Blocks indicator link
m.addCons(x3 <= M_blocks * y3, "blocks_indicator_link")

# Dolls cannot exceed cars
m.addCons(x4 <= x2, "dolls_le_cars")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data literals
profit_robot = 15
profit_car = 8
profit_blocks = 12
profit_doll = 5

plastic_available = 1200
plastic_robot = 30
plastic_car = 10
plastic_blocks = 20
plastic_doll = 15

electronics_available = 800
electronics_robot = 8
electronics_car = 5
electronics_blocks = 3
electronics_doll = 2

M_robot = 40
M_car = 120
M_blocks = 60
M_doll = 80

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
x1 = m.addVar("x1", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=M_robot)
x2 = m.addVar("x2", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=M_car)
x3 = m.addVar("x3", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=M_blocks)
x4 = m.addVar("x4", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=M_doll)

y1 = m.addVar("y1", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y2 = m.addVar("y2", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y3 = m.addVar("y3", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y4 = m.addVar("y4", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)

# Objective: maximize profit
m.setObjective(profit_robot * x1 + profit_car * x2 + profit_blocks * x3 + profit_doll * x4, "maximize")

# Plastic constraint
m.addCons(plastic_robot * x1 + plastic_car * x2 + plastic_blocks * x3 + plastic_doll * x4 <= plastic_available, "plastic_limit")

# Electronics constraint
m.addCons(electronics_robot * x1 + electronics_car * x2 + electronics_blocks * x3 + electronics_doll * x4 <= electronics_available, "electronics_limit")

# Robots and dolls mutually exclusive
m.addCons(y1 + y4 <= 1, "robots_dolls_mutually_exclusive")

# Robot indicator link
m.addCons(x1 <= M_robot * y1, "robot_indicator_link")

# Doll indicator link
m.addCons(x4 <= M_doll * y4, "doll_indicator_link")

# Cars imply blocks
m.addCons(y2 <= y3, "cars_imply_blocks")

# Car indicator link
m.addCons(x2 <= M_car * y2, "car_indicator_link")

# Blocks indicator link
m.addCons(x3 <= M_blocks * y3, "blocks_indicator_link")

# Dolls cannot exceed cars
m.addCons(x4 <= x2, "dolls_le_cars")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data literals
profit_robot = 15
profit_car = 8
profit_blocks = 12
profit_doll = 5

plastic_available = 1200
plastic_robot = 30
plastic_car = 10
plastic_blocks = 20
plastic_doll = 15

electronics_available = 800
electronics_robot = 8
electronics_car = 5
electronics_blocks = 3
electronics_doll = 2

M_robot = 40
M_car = 120
M_blocks = 60
M_doll = 80

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
x1 = m.addVar("x1", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=M_robot)
x2 = m.addVar("x2", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=M_car)
x3 = m.addVar("x3", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=M_blocks)
x4 = m.addVar("x4", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=M_doll)

y1 = m.addVar("y1", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y2 = m.addVar("y2", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y3 = m.addVar("y3", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y4 = m.addVar("y4", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)

# Objective: maximize profit
m.setObjective(profit_robot * x1 + profit_car * x2 + profit_blocks * x3 + profit_doll * x4, "maximize")

# Plastic constraint
m.addCons(plastic_robot * x1 + plastic_car * x2 + plastic_blocks * x3 + plastic_doll * x4 <= plastic_available, "plastic_limit")

# Electronics constraint
m.addCons(electronics_robot * x1 + electronics_car * x2 + electronics_blocks * x3 + electronics_doll * x4 <= electronics_available, "electronics_limit")

# Robots and dolls mutually exclusive
m.addCons(y1 + y4 <= 1, "robots_dolls_mutually_exclusive")

# Robot indicator link
m.addCons(x1 <= M_robot * y1, "robot_indicator_link")

# Doll indicator link
m.addCons(x4 <= M_doll * y4, "doll_indicator_link")

# Cars imply blocks
m.addCons(y2 <= y3, "cars_imply_blocks")

# Car indicator link
m.addCons(x2 <= M_car * y2, "car_indicator_link")

# Blocks indicator link
m.addCons(x3 <= M_blocks * y3, "blocks_indicator_link")

# Dolls cannot exceed cars
m.addCons(x4 <= x2, "dolls_le_cars")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

electronics_doll = 2

M_doll = 80

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data literals
cost_A = 120
cost_B = 110
cost_C = 100
tables_per_order_A = 20
tables_per_order_B = 15
tables_per_order_C = 15
min_tables = 150
max_tables = 600
min_B_tables_if_A = 30

# Derived constants
cost_per_order_A = cost_A * tables_per_order_A      # 2400
cost_per_order_B = cost_B * tables_per_order_B      # 1650
cost_per_order_C = cost_C * tables_per_order_C      # 1500
min_B_orders_if_A = min_B_tables_if_A // tables_per_order_B  # 2

# Model
m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
x_A = m.addVar("x_A", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=30)
x_B = m.addVar("x_B", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=40)
x_C = m.addVar("x_C", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=40)
y_A = m.addVar("y_A", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y_B = m.addVar("y_B", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)

# Objective: minimize total cost
obj = cost_per_order_A * x_A + cost_per_order_B * x_B + cost_per_order_C * x_C
m.setObjective(obj, "minimize")

# Constraint: minimum tables
m.addCons(tables_per_order_A * x_A + tables_per_order_B * x_B + tables_per_order_C * x_C >= min_tables, "min_tables")

# Constraint: maximum tables
m.addCons(tables_per_order_A * x_A + tables_per_order_B * x_B + tables_per_order_C * x_C <= max_tables, "max_tables")

# Link A: x_A <= 30 * y_A
m.addCons(x_A <= 30 * y_A, "link_A_upper")

# Link A: x_A >= y_A
m.addCons(x_A >= y_A, "link_A_lower")

# If A, at least 30 tables from B (i.e., at least 2 orders from B)
m.addCons(x_B >= min_B_orders_if_A * y_A, "min_B_if_A")

# Link B: x_B <= 40 * y_B
m.addCons(x_B <= 40 * y_B, "link_B_upper")

# Link B: x_B >= y_B
m.addCons(x_B >= y_B, "link_B_lower")

# If B, must order from C
m.addCons(x_C >= y_B, "C_if_B")

# Solve
m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data literals
cost_A = 120
cost_B = 110
cost_C = 100
tables_per_order_A = 20
tables_per_order_B = 15
tables_per_order_C = 15
min_tables = 150
max_tables = 600
min_B_tables_if_A = 30

# Derived constants
cost_per_order_A = cost_A * tables_per_order_A      # 2400
cost_per_order_B = cost_B * tables_per_order_B      # 1650
cost_per_order_C = cost_C * tables_per_order_C      # 1500
min_B_orders_if_A = min_B_tables_if_A // tables_per_order_B  # 2

# Model
m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
x_A = m.addVar("x_A", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=30)
x_B = m.addVar("x_B", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=40)
x_C = m.addVar("x_C", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=40)
y_A = m.addVar("y_A", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y_B = m.addVar("y_B", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)

# Objective: minimize total cost
obj = cost_per_order_A * x_A + cost_per_order_B * x_B + cost_per_order_C * x_C
m.setObjective(obj, "minimize")

# Constraint: minimum tables
m.addCons(tables_per_order_A * x_A + tables_per_order_B * x_B + tables_per_order_C * x_C >= min_tables, "min_tables")

# Constraint: maximum tables
m.addCons(tables_per_order_A * x_A + tables_per_order_B * x_B + tables_per_order_C * x_C <= max_tables, "max_tables")

# Link A: x_A <= 30 * y_A
m.addCons(x_A <= 30 * y_A, "link_A_upper")

# Link A: x_A >= y_A
m.addCons(x_A >= y_A, "link_A_lower")

# If A, at least 30 tables from B (i.e., at least 2 orders from B)
m.addCons(x_B >= min_B_orders_if_A * y_A, "min_B_if_A")

# Link B: x_B <= 40 * y_B
m.addCons(x_B <= 40 * y_B, "link_B_upper")

# Link B: x_B >= y_B
m.addCons(x_B >= y_B, "link_B_lower")

# If B, must order from C
m.addCons(x_C >= y_B, "C_if_B")

# Solve
m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

[export_rebinding_v1]
When business variables exist under different solver names, bind names instead of rewriting the model. Preserve the objective and constraints. Positive evidence: IDs 4, 8 and 25 passed independent audit after rebinding with unchanged objectives. Counterexample: ID 48 lacks total production roles, so name-only rebinding is insufficient; add missing roles instead.
Source: work/industryor_semantic_dag_dev_v0.2

[indicator_bidirectional_v1]
A binary indicator must be consistent with positive quantity in both directions: indicator <= quantity and quantity <= independent_upper_bound * indicator. Do not invent the upper bound. Positive evidence: IDs 9, 19, 20 and 21 recovered after scoped repair. Counterexample: indicator repair alone cannot fix a wrong business objective.
Source: work/industryor_semantic_dag_dev_v0.2

[objective_consistency_v1]
Recompute the business objective from semantic variables and check its direction. Goal-programming deviations are not business profit. ID 48 had feasible variables and an independent business optimum but a mismatched reported objective, and must remain rejected. Never inject a target value.
Source: work/industryor_semantic_dag_dev_v0.2/prob_048/branch_dag/regenerate/score.json

[regenerate_rebind_v1]
After regeneration, stale aliases can erase the export. Remove aliases whose solver names no longer exist, prefer verified canonical names, and rebind if needed. Rebinding completes evidence but does not prove business correctness. ID 48 demonstrates that objective semantics still need independent verification.
Source: work/industryor_semantic_dag_dev_v0.2/prob_048/branch_dag/regenerate/score.json

[dynamic_collection_binding_v1]
Dictionary comprehensions and simple loops may bind semantic names to expressions such as x['A']. Use only constant, code-verified index sets when repairing them. Do not guess nested or dynamic bindings. ID 19 supports this scoped mechanism; unsupported structures remain UNKNOWN.

cost_B = 110

min_B_orders_if_A = min_B_tables_if_A // tables_per_order_B  # 2

# Model
m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

x_A = m.addVar("x_A", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=30)
x_B = m.addVar("x_B", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=40)
x_C = m.addVar("x_C", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=40)
y_A = m.addVar("y_A", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y_B = m.addVar("y_B", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
max_demand = [5300, 4500, 5400]
selling_price = [124, 109, 115]
production_cost = [73.3, 52.9, 65.4]
production_quota = [500, 450, 550]
activation_cost = [170000, 150000, 100000]
min_batch = [20, 20, 16]
days_available = 22

n = 3

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
x = [m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=0, ub=max_demand[i], name=f"x_{i+1}") for i in range(n)]
y = [m.addVar(vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1, name=f"y_{i+1}") for i in range(n)]

# Objective: maximize profit
profit_per_unit = [selling_price[i] - production_cost[i] for i in range(n)]
obj = quicksum(profit_per_unit[i] * x[i] for i in range(n)) - quicksum(activation_cost[i] * y[i] for i in range(n))
m.setObjective(obj, "maximize")

# Production capacity constraint
m.addCons(quicksum(x[i] / production_quota[i] for i in range(n)) <= days_available, name="production_capacity")

# Demand constraints
for i in range(n):
    m.addCons(x[i] <= max_demand[i], name=f"demand_A{i+1}")

# Minimum batch constraints
for i in range(n):
    m.addCons(x[i] >= min_batch[i] * y[i], name=f"min_batch_A{i+1}")

# Linking constraints
for i in range(n):
    m.addCons(x[i] <= max_demand[i] * y[i], name=f"linking_A{i+1}")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
max_demand = [5300, 4500, 5400]
selling_price = [124, 109, 115]
production_cost = [73.3, 52.9, 65.4]
production_quota = [500, 450, 550]
activation_cost = [170000, 150000, 100000]
min_batch = [20, 20, 16]
days_available = 22

n = 3

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
x = [m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=0, ub=max_demand[i], name=f"x_{i+1}") for i in range(n)]
y = [m.addVar(vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1, name=f"y_{i+1}") for i in range(n)]

# Objective: maximize profit
profit_per_unit = [selling_price[i] - production_cost[i] for i in range(n)]
obj = quicksum(profit_per_unit[i] * x[i] for i in range(n)) - quicksum(activation_cost[i] * y[i] for i in range(n))
m.setObjective(obj, "maximize")

# Production capacity constraint
m.addCons(quicksum(x[i] / production_quota[i] for i in range(n)) <= days_available, name="production_capacity")

# Demand constraints
for i in range(n):
    m.addCons(x[i] <= max_demand[i], name=f"demand_A{i+1}")

# Minimum batch constraints
for i in range(n):
    m.addCons(x[i] >= min_batch[i] * y[i], name=f"min_batch_A{i+1}")

# Linking constraints
for i in range(n):
    m.addCons(x[i] <= max_demand[i] * y[i], name=f"linking_A{i+1}")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
max_demand = [5300, 4500, 5400]
selling_price = [124, 109, 115]
production_cost = [73.3, 52.9, 65.4]
production_quota = [500, 450, 550]
activation_cost = [170000, 150000, 100000]
min_batch = [20, 20, 16]
days_available = 22

n = 3

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
x = [m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=0, ub=max_demand[i], name=f"x_{i+1}") for i in range(n)]
y = [m.addVar(vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1, name=f"y_{i+1}") for i in range(n)]

# Objective: maximize profit
profit_per_unit = [selling_price[i] - production_cost[i] for i in range(n)]
obj = quicksum(profit_per_unit[i] * x[i] for i in range(n)) - quicksum(activation_cost[i] * y[i] for i in range(n))
m.setObjective(obj, "maximize")

# Production capacity constraint
m.addCons(quicksum(x[i] / production_quota[i] for i in range(n)) <= days_available, name="production_capacity")

# Demand constraints
for i in range(n):
    m.addCons(x[i] <= max_demand[i], name=f"demand_A{i+1}")

# Minimum batch constraints
for i in range(n):
    m.addCons(x[i] >= min_batch[i] * y[i], name=f"min_batch_A{i+1}")

# Linking constraints
for i in range(n):
    m.addCons(x[i] <= max_demand[i] * y[i], name=f"linking_A{i+1}")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data literals
labor_shirt = 3
material_shirt = 4
price_shirt = 120
varcost_shirt = 60

labor_short = 2
material_short = 3
price_short = 80
varcost_short = 40

labor_casual = 6
material_casual = 6
price_casual = 180
varcost_casual = 80

labor_avail = 1500
material_avail = 1600

fixed_shirt = 2000
fixed_short = 1500
fixed_casual = 1000

# Upper bounds from formulation
ub_x1 = 400
ub_x2 = 533.33
ub_x3 = 250

# Profit coefficients
profit1 = price_shirt - varcost_shirt      # 60
profit2 = price_short - varcost_short      # 40
profit3 = price_casual - varcost_casual    # 100

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
x1 = m.addVar("x1", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=ub_x1)
x2 = m.addVar("x2", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=ub_x2)
x3 = m.addVar("x3", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=ub_x3)
y1 = m.addVar("y1", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y2 = m.addVar("y2", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y3 = m.addVar("y3", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)

# Objective: maximize profit
obj = quicksum([
    profit1 * x1,
    profit2 * x2,
    profit3 * x3,
    -fixed_shirt * y1,
    -fixed_short * y2,
    -fixed_casual * y3
])
m.setObjective(obj, "maximize")

# Labor constraint
m.addCons(labor_shirt * x1 + labor_short * x2 + labor_casual * x3 <= labor_avail, "labor_limit")

# Material constraint
m.addCons(material_shirt * x1 + material_short * x2 + material_casual * x3 <= material_avail, "material_limit")

# Fixed-charge linking constraints
m.addCons(x1 <= ub_x1 * y1, "link_shirt")
m.addCons(x2 <= ub_x2 * y2, "link_short")
m.addCons(x3 <= ub_x3 * y3, "link_casual")

# Solve
m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data literals
labor_shirt = 3
material_shirt = 4
price_shirt = 120
varcost_shirt = 60

labor_short = 2
material_short = 3
price_short = 80
varcost_short = 40

labor_casual = 6
material_casual = 6
price_casual = 180
varcost_casual = 80

labor_avail = 1500
material_avail = 1600

fixed_shirt = 2000
fixed_short = 1500
fixed_casual = 1000

# Upper bounds from formulation
ub_x1 = 400
ub_x2 = 533.33
ub_x3 = 250

# Profit coefficients
profit1 = price_shirt - varcost_shirt      # 60
profit2 = price_short - varcost_short      # 40
profit3 = price_casual - varcost_casual    # 100

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
x1 = m.addVar("x1", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=ub_x1)
x2 = m.addVar("x2", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=ub_x2)
x3 = m.addVar("x3", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=ub_x3)
y1 = m.addVar("y1", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y2 = m.addVar("y2", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y3 = m.addVar("y3", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)

# Objective: maximize profit
obj = quicksum([
    profit1 * x1,
    profit2 * x2,
    profit3 * x3,
    -fixed_shirt * y1,
    -fixed_short * y2,
    -fixed_casual * y3
])
m.setObjective(obj, "maximize")

# Labor constraint
m.addCons(labor_shirt * x1 + labor_short * x2 + labor_casual * x3 <= labor_avail, "labor_limit")

# Material constraint
m.addCons(material_shirt * x1 + material_short * x2 + material_casual * x3 <= material_avail, "material_limit")

# Fixed-charge linking constraints
m.addCons(x1 <= ub_x1 * y1, "link_shirt")
m.addCons(x2 <= ub_x2 * y2, "link_short")
m.addCons(x3 <= ub_x3 * y3, "link_casual")

# Solve
m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

When business variables exist under different solver names, bind names instead of rewriting the model. Preserve the objective and constraints. A binary indicator must be consistent with positive quantity in both directions: indicator <= quantity and quantity <= independent_upper_bound * indicator. Do not invent the upper bound. # Data

pollution_truck = 100
pollution_van = 50
pollution_motorcycle = 10
pollution_ev = 0
max_pollution = 2000
min_truck_trips = 10
capacity_truck = 100
capacity_van = 80
capacity_motorcycle = 40
capacity_ev = 60
M_van = 23
M_ev = 30

# Model
m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Variables
t = m.addVar("t", vtype="I", lb=10, ub=18)
v = m.addVar("v", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=23)
mc = m.addVar("m", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=45)
e = m.addVar("e", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=30)
y_v = m.addVar("y_v", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y_e = m.addVar("y_e", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)

# Objective: minimize total pollution

    pollution_truck * t + pollution_van * v + pollution_motorcycle * mc + pollution_ev * e,
    "minimize"
)

# Constraints

m.addCons(capacity_truck * t + capacity_van * v + capacity_motorcycle * mc + capacity_ev * e >= total_units, "delivery_requirement")

# Pollution limit
m.addCons(pollution_truck * t + pollution_van * v + pollution_motorcycle * mc + pollution_ev * e <= max_pollution, "pollution_limit")

# Min truck trips
m.addCons(t >= min_truck_trips, "min_truck_trips")

# Mutual exclusivity
m.addCons(y_v + y_e <= 1, "mutual_exclusivity")

# Van link
m.addCons(v <= M_van * y_v, "van_link")

# EV link
m.addCons(e <= M_ev * y_e, "ev_link")

# Solve
m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")

    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

import json

# Data
total_units = 1800
pollution_truck = 100
pollution_van = 50
pollution_motorcycle = 10
pollution_ev = 0
max_pollution = 2000
min_truck_trips = 10
capacity_truck = 100
capacity_van = 80
capacity_motorcycle = 40
capacity_ev = 60
M = 45

# Model
m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Variables
t = m.addVar("t", vtype="I", lb=min_truck_trips, ub=M)
v = m.addVar("v", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=M)
mc = m.addVar("mc", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=M)
e = m.addVar("e", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=M)
y_v = m.addVar("y_v", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y_e = m.addVar("y_e", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)

# Objective: minimize total pollution

m.setObjective(obj, "minimize")

# Constraint: pollution limit
m.addCons(pollution_truck * t + pollution_van * v + pollution_motorcycle * mc + pollution_ev * e <= max_pollution, "pollution_limit")

# Solve

st = m.getStatus()

# x4 (option 2, year 2) matures -> 3*x4

m.addCons(x1 + x2 <= P, "initial_budget")

# Constraint 2: year2_budget (start of year 2: only x1 has matured; x2 is still locked for 2 years)
m.addCons(x3 + x4 <= 1.7 * x1, "year2_budget")

# Constraint 3: year3_budget (start of year 3: x3 matures from option 1, x2 matures from option 2)
m.addCons(x5 <= 1.7 * x3 + 3 * x2, "year3_budget")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")

x5 = m.addVar("x5", vtype="C", lb=0)  # option 1 invested at start of year 3

# Objective: maximize earnings (profit) by end of year 3
# Wealth at t=3 = 0.7*x1 + 2*x2 + 0.7*x3 + 2*x4 + 0.7*x5 + P
# Earnings = Wealth - P = 0.7*x1 + 2*x2 + 0.7*x3 + 2*x4 + 0.7*x5
m.setObjective(0.7 * x1 + 2 * x2 + 0.7 * x3 + 2 * x4 + 0.7 * x5, "maximize")

# At t=1, available = 1.7*x1 (opt1 matures) + (P - x1 - x2) (uninvested cash)

A binary indicator must be consistent with positive quantity in both directions: indicator <= quantity and quantity <= independent_upper_bound * indicator. Do not invent the upper bound. n = 6

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

x = [m.addVar(vtype="I", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), name=f"x{i+1}") for i in range(n)]

# Objective: minimize total salespeople
m.setObjective(quicksum(x), "minimize")

# Period 0 (2-6):   x1 + x6 >= 10
# Period 1 (6-10):  x1 + x2 >= 15

# Period 3 (14-18): x3 + x4 >= 20
# Period 4 (18-22): x4 + x5 >= 18

m.addCons(x[2] + x[3] >= req[3], name="coverage_period_4")
m.addCons(x[3] + x[4] >= req[4], name="coverage_period_5")
m.addCons(x[4] + x[5] >= req[5], name="coverage_period_6")

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables (continuous, bounds [0, 10000])
x1_A1 = m.addVar("x1_A1", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=10000)
x1_A2 = m.addVar("x1_A2", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=10000)
x2_A1 = m.addVar("x2_A1", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=10000)
x2_A2 = m.addVar("x2_A2", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=10000)
x3_A2 = m.addVar("x3_A2", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=10000)
x1_B1 = m.addVar("x1_B1", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=10000)
x1_B2 = m.addVar("x1_B2", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=10000)
x1_B3 = m.addVar("x1_B3", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=10000)
x2_B1 = m.addVar("x2_B1", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=10000)
x3_B2 = m.addVar("x3_B2", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=10000)

# Objective: maximize profit
obj = (P_1 - RM_1) * (x1_A1 + x1_A2) + (P_2 - RM_2) * (x2_A1 + x2_A2) + (P_3 - RM_3) * x3_A2 - C_A1 - C_A2 - C_B1 - C_B2 - C_B3
m.setObjective(obj, "maximize")

# Machine capacity constraints

m.addCons(t_1A2 * x1_A2 + t_2A2 * x2_A2 + t_3A2 * x3_A2 <= H_A2, "A2_capacity")
m.addCons(t_1B1 * x1_B1 + t_2B1 * x2_B1 <= H_B1, "B1_capacity")
m.addCons(t_1B2 * x1_B2 + t_3B2 * x3_B2 <= H_B2, "B2_capacity")
m.addCons(t_1B3 * x1_B3 <= H_B3, "B3_capacity")

# Flow balance constraints
m.addCons(x1_A1 + x1_A2 == x1_B1 + x1_B2 + x1_B3, "flow_balance_I")
m.addCons(x2_A1 + x2_A2 == x2_B1, "flow_balance_II")
m.addCons(x3_A2 == x3_B2, "flow_balance_III")

RM_3 = 0.50

P_3 = 2.80

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables (continuous, bounds [0, 10000])
x1_A1 = m.addVar("x1_A1", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=10000)
x1_A2 = m.addVar("x1_A2", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=10000)
x2_A1 = m.addVar("x2_A1", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=10000)
x2_A2 = m.addVar("x2_A2", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=10000)
x3_A2 = m.addVar("x3_A2", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=10000)
x1_B1 = m.addVar("x1_B1", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=10000)
x1_B2 = m.addVar("x1_B2", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=10000)
x1_B3 = m.addVar("x1_B3", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=10000)
x2_B1 = m.addVar("x2_B1", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=10000)
x3_B2 = m.addVar("x3_B2", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=10000)

# Objective: maximize profit
obj = (P_1 - RM_1) * (x1_A1 + x1_A2) + (P_2 - RM_2) * (x2_A1 + x2_A2) + (P_3 - RM_3) * x3_A2 - C_A1 - C_A2 - C_B1 - C_B2 - C_B3

m.addCons(t_1A2 * x1_A2 + t_2A2 * x2_A2 + t_3A2 * x3_A2 <= H_A2, "A2_capacity")
m.addCons(t_1B1 * x1_B1 + t_2B1 * x2_B1 <= H_B1, "B1_capacity")
m.addCons(t_1B2 * x1_B2 + t_3B2 * x3_B2 <= H_B2, "B2_capacity")
m.addCons(t_1B3 * x1_B3 <= H_B3, "B3_capacity")

m.addCons(x2_A1 + x2_A2 == x2_B1, "flow_balance_II")
m.addCons(x3_A2 == x3_B2, "flow_balance_III")

st = m.getStatus()

When business variables exist under different solver names, bind names instead of rewriting the model. Preserve the objective and constraints. Positive evidence: IDs 4, 8 and 25 passed independent audit after rebinding with unchanged objectives. Counterexample: ID 48 lacks total production roles, so name-only rebinding is insufficient; add missing roles instead.
Source: work/industryor_semantic_dag_dev_v0.2

[indicator_bidirectional_v1]
A binary indicator must be consistent with positive quantity in both directions: indicator <= quantity and quantity <= independent_upper_bound * indicator. Do not invent the upper bound. Positive evidence: IDs 9, 19, 20 and 21 recovered after scoped repair. Counterexample: indicator repair alone cannot fix a wrong business objective.
Source: work/industryor_semantic_dag_dev_v0.2

[objective_consistency_v1]
Recompute the business objective from semantic variables and check its direction. Goal-programming deviations are not business profit. ID 48 had feasible variables and an independent business optimum but a mismatched reported objective, and must remain rejected. Never inject a target value.
Source: work/industryor_semantic_dag_dev_v0.2/prob_048/branch_dag/regenerate/score.json

[regenerate_rebind_v1]
After regeneration, stale aliases can erase the export. Remove aliases whose solver names no longer exist, prefer verified canonical names, and rebind if needed. Source: work/industryor_semantic_dag_dev_v0.2/prob_048/branch_dag/regenerate/score.json

[dynamic_collection_binding_v1]
Dictionary comprehensions and simple loops may bind semantic names to expressions such as x['A']. Use only constant, code-verified index sets when repairing them. Do not guess nested or dynamic bindings. ID 19 supports this scoped mechanism; unsupported structures remain UNKNOWN.

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
F = 300000
r1 = 1.2
r2 = 1.5
r3 = 1.6
r4 = 1.4
L2 = 150000
L3 = 200000
L4 = 100000

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Variables (all continuous, >= 0)
x1 = m.addVar("x1", lb=0, vtype="C")
x2 = m.addVar("x2", lb=0, vtype="C")
x3 = m.addVar("x3", lb=0, vtype="C")
y = m.addVar("y", lb=0, vtype="C")
z = m.addVar("z", lb=0, vtype="C")
w = m.addVar("w", lb=0, vtype="C")
c1 = m.addVar("c1", lb=0, vtype="C")
c2 = m.addVar("c2", lb=0, vtype="C")
c3 = m.addVar("c3", lb=0, vtype="C")

# Constraints
# Year 1 budget
m.addCons(x1 + y + c1 == F, "year1_budget")
# Year 2 budget
m.addCons(x2 + z + c2 == r1 * x1 + c1, "year2_budget")
# Year 3 budget
m.addCons(x3 + w + c3 == r1 * x2 + r2 * y + c2, "year3_budget")
# Project limits
m.addCons(y <= L2, "project2_limit")
m.addCons(z <= L3, "project3_limit")
m.addCons(w <= L4, "project4_limit")

# Objective: maximize principal and interest at end of year 3
m.setObjective(r1 * x3 + r3 * z + r4 * w + c3, "maximize")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
F = 300000
r1 = 1.2
r2 = 1.5
r3 = 1.6
r4 = 1.4
L2 = 150000
L3 = 200000
L4 = 100000

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Variables (all continuous, >= 0)
x1 = m.addVar("x1", lb=0, vtype="C")
x2 = m.addVar("x2", lb=0, vtype="C")
x3 = m.addVar("x3", lb=0, vtype="C")
y = m.addVar("y", lb=0, vtype="C")
z = m.addVar("z", lb=0, vtype="C")
w = m.addVar("w", lb=0, vtype="C")
c1 = m.addVar("c1", lb=0, vtype="C")
c2 = m.addVar("c2", lb=0, vtype="C")
c3 = m.addVar("c3", lb=0, vtype="C")

# Constraints
# Year 1 budget
m.addCons(x1 + y + c1 == F, "year1_budget")
# Year 2 budget
m.addCons(x2 + z + c2 == r1 * x1 + c1, "year2_budget")
# Year 3 budget
m.addCons(x3 + w + c3 == r1 * x2 + r2 * y + c2, "year3_budget")
# Project limits
m.addCons(y <= L2, "project2_limit")
m.addCons(z <= L3, "project3_limit")
m.addCons(w <= L4, "project4_limit")

# Objective: maximize principal and interest at end of year 3
m.setObjective(r1 * x3 + r3 * z + r4 * w + c3, "maximize")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
demand = [1000, 2000, 1500, 2000, 1000, 1000]
supply = [1500, 1500, 1500, 1500, 1500, 1500]
target_p2 = 8000
target_p3 = 8000

# Valid positions for each type (1-indexed: 1=D-S1, 2=D-S2, 3=D-S3, 4=N-S1, 5=N-S2, 6=N-S3)
valid = {
    1: [1, 2, 4, 5],
    2: [2, 3, 5, 6],
    3: [1, 3, 4, 6],
    4: [1, 3, 4, 6],
    5: [2, 3, 5, 6],
    6: [3, 6]
}

def build_model(phase, phase1_opt=None, phase2_opt=None):
    m = Model()
    m.hideOutput()
    m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

    # Decision variables
    x = {}
    for t in range(1, 7):
        for p in valid[t]:
            x[(t, p)] = m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=0, ub=1500, name=f"x_{t}{p}")

    # Deviation variables
    d_minus = {}
    d_plus = {}
    for i in range(1, 9):
        d_minus[i] = m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=0, ub=9000, name=f"d{i}_minus")
        d_plus[i] = m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=0, ub=9000, name=f"d{i}_plus")

    # P1 goal constraints (demand satisfaction)
    m.addCons(x[(1,1)] + x[(3,1)] + x[(4,1)] + d_minus[1] - d_plus[1] == 1000, "goal_P1_S1_D")
    m.addCons(x[(1,2)] + x[(2,2)] + x[(5,2)] + d_minus[2] - d_plus[2] == 2000, "goal_P1_S2_D")
    m.addCons(x[(2,3)] + x[(3,3)] + x[(4,3)] + x[(5,3)] + x[(6,3)] + d_minus[3] - d_plus[3] == 1500, "goal_P1_S3_D")
    m.addCons(x[(1,4)] + x[(3,4)] + x[(4,4)] + d_minus[4] - d_plus[4] == 2000, "goal_P1_S1_N")
    m.addCons(x[(1,5)] + x[(2,5)] + x[(5,5)] + d_minus[5] - d_plus[5] == 1000, "goal_P1_S2_N")
    m.addCons(x[(2,6)] + x[(3,6)] + x[(4,6)] + x[(5,6)] + x[(6,6)] + d_minus[6] - d_plus[6] == 1000, "goal_P1_S3_N")

    # P2 goal constraint (preferred specialty)
    m.addCons(
        x[(1,1)] + x[(1,4)] + x[(2,2)] + x[(2,5)] + x[(3,1)] + x[(3,4)] +
        x[(4,3)] + x[(4,6)] + x[(5,3)] + x[(5,6)] + x[(6,3)] + x[(6,6)] +
        d_minus[7] - d_plus[7] == 8000, "goal_P2_pref_spec"
    )

    # P3 goal constraint (preferred city)
    m.addCons(
        x[(1,1)] + x[(1,2)] + x[(2,2)] + x[(2,3)] + x[(3,4)] + x[(3,6)] +
        x[(4,4)] + x[(4,6)] + x[(5,2)] + x[(5,3)] + x[(6,6)] +
        d_minus[8] - d_plus[8] == 8000, "goal_P3_pref_city"
    )

    # Supply constraints
    for t in range(1, 7):
        m.addCons(quicksum(x[(t, p)] for p in valid[t]) <= 1500, f"supply_type{t}")

    # Phase-specific objective
    if phase == 1:
        m.setObjective(quicksum(d_minus[i] for i in range(1, 7)), "minimize")
    elif phase == 2:
        m.addCons(quicksum(d_minus[i] for i in range(1, 7)) == phase1_opt, "fix_P1")
        m.setObjective(d_minus[7], "minimize")
    elif phase == 3:
        m.addCons(quicksum(d_minus[i] for i in range(1, 7)) == phase1_opt, "fix_P1")
        m.addCons(d_minus[7] == phase2_opt, "fix_P2")
        m.setObjective(d_minus[8], "minimize")

    m.optimize()
    return m

# Phase 1: Minimize P1 underachievement
m1 = build_model(1)
phase1_opt = m1.getObjVal() if m1.getNSols() > 0 else 0
print(f"Phase 1 (P1) optimal: {phase1_opt}")

# Phase 2: Fix P1, minimize P2 underachievement
m2 = build_model(2, phase1_opt=phase1_opt)
phase2_opt = m2.getObjVal() if m2.getNSols() > 0 else 0
print(f"Phase 2 (P2) optimal: {phase2_opt}")

# Phase 3: Fix P1 and P2, minimize P3 underachievement
m3 = build_model(3, phase1_opt=phase1_opt, phase2_opt=phase2_opt)

st = m3.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m3.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m3.getObjVal()}")
    print(f"At least {m3.getObjVal()} people can't meet P3")

weak_points: Variables are declared as 'continuous' rather than 'integer'; while the large scale (1500 per type) makes the continuous relaxation practically equivalent, a rigorous formulation for a personnel assignment problem should specify integrality.

The objective is written as a single weighted-sum expression P1*(...) + P2*(...) + P3*(...), which is a shorthand for lexicographic goal programming. A more explicit formulation would solve three sequential sub-problems (minimize P1 deviations, then fix and minimize P2, then fix and minimize P3) to guarantee true lexicographic priority and to directly yield the minimum d8⁻ asked in the question.

Upper bounds on all deviation variables are uniformly set to 9000, which is a loose bound. For example, d1⁻ (underachievement of the 1000-person Donghai-S1 demand) cannot exceed 1000, and d7⁻/d8⁻ cannot exceed 8000. Tighter bounds would improve numerical conditioning.

The formulation does not explicitly state the final answer extraction step: the question asks 'at least how many people can't meet P3,' which corresponds to the optimal value of d8⁻ after solving the lexicographic sequence. A complete formulation should note that the answer is the optimal d8⁻ value.

The source annotations for deviation variables d2 through d6 all repeat the same generic text ('All three types of professionals needed are fully met') rather than identifying the specific demand cell each deviation corresponds to, reducing traceability.

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
demand = [1000, 2000, 1500, 2000, 1000, 1000]
supply = [1500, 1500, 1500, 1500, 1500, 1500]
target_p2 = 8000
target_p3 = 8000

# Valid positions for each type (1-indexed: 1=D-S1, 2=D-S2, 3=D-S3, 4=N-S1, 5=N-S2, 6=N-S3)
valid = {
    1: [1, 2, 4, 5],
    2: [2, 3, 5, 6],
    3: [1, 3, 4, 6],
    4: [1, 3, 4, 6],
    5: [2, 3, 5, 6],
    6: [3, 6]
}

def build_model(phase, phase1_opt=None, phase2_opt=None):
    m = Model()
    m.hideOutput()
    m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

    # Decision variables
    x = {}
    for t in range(1, 7):
        for p in valid[t]:
            x[(t, p)] = m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=0, ub=1500, name=f"x_{t}{p}")

    # Deviation variables
    d_minus = {}
    d_plus = {}
    for i in range(1, 9):
        d_minus[i] = m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=0, ub=9000, name=f"d{i}_minus")
        d_plus[i] = m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=0, ub=9000, name=f"d{i}_plus")

    # P1 goal constraints (demand satisfaction)
    m.addCons(x[(1,1)] + x[(3,1)] + x[(4,1)] + d_minus[1] - d_plus[1] == 1000, "goal_P1_S1_D")
    m.addCons(x[(1,2)] + x[(2,2)] + x[(5,2)] + d_minus[2] - d_plus[2] == 2000, "goal_P1_S2_D")
    m.addCons(x[(2,3)] + x[(3,3)] + x[(4,3)] + x[(5,3)] + x[(6,3)] + d_minus[3] - d_plus[3] == 1500, "goal_P1_S3_D")
    m.addCons(x[(1,4)] + x[(3,4)] + x[(4,4)] + d_minus[4] - d_plus[4] == 2000, "goal_P1_S1_N")
    m.addCons(x[(1,5)] + x[(2,5)] + x[(5,5)] + d_minus[5] - d_plus[5] == 1000, "goal_P1_S2_N")
    m.addCons(x[(2,6)] + x[(3,6)] + x[(4,6)] + x[(5,6)] + x[(6,6)] + d_minus[6] - d_plus[6] == 1000, "goal_P1_S3_N")

    # P2 goal constraint (preferred specialty)
    m.addCons(
        x[(1,1)] + x[(1,4)] + x[(2,2)] + x[(2,5)] + x[(3,1)] + x[(3,4)] +
        x[(4,3)] + x[(4,6)] + x[(5,3)] + x[(5,6)] + x[(6,3)] + x[(6,6)] +
        d_minus[7] - d_plus[7] == 8000, "goal_P2_pref_spec"
    )

    # P3 goal constraint (preferred city)
    m.addCons(
        x[(1,1)] + x[(1,2)] + x[(2,2)] + x[(2,3)] + x[(3,4)] + x[(3,6)] +
        x[(4,4)] + x[(4,6)] + x[(5,2)] + x[(5,3)] + x[(6,6)] +
        d_minus[8] - d_plus[8] == 8000, "goal_P3_pref_city"
    )

    # Supply constraints
    for t in range(1, 7):
        m.addCons(quicksum(x[(t, p)] for p in valid[t]) <= 1500, f"supply_type{t}")

    # Phase-specific objective
    if phase == 1:
        m.setObjective(quicksum(d_minus[i] for i in range(1, 7)), "minimize")
    elif phase == 2:
        m.addCons(quicksum(d_minus[i] for i in range(1, 7)) == phase1_opt, "fix_P1")
        m.setObjective(d_minus[7], "minimize")
    elif phase == 3:
        m.addCons(quicksum(d_minus[i] for i in range(1, 7)) == phase1_opt, "fix_P1")
        m.addCons(d_minus[7] == phase2_opt, "fix_P2")
        m.setObjective(d_minus[8], "minimize")

    m.optimize()
    return m

# Phase 1: Minimize P1 underachievement
m1 = build_model(1)
phase1_opt = m1.getObjVal() if m1.getNSols() > 0 else 0
print(f"Phase 1 (P1) optimal: {phase1_opt}")

# Phase 2: Fix P1, minimize P2 underachievement
m2 = build_model(2, phase1_opt=phase1_opt)
phase2_opt = m2.getObjVal() if m2.getNSols() > 0 else 0
print(f"Phase 2 (P2) optimal: {phase2_opt}")

# Phase 3: Fix P1 and P2, minimize P3 underachievement
m3 = build_model(3, phase1_opt=phase1_opt, phase2_opt=phase2_opt)

st = m3.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
