from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
profit_apples = 2000
profit_pears = 1800
profit_oranges = 2200
profit_lemons = 3000
total_area = 120
M = 120

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
A = m.addVar("A", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=120)
P = m.addVar("P", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=120)
O = m.addVar("O", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=120)
L = m.addVar("L", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=120)

y_A = m.addVar("y_A", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y_P = m.addVar("y_P", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y_O = m.addVar("y_O", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y_L = m.addVar("y_L", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)

# Objective: maximize profit
m.setObjective(profit_apples * A + profit_pears * P + profit_oranges * O + profit_lemons * L, "maximize")

# Constraint: total area
m.addCons(A + P + O + L <= total_area, "total_area")

# Constraint: apple >= 2 * pear
m.addCons(A >= 2 * P, "apple_pear_ratio")

# Constraint: apple >= 3 * lemon
m.addCons(A >= 3 * L, "apple_lemon_ratio")

# Constraint: orange = 2 * lemon
m.addCons(O == 2 * L, "orange_lemon_ratio")

# Constraint: at most two types of fruit
m.addCons(y_A + y_P + y_O + y_L <= 2, "max_two_types")

# Linking constraints
m.addCons(A <= M * y_A, "link_apples")
m.addCons(P <= M * y_P, "link_pears")
m.addCons(O <= M * y_O, "link_oranges")
m.addCons(L <= M * y_L, "link_lemons")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")
    print(f"A = {m.getVal(A)}")
    print(f"P = {m.getVal(P)}")
    print(f"O = {m.getVal(O)}")
    print(f"L = {m.getVal(L)}")
    print(f"y_A = {m.getVal(y_A)}")
    print(f"y_P = {m.getVal(y_P)}")
    print(f"y_O = {m.getVal(y_O)}")
    print(f"y_L = {m.getVal(y_L)}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data literals
cost_A = 2.0
cost_B = 1.5
cost_C = 1.0
limit_A = 2000
limit_B = 2500
limit_C = 1200
proc_A = 0.5
proc_B = 0.4
proc_C = 0.3
price_A = 3.4
price_B = 2.85
price_C = 2.25
pct_A_in_brandA = 0.6
pct_B_in_brandA = 0.15
pct_C_in_brandA = 0.2
pct_C_in_brandB = 0.6
pct_C_in_brandC = 0.5

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
x1 = m.addVar("x1", lb=0, vtype="C")
x2 = m.addVar("x2", lb=0, vtype="C")
x3 = m.addVar("x3", lb=0, vtype="C")
a1 = m.addVar("a1", lb=0, vtype="C")
a2 = m.addVar("a2", lb=0, vtype="C")
a3 = m.addVar("a3", lb=0, vtype="C")
b1 = m.addVar("b1", lb=0, vtype="C")
b2 = m.addVar("b2", lb=0, vtype="C")
b3 = m.addVar("b3", lb=0, vtype="C")
c1 = m.addVar("c1", lb=0, vtype="C")
c2 = m.addVar("c2", lb=0, vtype="C")
c3 = m.addVar("c3", lb=0, vtype="C")

# Objective: maximize profit
obj = (price_A * x1 + price_B * x2 + price_C * x3
       - cost_A * (a1 + a2 + a3)
       - cost_B * (b1 + b2 + b3)
       - cost_C * (c1 + c2 + c3)
       - proc_A * x1 - proc_B * x2 - proc_C * x3)
m.setObjective(obj, "maximize")

# Mass balance constraints
m.addCons(a1 + b1 + c1 == x1, "mass_balance_brandA")
m.addCons(a2 + b2 + c2 == x2, "mass_balance_brandB")
m.addCons(a3 + b3 + c3 == x3, "mass_balance_brandC")

# Raw material monthly limits
m.addCons(a1 + a2 + a3 <= limit_A, "rawA_limit")
m.addCons(b1 + b2 + b3 <= limit_B, "rawB_limit")
m.addCons(c1 + c2 + c3 <= limit_C, "rawC_limit")

# Brand A composition constraints
m.addCons(a1 >= pct_A_in_brandA * x1, "brandA_min_rawA")
m.addCons(b1 >= pct_B_in_brandA * x1, "brandA_min_rawB")
m.addCons(c1 <= pct_C_in_brandA * x1, "brandA_max_rawC")

# Brand B composition constraints
m.addCons(c2 <= pct_C_in_brandB * x2, "brandB_max_rawC")

# Brand C composition constraints
m.addCons(c3 <= pct_C_in_brandC * x3, "brandC_max_rawC")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data literals
cost_A = 2.0
cost_B = 1.5
cost_C = 1.0
limit_A = 2000
limit_B = 2500
limit_C = 1200
proc_A = 0.5
proc_B = 0.4
proc_C = 0.3
price_A = 3.4
price_B = 2.85
price_C = 2.25
pct_A_in_brandA = 0.6
pct_B_in_brandA = 0.15
pct_C_in_brandA = 0.2
pct_C_in_brandB = 0.6
pct_C_in_brandC = 0.5

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
x1 = m.addVar("x1", lb=0, vtype="C")
x2 = m.addVar("x2", lb=0, vtype="C")
x3 = m.addVar("x3", lb=0, vtype="C")
a1 = m.addVar("a1", lb=0, vtype="C")
a2 = m.addVar("a2", lb=0, vtype="C")
a3 = m.addVar("a3", lb=0, vtype="C")
b1 = m.addVar("b1", lb=0, vtype="C")
b2 = m.addVar("b2", lb=0, vtype="C")
b3 = m.addVar("b3", lb=0, vtype="C")
c1 = m.addVar("c1", lb=0, vtype="C")
c2 = m.addVar("c2", lb=0, vtype="C")
c3 = m.addVar("c3", lb=0, vtype="C")

# Objective: maximize profit
obj = (price_A * x1 + price_B * x2 + price_C * x3
       - cost_A * (a1 + a2 + a3)
       - cost_B * (b1 + b2 + b3)
       - cost_C * (c1 + c2 + c3)
       - proc_A * x1 - proc_B * x2 - proc_C * x3)
m.setObjective(obj, "maximize")

# Mass balance constraints
m.addCons(a1 + b1 + c1 == x1, "mass_balance_brandA")
m.addCons(a2 + b2 + c2 == x2, "mass_balance_brandB")
m.addCons(a3 + b3 + c3 == x3, "mass_balance_brandC")

# Raw material monthly limits
m.addCons(a1 + a2 + a3 <= limit_A, "rawA_limit")
m.addCons(b1 + b2 + b3 <= limit_B, "rawB_limit")
m.addCons(c1 + c2 + c3 <= limit_C, "rawC_limit")

# Brand A composition constraints
m.addCons(a1 >= pct_A_in_brandA * x1, "brandA_min_rawA")
m.addCons(b1 >= pct_B_in_brandA * x1, "brandA_min_rawB")
m.addCons(c1 <= pct_C_in_brandA * x1, "brandA_max_rawC")

# Brand B composition constraints
m.addCons(c2 <= pct_C_in_brandB * x2, "brandB_max_rawC")

# Brand C composition constraints
m.addCons(c3 <= pct_C_in_brandC * x3, "brandC_max_rawC")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Distance matrix (symmetric), 1-indexed
d = {
    (1,2): 86, (1,3): 49, (1,4): 57, (1,5): 31, (1,6): 69, (1,7): 50,
    (2,1): 86, (2,3): 68, (2,4): 79, (2,5): 93, (2,6): 24, (2,7): 5,
    (3,1): 49, (3,2): 68, (3,4): 16, (3,5): 7,  (3,6): 72, (3,7): 67,
    (4,1): 57, (4,2): 79, (4,3): 16, (4,5): 90, (4,6): 69, (4,7): 1,
    (5,1): 31, (5,2): 93, (5,3): 7,  (5,4): 90, (5,6): 86, (5,7): 59,
    (6,1): 69, (6,2): 24, (6,3): 72, (6,4): 69, (6,5): 86, (6,7): 81,
    (7,1): 50, (7,2): 5,  (7,3): 67, (7,4): 1,  (7,5): 59, (7,6): 81,
}

n = 7
nodes = list(range(1, n + 1))
sub_nodes = list(range(2, n + 1))  # nodes 2..7 for MTZ

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Binary edge variables x[i,j]
x = {}
for i in nodes:
    for j in nodes:
        if i != j:
            x[i, j] = m.addVar(vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1, name=f"x_{i}_{j}")

# Continuous MTZ variables u[i] for i in 2..7
u = {}
for i in sub_nodes:
    u[i] = m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=1, ub=n - 1, name=f"u_{i}")

# Objective: minimize total distance
obj_terms = [d[i, j] * x[i, j] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j]
m.setObjective(quicksum(obj_terms), "minimize")

# Inflow constraints: each node has exactly one incoming edge
for i in nodes:
    inflow = quicksum(x[j, i] for j in nodes if j != i)
    m.addCons(inflow == 1, name=f"inflow_{i}")

# Outflow constraints: each node has exactly one outgoing edge
for i in nodes:
    outflow = quicksum(x[i, j] for j in nodes if j != i)
    m.addCons(outflow == 1, name=f"outflow_{i}")

# MTZ subtour elimination constraints
for i in sub_nodes:
    for j in sub_nodes:
        if i != j:
            m.addCons(u[i] - u[j] + n * x[j, i] <= n - 1, name=f"mtz_{i}_{j}")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

weak_points: MTZ subtour-elimination constraints use x_{j,i} in the term u_i - u_j + n*x_{j,i} <= n-1 instead of the standard x_{i,j}; while the resulting set is mathematically equivalent (it enforces a reversed position ordering that still eliminates subtours), this non-standard indexing is error-prone in implementation and could be misread as a bug.

The formulation models a symmetric TSP with 42 directed binary variables (x_{i,j} for all i≠j) rather than exploiting symmetry with 21 undirected edge variables; this doubles the variable count unnecessarily and adds redundant flow constraints (inflow_j and outflow_i are mirror images).

No explicit COPTPY model-building or solver-call structure is included (e.g., model creation, variable addition, constraint addition, objective setting, solve invocation, and solution extraction), which the problem statement specifically requests.

The auxiliary variable u_1 is never declared; although it is implicitly fixed at 1 by the MTZ structure (u_1 does not appear in any MTZ constraint), a self-contained formulation should state this or use bounds [1,1] to remove ambiguity.
The 'source' fields for parameters and variables are raw table-row fragments rather than clear references, making it harder to audit which matrix entry each parameter corresponds to.

If x_{i,j}=x_{j,i}=1, both MTZ inequalities require u_i < u_j and u_j < u_i simultaneously, which is impossible. Any valid TSP tour must use edges between non-depot nodes, so no feasible tour exists.

The MTZ subtour-elimination constraints should be applied in only one direction per unordered pair (e.g., only for i<j) when symmetry is enforced, or the symmetry constraints should be removed and a fully directed formulation used with MTZ on all directed arcs.

No explicit inflow (in-degree) constraints are stated. Although they are logically implied by the symmetry constraints combined with the outflow constraints, their absence reduces clarity and makes the formulation fragile if the symmetry constraints are later removed.
The original problem requests solving with COPTPY, but the candidate provides only the mathematical formulation without any solver code, variable creation, or solution extraction logic.

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Distance matrix (symmetric), 1-indexed
d = {
    (1,2): 86, (1,3): 49, (1,4): 57, (1,5): 31, (1,6): 69, (1,7): 50,
    (2,1): 86, (2,3): 68, (2,4): 79, (2,5): 93, (2,6): 24, (2,7): 5,
    (3,1): 49, (3,2): 68, (3,4): 16, (3,5): 7,  (3,6): 72, (3,7): 67,
    (4,1): 57, (4,2): 79, (4,3): 16, (4,5): 90, (4,6): 69, (4,7): 1,
    (5,1): 31, (5,2): 93, (5,3): 7,  (5,4): 90, (5,6): 86, (5,7): 59,
    (6,1): 69, (6,2): 24, (6,3): 72, (6,4): 69, (6,5): 86, (6,7): 81,
    (7,1): 50, (7,2): 5,  (7,3): 67, (7,4): 1,  (7,5): 59, (7,6): 81,
}

n = 7
nodes = list(range(1, n + 1))
sub_nodes = list(range(2, n + 1))  # nodes 2..7 for MTZ

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Binary edge variables x[i,j]
x = {}
for i in nodes:
    for j in nodes:
        if i != j:
            x[i, j] = m.addVar(vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1, name=f"x_{i}_{j}")

# Continuous MTZ variables u[i] for i in 2..7
u = {}
for i in sub_nodes:
    u[i] = m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=1, ub=n - 1, name=f"u_{i}")

# Objective: minimize total distance
obj_terms = [d[i, j] * x[i, j] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j]
m.setObjective(quicksum(obj_terms), "minimize")

# Inflow constraints: each node has exactly one incoming edge
for i in nodes:
    inflow = quicksum(x[j, i] for j in nodes if j != i)
    m.addCons(inflow == 1, name=f"inflow_{i}")

# Outflow constraints: each node has exactly one outgoing edge
for i in nodes:
    outflow = quicksum(x[i, j] for j in nodes if j != i)
    m.addCons(outflow == 1, name=f"outflow_{i}")

# MTZ subtour elimination constraints
for i in sub_nodes:
    for j in sub_nodes:
        if i != j:
            m.addCons(u[i] - u[j] + n * x[j, i] <= n - 1, name=f"mtz_{i}_{j}")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

    (2,1): 86, (2,3): 68, (2,4): 79, (2,5): 93, (2,6): 24, (2,7): 5,
    (3,1): 49, (3,2): 68, (3,4): 16, (3,5): 7,  (3,6): 72, (3,7): 67,
    (4,1): 57, (4,2): 79, (4,3): 16, (4,5): 90, (4,6): 69, (4,7): 1,
    (5,1): 31, (5,2): 93, (5,3): 7,  (5,4): 90, (5,6): 86, (5,7): 59,
    (6,1): 69, (6,2): 24, (6,3): 72, (6,4): 69, (6,5): 86, (6,7): 81,
    (7,1): 50, (7,2): 5,  (7,3): 67, (7,4): 1,  (7,5): 59, (7,6): 81,
}

n = 7
nodes = list(range(1, n + 1))
sub_nodes = list(range(2, n + 1))  # nodes 2..7 for MTZ

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Binary edge variables x[i,j]
x = {}
for i in nodes:
    for j in nodes:
        if i != j:
            x[i, j] = m.addVar(vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1, name=f"x_{i}_{j}")

# Continuous MTZ variables u[i] for i in 2..7
u = {}
for i in sub_nodes:
    u[i] = m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=1, ub=n - 1, name=f"u_{i}")

# Objective: minimize total distance
obj_terms = [d[i, j] * x[i, j] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j]
m.setObjective(quicksum(obj_terms), "minimize")

# Inflow constraints: each node has exactly one incoming edge
for i in nodes:
    inflow = quicksum(x[j, i] for j in nodes if j != i)
    m.addCons(inflow == 1, name=f"inflow_{i}")

# Outflow constraints: each node has exactly one outgoing edge
for i in nodes:
    outflow = quicksum(x[i, j] for j in nodes if j != i)
    m.addCons(outflow == 1, name=f"outflow_{i}")

# MTZ subtour elimination constraints
for i in sub_nodes:
    for j in sub_nodes:
        if i != j:
            m.addCons(u[i] - u[j] + n * x[j, i] <= n - 1, name=f"mtz_{i}_{j}")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

weak_points: Critical infeasibility: the combination of symmetry constraints (x_{i,j}=x_{j,i}) and bidirectional MTZ constraints (u_i - u_j + 7*x_{i,j} <= 6 AND u_j - u_i + 7*x_{j,i} <= 6 for all i,j in {2..7}, i!=j) makes the model infeasible. If x_{i,j}=x_{j,i}=1, both MTZ inequalities require u_i < u_j and u_j < u_i simultaneously, which is impossible. Any valid TSP tour must use edges between non-depot nodes, so no feasible tour exists.

The MTZ subtour-elimination constraints should be applied in only one direction per unordered pair (e.g., only for i<j) when symmetry is enforced, or the symmetry constraints should be removed and a fully directed formulation used with MTZ on all directed arcs.

No explicit inflow (in-degree) constraints are stated. Although they are logically implied by the symmetry constraints combined with the outflow constraints, their absence reduces clarity and makes the formulation fragile if the symmetry constraints are later removed.
The original problem requests solving with COPTPY, but the candidate provides only the mathematical formulation without any solver code, variable creation, or solution extraction logic.

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Distance matrix (symmetric), 1-indexed
d = {
    (1,2): 86, (1,3): 49, (1,4): 57, (1,5): 31, (1,6): 69, (1,7): 50,
    (2,1): 86, (2,3): 68, (2,4): 79, (2,5): 93, (2,6): 24, (2,7): 5,
    (3,1): 49, (3,2): 68, (3,4): 16, (3,5): 7,  (3,6): 72, (3,7): 67,
    (4,1): 57, (4,2): 79, (4,3): 16, (4,5): 90, (4,6): 69, (4,7): 1,
    (5,1): 31, (5,2): 93, (5,3): 7,  (5,4): 90, (5,6): 86, (5,7): 59,
    (6,1): 69, (6,2): 24, (6,3): 72, (6,4): 69, (6,5): 86, (6,7): 81,
    (7,1): 50, (7,2): 5,  (7,3): 67, (7,4): 1,  (7,5): 59, (7,6): 81,
}

n = 7
nodes = list(range(1, n + 1))
sub_nodes = list(range(2, n + 1))  # nodes 2..7 for MTZ

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Binary edge variables x[i,j]
x = {}
for i in nodes:
    for j in nodes:
        if i != j:
            x[i, j] = m.addVar(vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1, name=f"x_{i}_{j}")

# Continuous MTZ variables u[i] for i in 2..7
u = {}
for i in sub_nodes:
    u[i] = m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=1, ub=n - 1, name=f"u_{i}")

# Objective: minimize total distance
obj_terms = [d[i, j] * x[i, j] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j]
m.setObjective(quicksum(obj_terms), "minimize")

# Inflow constraints: each node has exactly one incoming edge
for i in nodes:
    inflow = quicksum(x[j, i] for j in nodes if j != i)
    m.addCons(inflow == 1, name=f"inflow_{i}")

# Outflow constraints: each node has exactly one outgoing edge
for i in nodes:
    outflow = quicksum(x[i, j] for j in nodes if j != i)
    m.addCons(outflow == 1, name=f"outflow_{i}")

# MTZ subtour elimination constraints
for i in sub_nodes:
    for j in sub_nodes:
        if i != j:
            m.addCons(u[i] - u[j] + n * x[j, i] <= n - 1, name=f"mtz_{i}_{j}")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

weak_points: Critical infeasibility: the combination of symmetry constraints (x_{i,j}=x_{j,i}) and bidirectional MTZ constraints (u_i - u_j + 7*x_{i,j} <= 6 AND u_j - u_i + 7*x_{j,i} <= 6 for all i,j in {2..7}, i!=j) makes the model infeasible. If x_{i,j}=x_{j,i}=1, both MTZ inequalities require u_i < u_j and u_j < u_i simultaneously, which is impossible. Any valid TSP tour must use edges between non-depot nodes, so no feasible tour exists.

The MTZ subtour-elimination constraints should be applied in only one direction per unordered pair (e.g., only for i<j) when symmetry is enforced, or the symmetry constraints should be removed and a fully directed formulation used with MTZ on all directed arcs.

No explicit inflow (in-degree) constraints are stated. Although they are logically implied by the symmetry constraints combined with the outflow constraints, their absence reduces clarity and makes the formulation fragile if the symmetry constraints are later removed.
The original problem requests solving with COPTPY, but the candidate provides only the mathematical formulation without any solver code, variable creation, or solution extraction logic.

d = {
    (1,2): 86, (1,3): 49, (1,4): 57, (1,5): 31, (1,6): 69, (1,7): 50,
    (2,1): 86, (2,3): 68, (2,4): 79, (2,5): 93, (2,6): 24, (2,7): 5,
    (3,1): 49, (3,2): 68, (3,4): 16, (3,5): 7,  (3,6): 72, (3,7): 67,
    (4,1): 57, (4,2): 79, (4,3): 16, (4,5): 90, (4,6): 69, (4,7): 1,
    (5,1): 31, (5,2): 93, (5,3): 7,  (5,4): 90, (5,6): 86, (5,7): 59,
    (6,1): 69, (6,2): 24, (6,3): 72, (6,4): 69, (6,5): 86, (6,7): 81,
    (7,1): 50, (7,2): 5,  (7,3): 67, (7,4): 1,  (7,5): 59, (7,6): 81,
}

n = 7
nodes = list(range(1, n + 1))
sub_nodes = list(range(2, n + 1))  # nodes 2..7 for MTZ

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Binary edge variables x[i,j]
x = {}
for i in nodes:
    for j in nodes:
        if i != j:
            x[i, j] = m.addVar(vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1, name=f"x_{i}_{j}")

# Continuous MTZ variables u[i] for i in 2..7
u = {}
for i in sub_nodes:
    u[i] = m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=1, ub=n - 1, name=f"u_{i}")

# Objective: minimize total distance
obj_terms = [d[i, j] * x[i, j] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j]
m.setObjective(quicksum(obj_terms), "minimize")

# Inflow constraints: each node has exactly one incoming edge
for i in nodes:
    inflow = quicksum(x[j, i] for j in nodes if j != i)
    m.addCons(inflow == 1, name=f"inflow_{i}")

# Outflow constraints: each node has exactly one outgoing edge
for i in nodes:
    outflow = quicksum(x[i, j] for j in nodes if j != i)
    m.addCons(outflow == 1, name=f"outflow_{i}")

# MTZ subtour elimination constraints
for i in sub_nodes:
    for j in sub_nodes:
        if i != j:
            m.addCons(u[i] - u[j] + n * x[j, i] <= n - 1, name=f"mtz_{i}_{j}")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
f = {"A": 1000, "B": 920, "C": 800, "D": 700}
c = {"A": 20, "B": 24, "C": 16, "D": 28}
cap = {"A": 900, "B": 1000, "C": 1200, "D": 1600}
demand = 2000
devices = ["A", "B", "C", "D"]

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
x = {}
y = {}
for d in devices:
    x[d] = m.addVar(name=f"x_{d}", lb=0, ub=cap[d], vtype="C")
    y[d] = m.addVar(name=f"y_{d}", lb=0, ub=1, vtype="B")

# Objective: minimize total cost
obj = quicksum(f[d] * y[d] for d in devices) + quicksum(c[d] * x[d] for d in devices)
m.setObjective(obj, "minimize")

# Demand satisfaction
m.addCons(quicksum(x[d] for d in devices) == demand, name="demand_satisfaction")

# Capacity linking constraints
for d in devices:
    m.addCons(x[d] <= cap[d] * y[d], name=f"capacity_{d}")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")
    for d in devices:
        print(f"  x_{d} = {m.getVal(x[d])}, y_{d} = {m.getVal(y[d])}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
f = {"A": 1000, "B": 920, "C": 800, "D": 700}
c = {"A": 20, "B": 24, "C": 16, "D": 28}
cap = {"A": 900, "B": 1000, "C": 1200, "D": 1600}
demand = 2000
devices = ["A", "B", "C", "D"]

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
x = {}
y = {}
for d in devices:
    x[d] = m.addVar(name=f"x_{d}", lb=0, ub=cap[d], vtype="C")
    y[d] = m.addVar(name=f"y_{d}", lb=0, ub=1, vtype="B")

# Objective: minimize total cost
obj = quicksum(f[d] * y[d] for d in devices) + quicksum(c[d] * x[d] for d in devices)
m.setObjective(obj, "minimize")

# Demand satisfaction
m.addCons(quicksum(x[d] for d in devices) == demand, name="demand_satisfaction")

# Capacity linking constraints
for d in devices:
    m.addCons(x[d] <= cap[d] * y[d], name=f"capacity_{d}")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")
    for d in devices:
        print(f"  x_{d} = {m.getVal(x[d])}, y_{d} = {m.getVal(y[d])}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
f = {"A": 1000, "B": 920, "C": 800, "D": 700}
c = {"A": 20, "B": 24, "C": 16, "D": 28}
cap = {"A": 900, "B": 1000, "C": 1200, "D": 1600}
demand = 2000
devices = ["A", "B", "C", "D"]

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
x = {}
y = {}
for d in devices:
    x[d] = m.addVar(name=f"x_{d}", lb=0, ub=cap[d], vtype="C")
    y[d] = m.addVar(name=f"y_{d}", lb=0, ub=1, vtype="B")

# Objective: minimize total cost
obj = quicksum(f[d] * y[d] for d in devices) + quicksum(c[d] * x[d] for d in devices)
m.setObjective(obj, "minimize")

# Demand satisfaction
m.addCons(quicksum(x[d] for d in devices) == demand, name="demand_satisfaction")

# Capacity linking constraints
for d in devices:
    m.addCons(x[d] <= cap[d] * y[d], name=f"capacity_{d}")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")
    for d in devices:
        print(f"  x_{d} = {m.getVal(x[d])}, y_{d} = {m.getVal(y[d])}")

When business variables exist under different solver names, bind names instead of rewriting the model. Preserve the objective and constraints. Positive evidence: IDs 4, 8 and 25 passed independent audit after rebinding with unchanged objectives. Counterexample: ID 48 lacks total production roles, so name-only rebinding is insufficient; add missing roles instead.
Source: work/industryor_semantic_dag_dev_v0.2

[indicator_bidirectional_v1]
A binary indicator must be consistent with positive quantity in both directions: indicator <= quantity and quantity <= independent_upper_bound * indicator. Do not invent the upper bound. Positive evidence: IDs 9, 19, 20 and 21 recovered after scoped repair. Counterexample: indicator repair alone cannot fix a wrong business objective.
Source: work/industryor_semantic_dag_dev_v0.2

[objective_consistency_v1]
Recompute the business objective from semantic variables and check its direction. Goal-programming deviations are not business profit. ID 48 had feasible variables and an independent business optimum but a mismatched reported objective, and must remain rejected. Never inject a target value.

revenue_C = 30000
revenue_D = 50000

cost_B = 2.5
cost_C = 1.8
cost_D = 3.0

budget = 6.0

# Model
m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables (binary)
x_A = m.addVar("x_A", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
x_B = m.addVar("x_B", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
x_C = m.addVar("x_C", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
x_D = m.addVar("x_D", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)

# Objective: maximize annual income
obj = revenue_A * x_A + revenue_B * x_B + revenue_C * x_C + revenue_D * x_D
m.setObjective(obj, "maximize")

# Budget constraint: 1.6*x_A + 2.5*x_B + 1.8*x_C + 3*x_D <= 6
m.addCons(cost_A * x_A + cost_B * x_B + cost_C * x_C + cost_D * x_D <= budget, "budget_constraint")

# Mutual exclusion: if D then not A => x_A + x_D <= 1
m.addCons(x_A + x_D <= 1, "mutual_exclusion_AD")

# Solve
m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
revenue_A = 15000
revenue_B = 40000
revenue_C = 30000
revenue_D = 50000

cost_A = 1.6
cost_B = 2.5
cost_C = 1.8
cost_D = 3.0

budget = 6.0

# Model
m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables (binary)
x_A = m.addVar("x_A", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
x_B = m.addVar("x_B", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
x_C = m.addVar("x_C", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
x_D = m.addVar("x_D", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)

# Objective: maximize annual income
obj = revenue_A * x_A + revenue_B * x_B + revenue_C * x_C + revenue_D * x_D
m.setObjective(obj, "maximize")

# Budget constraint: 1.6*x_A + 2.5*x_B + 1.8*x_C + 3*x_D <= 6
m.addCons(cost_A * x_A + cost_B * x_B + cost_C * x_C + cost_D * x_D <= budget, "budget_constraint")

# Mutual exclusion: if D then not A => x_A + x_D <= 1
m.addCons(x_A + x_D <= 1, "mutual_exclusion_AD")

# Solve
m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

import json

# Data

horse_pollution = 80
bicycle_pollution = 0
handcart_pollution = 0
pollution_limit = 1000
min_horse_trips = 8
horse_capacity = 55
bicycle_capacity = 30
handcart_capacity = 40
M_b = 19
M_c = 14

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
h = m.addVar("h", vtype="I", lb=8, ub=12)
b = m.addVar("b", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=M_b)
c = m.addVar("c", vtype="I", lb=0, ub=M_c)
y_b = m.addVar("y_b", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
y_c = m.addVar("y_c", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)

# Objective: minimize pollution
m.setObjective(horse_pollution * h, "minimize")

# Constraints
m.addCons(h >= min_horse_trips, "min_horse_trips")
m.addCons(horse_pollution * h <= pollution_limit, "pollution_limit")
m.addCons(horse_capacity * h + bicycle_capacity * b + handcart_capacity * c >= total_produce, "produce_requirement")
m.addCons(y_b + y_c == 1, "exactly_one_non_horse_method")
m.addCons(b <= M_b * y_b, "bicycle_linking")
m.addCons(c <= M_c * y_c, "handcart_linking")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
candidates = ['F', 'G', 'H', 'I', 'J']
salary = {'F': 12000, 'G': 15000, 'H': 18000, 'I': 5000, 'J': 10000}
skill = {'F': 2, 'G': 3, 'H': 4, 'I': 1, 'J': 2}
pm_exp = {'F': 1, 'G': 2, 'H': 2, 'I': 5, 'J': 4}
budget = 40000
max_employees = 4
min_skill = 8
min_pm = 8

# Model
m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables (binary)
x = {}
for c in candidates:
    x[c] = m.addVar(name=f"x_{c}", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)

# Objective: minimize total salary
m.setObjective(quicksum(salary[c] * x[c] for c in candidates), "minimize")

# Budget constraint
m.addCons(quicksum(salary[c] * x[c] for c in candidates) <= budget, name="budget_constraint")

# Max employees constraint
m.addCons(quicksum(x[c] for c in candidates) <= max_employees, name="max_employees_constraint")

# Minimum skill level constraint
m.addCons(quicksum(skill[c] * x[c] for c in candidates) >= min_skill, name="skill_constraint")

# Minimum PM experience constraint
m.addCons(quicksum(pm_exp[c] * x[c] for c in candidates) >= min_pm, name="pm_experience_constraint")

# Mutual exclusion: at most one of G and J
m.addCons(x['G'] + x['J'] <= 1, name="mutual_exclusion_GJ")

# Solve
m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")
    for c in candidates:
        print(f"  {c}: {m.getVal(x[c])}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
candidates = ['F', 'G', 'H', 'I', 'J']
salary = {'F': 12000, 'G': 15000, 'H': 18000, 'I': 5000, 'J': 10000}
skill = {'F': 2, 'G': 3, 'H': 4, 'I': 1, 'J': 2}
pm_exp = {'F': 1, 'G': 2, 'H': 2, 'I': 5, 'J': 4}
budget = 40000
max_employees = 4
min_skill = 8
min_pm = 8

# Model
m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables (binary)
x = {}
for c in candidates:
    x[c] = m.addVar(name=f"x_{c}", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)

# Objective: minimize total salary
m.setObjective(quicksum(salary[c] * x[c] for c in candidates), "minimize")

# Budget constraint
m.addCons(quicksum(salary[c] * x[c] for c in candidates) <= budget, name="budget_constraint")

# Max employees constraint
m.addCons(quicksum(x[c] for c in candidates) <= max_employees, name="max_employees_constraint")

# Minimum skill level constraint
m.addCons(quicksum(skill[c] * x[c] for c in candidates) >= min_skill, name="skill_constraint")

# Minimum PM experience constraint
m.addCons(quicksum(pm_exp[c] * x[c] for c in candidates) >= min_pm, name="pm_experience_constraint")

# Mutual exclusion: at most one of G and J
m.addCons(x['G'] + x['J'] <= 1, name="mutual_exclusion_GJ")

# Solve
m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")
    for c in candidates:
        print(f"  {c}: {m.getVal(x[c])}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
candidates = ['F', 'G', 'H', 'I', 'J']
salary = {'F': 12000, 'G': 15000, 'H': 18000, 'I': 5000, 'J': 10000}
skill = {'F': 2, 'G': 3, 'H': 4, 'I': 1, 'J': 2}
pm_exp = {'F': 1, 'G': 2, 'H': 2, 'I': 5, 'J': 4}
budget = 40000
max_employees = 4
min_skill = 8
min_pm = 8

# Model
m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables (binary)
x = {}
for c in candidates:
    x[c] = m.addVar(name=f"x_{c}", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)

# Objective: minimize total salary
m.setObjective(quicksum(salary[c] * x[c] for c in candidates), "minimize")

# Budget constraint
m.addCons(quicksum(salary[c] * x[c] for c in candidates) <= budget, name="budget_constraint")

# Max employees constraint
m.addCons(quicksum(x[c] for c in candidates) <= max_employees, name="max_employees_constraint")

# Minimum skill level constraint
m.addCons(quicksum(skill[c] * x[c] for c in candidates) >= min_skill, name="skill_constraint")

# Minimum PM experience constraint
m.addCons(quicksum(pm_exp[c] * x[c] for c in candidates) >= min_pm, name="pm_experience_constraint")

# Mutual exclusion: at most one of G and J
m.addCons(x['G'] + x['J'] <= 1, name="mutual_exclusion_GJ")

# Solve
m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")
    for c in candidates:
        print(f"  {c}: {m.getVal(x[c])}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data transcribed from problem
a1_A = 2
a2_A = 1
a1_B = 1
a2_B = 3
c1 = 30
c2 = 50
T_A = 250
T_B = 150
r_A = 80
r_B = 20
C_max = 5500
d1_min = 80
d2_min = 50
OT_max = 20

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
x1 = m.addVar("x1", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C")
x2 = m.addVar("x2", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C")

# Objective: minimize total cost
obj = r_A * (a1_A * x1 + a2_A * x2) + r_B * (a1_B * x1 + a2_B * x2) + c1 * x1 + c2 * x2
m.setObjective(obj, "minimize")

# Constraint 1: Inspection and sales costs
m.addCons(c1 * x1 + c2 * x2 <= C_max, name="inspection_sales_cost")

# Constraint 2: At least 80 microwave ovens
m.addCons(x1 >= d1_min, name="min_microwave")

# Constraint 3: Workshop A fully utilized
m.addCons(a1_A * x1 + a2_A * x2 >= T_A, name="workshop_A_full")

# Constraint 4: Workshop B fully utilized
m.addCons(a1_B * x1 + a2_B * x2 >= T_B, name="workshop_B_full")

# Constraint 5: Overtime in workshop A
m.addCons(a1_A * x1 + a2_A * x2 <= T_A + OT_max, name="overtime_A")

# Constraint 6: At least 50 water heaters
m.addCons(x2 >= d2_min, name="min_water_heater")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")
    print(f"x1 (microwave ovens): {m.getVal(x1)}")
    print(f"x2 (water heaters): {m.getVal(x2)}")

m.setObjective(obj, "minimize")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
d_I = [30000, 30000, 30000, 100000, 100000, 100000]
d_II = [15000, 15000, 15000, 50000, 50000, 50000]
c_I = 4.5
c_II = 7
cap = 120000
v_I = 0.2
v_II = 0.4
W = 15000
h_own = 1
h_ext = 1.5
I_I_0 = 0
I_II_0 = 0

T = 6  # months: Jul(1) to Dec(6)

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
x_I = [m.addVar(v=f"x_I_{t}", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
x_II = [m.addVar(v=f"x_II_{t}", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
I_I = [m.addVar(v=f"I_I_{t}", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
I_II = [m.addVar(v=f"I_II_{t}", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
E = [m.addVar(v=f"E_{t}", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C") for t in range(T)]

# Objective: minimize total production + inventory + external warehouse cost
obj = (c_I * quicksum(x_I) + c_II * quicksum(x_II)
       + v_I * h_own * quicksum(I_I) + v_II * h_own * quicksum(I_II)
       + (h_ext - h_own) * quicksum(E))
m.setObjective(obj, "minimize")

# Inventory balance constraints for Product I
m.addCons(I_I[0] - x_I[0] == -d_I[0], "inv_I_1")
for t in range(1, T):
    m.addCons(I_I[t] - I_I[t-1] - x_I[t] == -d_I[t], f"inv_I_{t+1}")

# Inventory balance constraints for Product II
m.addCons(I_II[0] - x_II[0] == -d_II[0], "inv_II_1")
for t in range(1, T):
    m.addCons(I_II[t] - I_II[t-1] - x_II[t] == -d_II[t], f"inv_II_{t+1}")

# Production capacity constraints
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(x_I[t] + x_II[t] <= cap, f"cap_{t+1}")

The storage cost in the objective is decomposed as (volume × 1) + (E × 0.5), which is algebraically correct (base rate for all volume plus the 0.5 surcharge for external portion), but this linearization is not documented or justified in the formulation, making it harder for a reviewer to verify correctness without re-deriving it.

The external warehouse constraint E(t) - 0.2·I_I(t) - 0.4·I_II(t) ≥ -15000 is correct but written in a non-standard form; an equivalent and more transparent form would be 0.2·I_I(t) + 0.4·I_II(t) - E(t) ≤ 15000, making the 'own warehouse volume ≤ capacity' interpretation immediately visible.

No terminal inventory constraint (e.g., I_I(6) = 0 or I_II(6) = 0) is included. While the problem does not explicitly require zero ending inventory, the absence of any such condition or discussion leaves the model open to accumulating unwanted end-of-horizon stock, which may not reflect practical intent.

The formulation implicitly assumes no backordering (I(t) ≥ 0 for all t). This is a reasonable interpretation of 'meeting market demand,' but it is not explicitly stated or justified, and a later formulation should make this assumption clear or add a note.

weak_points: Storage cost is charged on end-of-month inventory (I(t)); the problem's 'per cubic meter per month' cost could more naturally apply to the inventory held during the month (beginning-of-month or average), making the timing assumption implicit and potentially off by one period.

The external warehouse variable E(t) is not explicitly pinned to the overflow amount; the formulation relies on the positive objective coefficient to drive E(t) to max(0, volume-15000) at optimality rather than enforcing it structurally, which is less robust and harder to verify.

No terminal inventory constraint (I_I(6)=0, I_II(6)=0) is imposed; while the optimizer will tend to minimize leftover stock, the problem's demand-satisfaction requirement does not strictly force zero ending inventory, leaving a small degree of freedom that could be tightened.

Production costs are stored as single scalar parameters (c_I=4.5, c_II=7) rather than per-month arrays; although correct for the Jul–Dec window where costs are constant, this reduces clarity and extensibility if the planning horizon were to include the Jan–May period with different costs.

Demand satisfaction is only implicit through the inventory-balance equalities combined with non-negativity bounds on I(t); an explicit per-period demand-coverage constraint (x(t)+I(t-1) >= d(t)) would make the requirement more transparent and easier to audit.

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
d_I = [30000, 30000, 30000, 100000, 100000, 100000]
d_II = [15000, 15000, 15000, 50000, 50000, 50000]
c_I = 4.5
c_II = 7
cap = 120000
v_I = 0.2
v_II = 0.4
W = 15000
h_own = 1
h_ext = 1.5
I_I_0 = 0
I_II_0 = 0

T = 6  # months: Jul(1) to Dec(6)

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
x_I = [m.addVar(v=f"x_I_{t}", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
x_II = [m.addVar(v=f"x_II_{t}", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
I_I = [m.addVar(v=f"I_I_{t}", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
I_II = [m.addVar(v=f"I_II_{t}", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
E = [m.addVar(v=f"E_{t}", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C") for t in range(T)]

# Objective: minimize total production + inventory + external warehouse cost
obj = (c_I * quicksum(x_I) + c_II * quicksum(x_II)
       + v_I * h_own * quicksum(I_I) + v_II * h_own * quicksum(I_II)
       + (h_ext - h_own) * quicksum(E))
m.setObjective(obj, "minimize")

# Inventory balance constraints for Product I
m.addCons(I_I[0] - x_I[0] == -d_I[0], "inv_I_1")
for t in range(1, T):
    m.addCons(I_I[t] - I_I[t-1] - x_I[t] == -d_I[t], f"inv_I_{t+1}")

# Inventory balance constraints for Product II
m.addCons(I_II[0] - x_II[0] == -d_II[0], "inv_II_1")
for t in range(1, T):
    m.addCons(I_II[t] - I_II[t-1] - x_II[t] == -d_II[t], f"inv_II_{t+1}")

# Production capacity constraints
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(x_I[t] + x_II[t] <= cap, f"cap_{t+1}")

# External warehouse constraints: E(t) >= v_I*I_I(t) + v_II*I_II(t) - W
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(E[t] - v_I * I_I[t] - v_II * I_II[t] >= -W, f"ext_{t+1}")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

weak_points: Inventory variables I_I(t) and I_II(t) are not explicitly labeled as end-of-month inventory in their descriptions, which could cause ambiguity in interpretation of the storage cost timing.

The storage cost in the objective is decomposed as (volume × 1) + (E × 0.5), which is algebraically correct (base rate for all volume plus the 0.5 surcharge for external portion), but this linearization is not documented or justified in the formulation, making it harder for a reviewer to verify correctness without re-deriving it.

The external warehouse constraint E(t) - 0.2·I_I(t) - 0.4·I_II(t) ≥ -15000 is correct but written in a non-standard form; an equivalent and more transparent form would be 0.2·I_I(t) + 0.4·I_II(t) - E(t) ≤ 15000, making the 'own warehouse volume ≤ capacity' interpretation immediately visible.

No terminal inventory constraint (e.g., I_I(6) = 0 or I_II(6) = 0) is included. While the problem does not explicitly require zero ending inventory, the absence of any such condition or discussion leaves the model open to accumulating unwanted end-of-horizon stock, which may not reflect practical intent.

The formulation implicitly assumes no backordering (I(t) ≥ 0 for all t). This is a reasonable interpretation of 'meeting market demand,' but it is not explicitly stated or justified, and a later formulation should make this assumption clear or add a note.

The external warehouse variable E(t) is only implicitly bounded above by the warehouse inequality (E(t) >= volume - 15000) and the non-negativity bound; there is no explicit constraint E(t) <= 0.2*I_I(t) + 0.4*I_II(t) to prevent E(t) from exceeding total stored volume, relying entirely on the objective to drive it to the minimum at optimum.

The storage-cost linearization (1 * total_volume + 0.5 * E(t)) correctly decomposes the piecewise cost (1 yuan/m³ for factory, 1.5 yuan/m³ for external), but the formulation does not explicitly state or document that E(t) represents the excess volume beyond the 15,000 m³ factory capacity, making the economic interpretation less transparent to a reader.

No explicit constraint or note addresses whether end-of-horizon inventory (I_I(6), I_II(6)) should be zero or is free; the problem does not specify a terminal inventory requirement, but the formulation silently allows positive ending inventory, which may or may not be intended.

weak_points: Storage cost is charged on end-of-month inventory (I(t)); the problem's 'per cubic meter per month' cost could more naturally apply to the inventory held during the month (beginning-of-month or average), making the timing assumption implicit and potentially off by one period.

The external warehouse variable E(t) is not explicitly pinned to the overflow amount; the formulation relies on the positive objective coefficient to drive E(t) to max(0, volume-15000) at optimality rather than enforcing it structurally, which is less robust and harder to verify.

No terminal inventory constraint (I_I(6)=0, I_II(6)=0) is imposed; while the optimizer will tend to minimize leftover stock, the problem's demand-satisfaction requirement does not strictly force zero ending inventory, leaving a small degree of freedom that could be tightened.

Production costs are stored as single scalar parameters (c_I=4.5, c_II=7) rather than per-month arrays; although correct for the Jul–Dec window where costs are constant, this reduces clarity and extensibility if the planning horizon were to include the Jan–May period with different costs.

Demand satisfaction is only implicit through the inventory-balance equalities combined with non-negativity bounds on I(t); an explicit per-period demand-coverage constraint (x(t)+I(t-1) >= d(t)) would make the requirement more transparent and easier to audit.

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
d_I = [30000, 30000, 30000, 100000, 100000, 100000]
d_II = [15000, 15000, 15000, 50000, 50000, 50000]
c_I = 4.5
c_II = 7
cap = 120000
v_I = 0.2
v_II = 0.4
W = 15000
h_own = 1
h_ext = 1.5
I_I_0 = 0
I_II_0 = 0

T = 6  # months: Jul(1) to Dec(6)

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
x_I = [m.addVar(v=f"x_I_{t}", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
x_II = [m.addVar(v=f"x_II_{t}", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
I_I = [m.addVar(v=f"I_I_{t}", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
I_II = [m.addVar(v=f"I_II_{t}", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
E = [m.addVar(v=f"E_{t}", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C") for t in range(T)]

# Objective: minimize total production + inventory + external warehouse cost
obj = (c_I * quicksum(x_I) + c_II * quicksum(x_II)
       + v_I * h_own * quicksum(I_I) + v_II * h_own * quicksum(I_II)
       + (h_ext - h_own) * quicksum(E))
m.setObjective(obj, "minimize")

# Inventory balance constraints for Product I
m.addCons(I_I[0] - x_I[0] == -d_I[0], "inv_I_1")
for t in range(1, T):
    m.addCons(I_I[t] - I_I[t-1] - x_I[t] == -d_I[t], f"inv_I_{t+1}")

# Inventory balance constraints for Product II
m.addCons(I_II[0] - x_II[0] == -d_II[0], "inv_II_1")
for t in range(1, T):
    m.addCons(I_II[t] - I_II[t-1] - x_II[t] == -d_II[t], f"inv_II_{t+1}")

# Production capacity constraints
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(x_I[t] + x_II[t] <= cap, f"cap_{t+1}")

# External warehouse constraints: E(t) >= v_I*I_I(t) + v_II*I_II(t) - W
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(E[t] - v_I * I_I[t] - v_II * I_II[t] >= -W, f"ext_{t+1}")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

weak_points: Inventory variables I_I(t) and I_II(t) are not explicitly labeled as end-of-month inventory in their descriptions, which could cause ambiguity in interpretation of the storage cost timing.

The storage cost in the objective is decomposed as (volume × 1) + (E × 0.5), which is algebraically correct (base rate for all volume plus the 0.5 surcharge for external portion), but this linearization is not documented or justified in the formulation, making it harder for a reviewer to verify correctness without re-deriving it.

The external warehouse constraint E(t) - 0.2·I_I(t) - 0.4·I_II(t) ≥ -15000 is correct but written in a non-standard form; an equivalent and more transparent form would be 0.2·I_I(t) + 0.4·I_II(t) - E(t) ≤ 15000, making the 'own warehouse volume ≤ capacity' interpretation immediately visible.

No terminal inventory constraint (e.g., I_I(6) = 0 or I_II(6) = 0) is included. While the problem does not explicitly require zero ending inventory, the absence of any such condition or discussion leaves the model open to accumulating unwanted end-of-horizon stock, which may not reflect practical intent.

The formulation implicitly assumes no backordering (I(t) ≥ 0 for all t). This is a reasonable interpretation of 'meeting market demand,' but it is not explicitly stated or justified, and a later formulation should make this assumption clear or add a note.

weak_points: The 'no_backorder_I' and 'no_backorder_II' constraints (I_I(t) >= 0, I_II(t) >= 0) are redundant because all inventory variables already have a lower bound of 0 in their variable definitions; this adds unnecessary clutter without changing the feasible region.

The external warehouse variable E(t) is only implicitly bounded above by the warehouse inequality (E(t) >= volume - 15000) and the non-negativity bound; there is no explicit constraint E(t) <= 0.2*I_I(t) + 0.4*I_II(t) to prevent E(t) from exceeding total stored volume, relying entirely on the objective to drive it to the minimum at optimum.

The storage-cost linearization (1 * total_volume + 0.5 * E(t)) correctly decomposes the piecewise cost (1 yuan/m³ for factory, 1.5 yuan/m³ for external), but the formulation does not explicitly state or document that E(t) represents the excess volume beyond the 15,000 m³ factory capacity, making the economic interpretation less transparent to a reader.

No explicit constraint or note addresses whether end-of-horizon inventory (I_I(6), I_II(6)) should be zero or is free; the problem does not specify a terminal inventory requirement, but the formulation silently allows positive ending inventory, which may or may not be intended.

weak_points: Storage cost is charged on end-of-month inventory (I(t)); the problem's 'per cubic meter per month' cost could more naturally apply to the inventory held during the month (beginning-of-month or average), making the timing assumption implicit and potentially off by one period.

The external warehouse variable E(t) is not explicitly pinned to the overflow amount; the formulation relies on the positive objective coefficient to drive E(t) to max(0, volume-15000) at optimality rather than enforcing it structurally, which is less robust and harder to verify.

No terminal inventory constraint (I_I(6)=0, I_II(6)=0) is imposed; while the optimizer will tend to minimize leftover stock, the problem's demand-satisfaction requirement does not strictly force zero ending inventory, leaving a small degree of freedom that could be tightened.

Production costs are stored as single scalar parameters (c_I=4.5, c_II=7) rather than per-month arrays; although correct for the Jul–Dec window where costs are constant, this reduces clarity and extensibility if the planning horizon were to include the Jan–May period with different costs.

Demand satisfaction is only implicit through the inventory-balance equalities combined with non-negativity bounds on I(t); an explicit per-period demand-coverage constraint (x(t)+I(t-1) >= d(t)) would make the requirement more transparent and easier to audit.

weak_points: Inventory variables I_I(t) and I_II(t) are not explicitly labeled as end-of-month inventory in their descriptions, which could cause ambiguity in interpretation of the storage cost timing.

The storage cost in the objective is decomposed as (volume × 1) + (E × 0.5), which is algebraically correct (base rate for all volume plus the 0.5 surcharge for external portion), but this linearization is not documented or justified in the formulation, making it harder for a reviewer to verify correctness without re-deriving it.

The external warehouse constraint E(t) - 0.2·I_I(t) - 0.4·I_II(t) ≥ -15000 is correct but written in a non-standard form; an equivalent and more transparent form would be 0.2·I_I(t) + 0.4·I_II(t) - E(t) ≤ 15000, making the 'own warehouse volume ≤ capacity' interpretation immediately visible.

No terminal inventory constraint (e.g., I_I(6) = 0 or I_II(6) = 0) is included. While the problem does not explicitly require zero ending inventory, the absence of any such condition or discussion leaves the model open to accumulating unwanted end-of-horizon stock, which may not reflect practical intent.

The formulation implicitly assumes no backordering (I(t) ≥ 0 for all t). This is a reasonable interpretation of 'meeting market demand,' but it is not explicitly stated or justified, and a later formulation should make this assumption clear or add a note.

weak_points: The 'no_backorder_I' and 'no_backorder_II' constraints (I_I(t) >= 0, I_II(t) >= 0) are redundant because all inventory variables already have a lower bound of 0 in their variable definitions; this adds unnecessary clutter without changing the feasible region.

The external warehouse variable E(t) is only implicitly bounded above by the warehouse inequality (E(t) >= volume - 15000) and the non-negativity bound; there is no explicit constraint E(t) <= 0.2*I_I(t) + 0.4*I_II(t) to prevent E(t) from exceeding total stored volume, relying entirely on the objective to drive it to the minimum at optimum.

The storage-cost linearization (1 * total_volume + 0.5 * E(t)) correctly decomposes the piecewise cost (1 yuan/m³ for factory, 1.5 yuan/m³ for external), but the formulation does not explicitly state or document that E(t) represents the excess volume beyond the 15,000 m³ factory capacity, making the economic interpretation less transparent to a reader.

No explicit constraint or note addresses whether end-of-horizon inventory (I_I(6), I_II(6)) should be zero or is free; the problem does not specify a terminal inventory requirement, but the formulation silently allows positive ending inventory, which may or may not be intended.

weak_points: Storage cost is charged on end-of-month inventory (I(t)); the problem's 'per cubic meter per month' cost could more naturally apply to the inventory held during the month (beginning-of-month or average), making the timing assumption implicit and potentially off by one period.

The external warehouse variable E(t) is not explicitly pinned to the overflow amount; the formulation relies on the positive objective coefficient to drive E(t) to max(0, volume-15000) at optimality rather than enforcing it structurally, which is less robust and harder to verify.

No terminal inventory constraint (I_I(6)=0, I_II(6)=0) is imposed; while the optimizer will tend to minimize leftover stock, the problem's demand-satisfaction requirement does not strictly force zero ending inventory, leaving a small degree of freedom that could be tightened.

Production costs are stored as single scalar parameters (c_I=4.5, c_II=7) rather than per-month arrays; although correct for the Jul–Dec window where costs are constant, this reduces clarity and extensibility if the planning horizon were to include the Jan–May period with different costs.

Demand satisfaction is only implicit through the inventory-balance equalities combined with non-negativity bounds on I(t); an explicit per-period demand-coverage constraint (x(t)+I(t-1) >= d(t)) would make the requirement more transparent and easier to audit.

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
d_I = [30000, 30000, 30000, 100000, 100000, 100000]
d_II = [15000, 15000, 15000, 50000, 50000, 50000]
c_I = 4.5
c_II = 7
cap = 120000
v_I = 0.2
v_II = 0.4
W = 15000
h_own = 1
h_ext = 1.5
I_I_0 = 0
I_II_0 = 0

T = 6  # months: Jul(1) to Dec(6)

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
x_I = [m.addVar(v=f"x_I_{t}", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
x_II = [m.addVar(v=f"x_II_{t}", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
I_I = [m.addVar(v=f"I_I_{t}", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
I_II = [m.addVar(v=f"I_II_{t}", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C") for t in range(T)]
E = [m.addVar(v=f"E_{t}", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C") for t in range(T)]

# Objective: minimize total production + inventory + external warehouse cost
obj = (c_I * quicksum(x_I) + c_II * quicksum(x_II)
       + v_I * h_own * quicksum(I_I) + v_II * h_own * quicksum(I_II)
       + (h_ext - h_own) * quicksum(E))
m.setObjective(obj, "minimize")

# Inventory balance constraints for Product I
m.addCons(I_I[0] - x_I[0] == -d_I[0], "inv_I_1")
for t in range(1, T):
    m.addCons(I_I[t] - I_I[t-1] - x_I[t] == -d_I[t], f"inv_I_{t+1}")

# Inventory balance constraints for Product II
m.addCons(I_II[0] - x_II[0] == -d_II[0], "inv_II_1")
for t in range(1, T):
    m.addCons(I_II[t] - I_II[t-1] - x_II[t] == -d_II[t], f"inv_II_{t+1}")

# Production capacity constraints
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(x_I[t] + x_II[t] <= cap, f"cap_{t+1}")

# External warehouse constraints: E(t) >= v_I*I_I(t) + v_II*I_II(t) - W
for t in range(T):
    m.addCons(E[t] - v_I * I_I[t] - v_II * I_II[t] >= -W, f"ext_{t+1}")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

import json

# Data
supply_A_min = 80
supply_B_min = 100
demand = [55, 75, 50]
dist_A = [10, 5, 6]
dist_B = [4, 8, 15]

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

x_A = [m.addVar(f"x_A{i+1}", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=m.infinity()) for i in range(3)]
x_B = [m.addVar(f"x_B{i+1}", vtype="C", lb=0, ub=m.infinity()) for i in range(3)]

obj = quicksum(dist_A[i] * x_A[i] + dist_B[i] * x_B[i] for i in range(3))

m.addCons(quicksum(x_B[i] for i in range(3)) >= supply_B_min, name="supply_B")

# Demand constraints (=)
for i in range(3):
    m.addCons(x_A[i] + x_B[i] == demand[i], name=f"demand_area{i+1}")

m.optimize()

obj = quicksum(dist_A[j] * x[0, j] for j in range(3)) + quicksum(dist_B[j] * x[1, j] for j in range(3))

m.addCons(quicksum(x[0, j] for j in range(3)) >= supply_A_min, name="supply_A_lower_bound")
m.addCons(quicksum(x[1, j] for j in range(3)) >= supply_B_min, name="supply_B_lower_bound")

# Demand constraints (equalities)
for j in range(3):
    m.addCons(x[0, j] + x[1, j] == demand[j], name=f"demand_area{j+1}")

    (2, 1, 0),  # x2
    (2, 0, 4),  # x3
    (1, 1, 3),  # x4

    (0, 2, 2),  # x6
    (0, 1, 6),  # x7

m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables (continuous, >= 0)
x = []
for i in range(len(patterns)):
    x.append(m.addVar(name=f"x{i+1}", lb=0.0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C"))

# Objective: minimize total waste
obj = quicksum(patterns[i][2] * x[i] for i in range(len(patterns)))
m.setObjective(obj, "minimize")

# Constraint: demand for 3m pieces

    quicksum(patterns[i][0] * x[i] for i in range(len(patterns))) >= d3,
    name="demand_3m"
)

# Constraint: demand for 4m pieces
m.addCons(
    quicksum(patterns[i][1] * x[i] for i in range(len(patterns))) >= d4,
    name="demand_4m"
)

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

Source attributions for the binary x_ij variables are generic ('formulate an integer programming model for this problem') rather than referencing the specific modeling decision (e.g., 'x_ij = 1 if the salesman travels directly from city i to city j').

The distance matrix is asymmetric (e.g., d_14=12 vs d_41=15), and while the formulation correctly captures this, no explicit note is made that the problem is an asymmetric TSP (ATSP), which is a relevant modeling distinction.

weak_points: The MTZ subtour-elimination constraints for arcs going TO city 1 (mtz_21, mtz_31, mtz_41) are infeasible: with u_1=1 and u_j≥2 for j≠1, the constraint u_j - u_1 + 4*x_j1 ≤ 3 forces u_j ≤ 0 whenever x_j1=1, contradicting the lower bound u_j≥2. Combined with the inflow constraint x_21+x_31+x_41=1, the entire formulation has no feasible solution.

The correct MTZ formulation should apply the ordering constraint u_i - u_j + n*x_ij ≤ n-1 only for arcs between non-depot cities (i,j ∈ {2,…,n}, i≠j). Arcs returning to the depot (city 1) must be excluded from the MTZ set; the return is already enforced by the flow-in constraint on city 1.
The three MTZ constraints for arcs FROM city 1 (mtz_12, mtz_13, mtz_14) are redundant given the variable bounds (u_1=1, u_j≥2) and add no tightening; they could be removed for a cleaner model.

Because the formulation is infeasible as written, it cannot produce any valid TSP tour, rendering the otherwise correct objective, flow constraints, and parameter set unusable until the three infeasible MTZ constraints are removed or reformulated.

Combined with the inflow constraint x_21+x_31+x_41=1, the entire formulation has no feasible solution.

The correct MTZ formulation should apply the ordering constraint u_i - u_j + n*x_ij ≤ n-1 only for arcs between non-depot cities (i,j ∈ {2,…,n}, i≠j). Arcs returning to the depot (city 1) must be excluded from the MTZ set; the return is already enforced by the flow-in constraint on city 1.
The three MTZ constraints for arcs FROM city 1 (mtz_12, mtz_13, mtz_14) are redundant given the variable bounds (u_1=1, u_j≥2) and add no tightening; they could be removed for a cleaner model.

Because the formulation is infeasible as written, it cannot produce any valid TSP tour, rendering the otherwise correct objective, flow constraints, and parameter set unusable until the three infeasible MTZ constraints are removed or reformulated.

weak_points: The u_i variables are declared as continuous rather than integer; while the MTZ constraints will force integer values in practice, declaring them as integer (or at least noting integrality) is the standard and tighter formulation.

u_1 is not fixed to a constant value (e.g., u_1 = 1). The standard MTZ formulation fixes the position of the depot/starting city to remove translation symmetry and tighten the LP relaxation; here all four u variables are free in [1,4].

The problem statement says the salesman 'visits two other cities to sell merchandise' which is ambiguous for a 4-city instance (the salesman actually visits three other cities). The formulation correctly models all 4 cities, but a later formulation could explicitly note this interpretation to avoid confusion.

Source attributions for the binary x_ij variables are generic ('formulate an integer programming model for this problem') rather than referencing the specific modeling decision (e.g., 'x_ij = 1 if the salesman travels directly from city i to city j').

The distance matrix is asymmetric (e.g., d_14=12 vs d_41=15), and while the formulation correctly captures this, no explicit note is made that the problem is an asymmetric TSP (ATSP), which is a relevant modeling distinction.

[export_rebinding_v1]
When business variables exist under different solver names, bind names instead of rewriting the model. Preserve the objective and constraints. Positive evidence: IDs 4, 8 and 25 passed independent audit after rebinding with unchanged objectives. Counterexample: ID 48 lacks total production roles, so name-only rebinding is insufficient; add missing roles instead.
Source: work/industryor_semantic_dag_dev_v0.2

[indicator_bidirectional_v1]
A binary indicator must be consistent with positive quantity in both directions: indicator <= quantity and quantity <= independent_upper_bound * indicator. Do not invent the upper bound. Positive evidence: IDs 9, 19, 20 and 21 recovered after scoped repair. Counterexample: indicator repair alone cannot fix a wrong business objective.
Source: work/industryor_semantic_dag_dev_v0.2

[objective_consistency_v1]
Recompute the business objective from semantic variables and check its direction. Goal-programming deviations are not business profit. ID 48 had feasible variables and an independent business optimum but a mismatched reported objective, and must remain rejected. Never inject a target value.
Source: work/industryor_semantic_dag_dev_v0.2/prob_048/branch_dag/regenerate/score.json

[regenerate_rebind_v1]
After regeneration, stale aliases can erase the export. Remove aliases whose solver names no longer exist, prefer verified canonical names, and rebind if needed. Rebinding completes evidence but does not prove business correctness. ID 48 demonstrates that objective semantics still need independent verification.
Source: work/industryor_semantic_dag_dev_v0.2/prob_048/branch_dag/regenerate/score.json

[dynamic_collection_binding_v1]
Dictionary comprehensions and simple loops may bind semantic names to expressions such as x['A']. Use only constant, code-verified index sets when repairing them. Do not guess nested or dynamic bindings. ID 19 supports this scoped mechanism; unsupported structures remain UNKNOWN.

Combined with the inflow constraint x_21+x_31+x_41=1, the entire formulation has no feasible solution.

The correct MTZ formulation should apply the ordering constraint u_i - u_j + n*x_ij ≤ n-1 only for arcs between non-depot cities (i,j ∈ {2,…,n}, i≠j). Arcs returning to the depot (city 1) must be excluded from the MTZ set; the return is already enforced by the flow-in constraint on city 1.
The three MTZ constraints for arcs FROM city 1 (mtz_12, mtz_13, mtz_14) are redundant given the variable bounds (u_1=1, u_j≥2) and add no tightening; they could be removed for a cleaner model.

Because the formulation is infeasible as written, it cannot produce any valid TSP tour, rendering the otherwise correct objective, flow constraints, and parameter set unusable until the three infeasible MTZ constraints are removed or reformulated.

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
d_11 = 10
d_12 = 20
d_21 = 30
d_22 = 40
c_11 = 5
c_12 = 8
c_21 = 6
c_22 = 7

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables: x_ij = 1 if factory i is assigned to location j
x_11 = m.addVar("x_11", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
x_12 = m.addVar("x_12", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
x_21 = m.addVar("x_21", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
x_22 = m.addVar("x_22", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)

# Objective: minimize total transportation cost
obj = (d_11 * c_11 * x_11 + d_11 * c_21 * x_12 +
       d_12 * c_12 * x_11 + d_12 * c_22 * x_12 +
       d_21 * c_11 * x_21 + d_21 * c_21 * x_22 +
       d_22 * c_12 * x_21 + d_22 * c_22 * x_22)
m.setObjective(obj, "minimize")

# Constraints: each factory assigned to exactly one location
m.addCons(x_11 + x_12 == 1, "assign_factory_1")
m.addCons(x_21 + x_22 == 1, "assign_factory_2")

# Constraints: each location assigned exactly one factory
m.addCons(x_11 + x_21 == 1, "assign_location_1")
m.addCons(x_12 + x_22 == 1, "assign_location_2")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

The candidate uses single-variable terms like d_11*c_11*x_11 which do not capture the interaction between the locations assigned to pairs of factories.

The candidate's objective never multiplies two assignment variables, so it cannot represent the joint location-dependent cost.

c_22 = 7

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables: x_ij = 1 if factory i is assigned to location j
x_11 = m.addVar("x_11", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
x_12 = m.addVar("x_12", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
x_21 = m.addVar("x_21", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)
x_22 = m.addVar("x_22", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)

# Objective: minimize total transportation cost
obj = (d_11 * c_11 * x_11 + d_11 * c_21 * x_12 +
       d_12 * c_12 * x_11 + d_12 * c_22 * x_12 +
       d_21 * c_11 * x_21 + d_21 * c_21 * x_22 +
       d_22 * c_12 * x_21 + d_22 * c_22 * x_22)
m.setObjective(obj, "minimize")

# Constraints: each factory assigned to exactly one location
m.addCons(x_11 + x_12 == 1, "assign_factory_1")
m.addCons(x_21 + x_22 == 1, "assign_factory_2")

# Constraints: each location assigned exactly one factory
m.addCons(x_11 + x_21 == 1, "assign_location_1")
m.addCons(x_12 + x_22 == 1, "assign_location_2")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
income = {1: 12500, 2: 35000, 3: 23000, 4: 100000}
cost = {1: 1.5, 2: 2.1, 3: 2.3, 4: 4.2}
budget = 7.0

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables: binary
x = {}
for i in [1, 2, 3, 4]:
    x[i] = m.addVar(name=f"x{i}", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)

# Objective: maximize annual income
m.setObjective(quicksum(income[i] * x[i] for i in [1, 2, 3, 4]), "maximize")

# Budget constraint
m.addCons(quicksum(cost[i] * x[i] for i in [1, 2, 3, 4]) <= budget, name="budget")

# If Property 4 is purchased, Property 3 cannot be purchased: x4 + x3 <= 1
m.addCons(x[4] + x[3] <= 1, name="exclusion_4_not_3")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")
    for i in [1, 2, 3, 4]:
        print(f"x{i} = {m.getVal(x[i])}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
cost = {"Alice": 1000, "Bob": 900, "Charlie": 600, "Diana": 500, "Ella": 700}
children = ["Alice", "Bob", "Charlie", "Diana", "Ella"]
max_children = 3
min_children = 2

# Model
m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Variables
x = {}
for c in children:
    x[c] = m.addVar(name=f"x_{c}", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)

# Objective: minimize total cost
m.setObjective(quicksum(cost[c] * x[c] for c in children), "minimize")

# Constraint: max 3 children
m.addCons(quicksum(x[c] for c in children) <= max_children, name="max_children")

# Constraint: Bob is definitely taken
m.addCons(x["Bob"] == 1, name="bob_fixed")

# Constraint: Alice and Diana conflict
m.addCons(x["Alice"] + x["Diana"] <= 1, name="alice_diana_conflict")

# Constraint: Bob and Charlie conflict
m.addCons(x["Bob"] + x["Charlie"] <= 1, name="bob_charlie_conflict")

# Constraint: Charlie implies Diana
m.addCons(x["Charlie"] <= x["Diana"], name="charlie_implies_diana")

# Constraint: Diana implies Ella
m.addCons(x["Diana"] <= x["Ella"], name="diana_implies_ella")

# Constraint: at least 2 children
m.addCons(quicksum(x[c] for c in children) >= min_children, name="min_children")

# Solve
m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
cost = {"Alice": 1000, "Bob": 900, "Charlie": 600, "Diana": 500, "Ella": 700}
children = ["Alice", "Bob", "Charlie", "Diana", "Ella"]
max_children = 3
min_children = 2

# Model
m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Variables
x = {}
for c in children:
    x[c] = m.addVar(name=f"x_{c}", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1)

# Objective: minimize total cost
m.setObjective(quicksum(cost[c] * x[c] for c in children), "minimize")

# Constraint: max 3 children
m.addCons(quicksum(x[c] for c in children) <= max_children, name="max_children")

# Constraint: Bob is definitely taken
m.addCons(x["Bob"] == 1, name="bob_fixed")

# Constraint: Alice and Diana conflict
m.addCons(x["Alice"] + x["Diana"] <= 1, name="alice_diana_conflict")

# Constraint: Bob and Charlie conflict
m.addCons(x["Bob"] + x["Charlie"] <= 1, name="bob_charlie_conflict")

# Constraint: Charlie implies Diana
m.addCons(x["Charlie"] <= x["Diana"], name="charlie_implies_diana")

# Constraint: Diana implies Ella
m.addCons(x["Diana"] <= x["Ella"], name="diana_implies_ella")

# Constraint: at least 2 children
m.addCons(quicksum(x[c] for c in children) >= min_children, name="min_children")

# Solve
m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
dur = {'A': 4, 'B': 3, 'C': 5, 'D': 2, 'E': 10, 'F': 10, 'G': 1}
cost_work_per_day = 1000
cost_machine_per_day = 5000

# Precedence: (predecessor, successor)
precedence = [
    ('A', 'G'), ('A', 'D'),
    ('E', 'F'), ('G', 'F'),
    ('D', 'C'), ('F', 'C'),
    ('F', 'B'),
]

activities = ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E', 'F', 'G']

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables: start times (continuous, >= 0)
t = {}
for a in activities:
    t[a] = m.addVar(name=f"t_{a}", lb=0.0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C")

# Project completion time
T = m.addVar(name="T", lb=0.0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C")

# Precedence constraints
for (pred, succ) in precedence:
    m.addCons(t[succ] >= t[pred] + dur[pred], name=f"{pred}_precedes_{succ}")

# Completion constraints: T >= start of each activity + its duration
for a in activities:
    m.addCons(T >= t[a] + dur[a], name=f"T_after_{a}")

# Objective: minimize 1000*T + 5000*(t_B + 3 - t_A)
# Machine rented from start of A to end of B (t_B + dur_B)
obj = cost_work_per_day * T + cost_machine_per_day * (t['B'] + dur['B'] - t['A'])
m.setObjective(obj, "minimize")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")
    for a in activities:
        print(f"  t_{a} = {m.getVal(t[a])}")
    print(f"  T = {m.getVal(T)}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
dur = {'A': 4, 'B': 3, 'C': 5, 'D': 2, 'E': 10, 'F': 10, 'G': 1}
cost_work_per_day = 1000
cost_machine_per_day = 5000

# Precedence: (predecessor, successor)
precedence = [
    ('A', 'G'), ('A', 'D'),
    ('E', 'F'), ('G', 'F'),
    ('D', 'C'), ('F', 'C'),
    ('F', 'B'),
]

activities = ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E', 'F', 'G']

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables: start times (continuous, >= 0)
t = {}
for a in activities:
    t[a] = m.addVar(name=f"t_{a}", lb=0.0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C")

# Project completion time
T = m.addVar(name="T", lb=0.0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C")

# Precedence constraints
for (pred, succ) in precedence:
    m.addCons(t[succ] >= t[pred] + dur[pred], name=f"{pred}_precedes_{succ}")

# Completion constraints: T >= start of each activity + its duration
for a in activities:
    m.addCons(T >= t[a] + dur[a], name=f"T_after_{a}")

# Objective: minimize 1000*T + 5000*(t_B + 3 - t_A)
# Machine rented from start of A to end of B (t_B + dur_B)
obj = cost_work_per_day * T + cost_machine_per_day * (t['B'] + dur['B'] - t['A'])
m.setObjective(obj, "minimize")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")
    for a in activities:
        print(f"  t_{a} = {m.getVal(t[a])}")
    print(f"  T = {m.getVal(T)}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
dur = {'A': 4, 'B': 3, 'C': 5, 'D': 2, 'E': 10, 'F': 10, 'G': 1}
cost_work_per_day = 1000
cost_machine_per_day = 5000

# Precedence: (predecessor, successor)
precedence = [
    ('A', 'G'), ('A', 'D'),
    ('E', 'F'), ('G', 'F'),
    ('D', 'C'), ('F', 'C'),
    ('F', 'B'),
]

activities = ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E', 'F', 'G']

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables: start times (continuous, >= 0)
t = {}
for a in activities:
    t[a] = m.addVar(name=f"t_{a}", lb=0.0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C")

# Project completion time
T = m.addVar(name="T", lb=0.0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C")

# Precedence constraints
for (pred, succ) in precedence:
    m.addCons(t[succ] >= t[pred] + dur[pred], name=f"{pred}_precedes_{succ}")

# Completion constraints: T >= start of each activity + its duration
for a in activities:
    m.addCons(T >= t[a] + dur[a], name=f"T_after_{a}")

# Objective: minimize 1000*T + 5000*(t_B + 3 - t_A)
# Machine rented from start of A to end of B (t_B + dur_B)
obj = cost_work_per_day * T + cost_machine_per_day * (t['B'] + dur['B'] - t['A'])
m.setObjective(obj, "minimize")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")
    for a in activities:
        print(f"  t_{a} = {m.getVal(t[a])}")
    print(f"  T = {m.getVal(T)}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data literals
a_p1 = 2
a_p2 = 3
b_p1 = 3
b_p2 = 4
avail_p1 = 16
avail_p2 = 24
c_per_b = 2
c_max_sell = 5
c_dispose_cost = 2
profit_a = 4
profit_b = 10
profit_c = 3

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
x_A = m.addVar("x_A", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C")
x_B = m.addVar("x_B", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C")
y = m.addVar("y", lb=0, ub=c_max_sell, vtype="C")
z = m.addVar("z", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C")

# Objective: maximize total profit
m.setObjective(profit_a * x_A + profit_b * x_B + profit_c * y - c_dispose_cost * z, "maximize")

# Constraint: process 1 time
m.addCons(a_p1 * x_A + b_p1 * x_B <= avail_p1, name="process_1_time")

# Constraint: process 2 time
m.addCons(a_p2 * x_A + b_p2 * x_B <= avail_p2, name="process_2_time")

# Constraint: by-product balance
m.addCons(y + z == c_per_b * x_B, name="byproduct_balance")

# Constraint: by-product sales limit (already enforced by ub on y, but add explicitly)
m.addCons(y <= c_max_sell, name="byproduct_sales_limit")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data literals
a_p1 = 2
a_p2 = 3
b_p1 = 3
b_p2 = 4
avail_p1 = 16
avail_p2 = 24
c_per_b = 2
c_max_sell = 5
c_dispose_cost = 2
profit_a = 4
profit_b = 10
profit_c = 3

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables
x_A = m.addVar("x_A", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C")
x_B = m.addVar("x_B", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C")
y = m.addVar("y", lb=0, ub=c_max_sell, vtype="C")
z = m.addVar("z", lb=0, ub=m.infinity(), vtype="C")

# Objective: maximize total profit
m.setObjective(profit_a * x_A + profit_b * x_B + profit_c * y - c_dispose_cost * z, "maximize")

# Constraint: process 1 time
m.addCons(a_p1 * x_A + b_p1 * x_B <= avail_p1, name="process_1_time")

# Constraint: process 2 time
m.addCons(a_p2 * x_A + b_p2 * x_B <= avail_p2, name="process_2_time")

# Constraint: by-product balance
m.addCons(y + z == c_per_b * x_B, name="byproduct_balance")

# Constraint: by-product sales limit (already enforced by ub on y, but add explicitly)
m.addCons(y <= c_max_sell, name="byproduct_sales_limit")

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum
import json

# Data
a = 70
b = 100
storage_capacity = 20  # 10,000 m³

purchase_price = [410, 430, 460, 450]  # Winter, Spring, Summer, Autumn
sale_price = [425, 440, 465, 455]
max_sales = [100, 140, 200, 160]

# Objective coefficients (profit per unit for x_ij)
# x_ij: purchase in quarter i, sell in quarter j (i <= j), storage time u = j - i
# profit = sale_price[j] - purchase_price[i] - (a + b*u)
obj_coef = {}
for i in range(4):
    for j in range(i, 4):
        u = j - i
        obj_coef[(i, j)] = sale_price[j] - purchase_price[i] - (a + b * u)

# Verify coefficients match formulation
# x11=-55, x12=-140, x13=-215, x14=-325
# x22=-60, x23=-135, x24=-245
# x33=-65, x34=-175
# x44=-65

m = Model()
m.hideOutput()
m.setRealParam("limits/time", 570)

# Decision variables: x[i][j] for i <= j
x = {}
for i in range(4):
    for j in range(i, 4):
        x[(i, j)] = m.addVar(vtype="C", lb=0, name=f"x{i+1}{j+1}")

# Objective: maximize profit
obj_terms = [obj_coef[(i, j)] * x[(i, j)] for i in range(4) for j in range(i, 4)]
m.setObjective(quicksum(obj_terms), "maximize")

# Sales constraints: total sold in each quarter <= max sales
m.addCons(x[(0, 0)] <= max_sales[0], name="sales_winter")
m.addCons(x[(0, 1)] + x[(1, 1)] <= max_sales[1], name="sales_spring")
m.addCons(x[(0, 2)] + x[(1, 2)] + x[(2, 2)] <= max_sales[2], name="sales_summer")
m.addCons(x[(0, 3)] + x[(1, 3)] + x[(2, 3)] + x[(3, 3)] <= max_sales[3], name="sales_autumn")

# Storage capacity constraints (inventory at end of each quarter <= 20)
# End of Winter: timber purchased in Winter and not yet sold
m.addCons(x[(0, 1)] + x[(0, 2)] + x[(0, 3)] <= storage_capacity, name="storage_end_winter")
# End of Spring: remaining from Winter + new from Spring not yet sold
m.addCons(x[(0, 1)] + x[(0, 2)] + x[(0, 3)] + x[(1, 2)] + x[(1, 3)] <= storage_capacity, name="storage_end_spring")
# End of Summer: remaining from Winter + Spring + new from Summer not yet sold
m.addCons(x[(0, 1)] + x[(0, 2)] + x[(0, 3)] + x[(1, 2)] + x[(1, 3)] + x[(2, 3)] <= storage_capacity, name="storage_end_summer")

# Clear by autumn: all inventory must be sold by end of autumn
# Total sold in autumn >= inventory at end of summer
m.addCons(
    x[(0, 3)] + x[(1, 3)] + x[(2, 3)] + x[(3, 3)] >=
    x[(0, 1)] + x[(0, 2)] + x[(0, 3)] + x[(1, 2)] + x[(1, 3)] + x[(2, 3)],
    name="clear_by_autumn"
)

m.optimize()

st = m.getStatus()
print(f"status: {st}")
if m.getNSols() > 0:
    print(f"objective: {m.getObjVal()}")
